docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
Defines how Bifröst reaches alternatives of itself.

For example if itself runs currently runs on AMD64 architecture, but needs for a target system an ARM64 instance. Or if the host is Windows, but the target is Linux.

Especially if a containerized environment (like Docker environment) is used, some features requires a supporting process that runs directly inside the container to enable all features. Such as tcp portforward from the context of the container or SSH Agent forward.

docs.title: downloadUrl
docs.text:
URL Alternative Binary = 

"https://github.com/engity-com/bifroest/releases/download/v{{.version}}/bifroest-{{.os}}-{{.arch}}-{{.edition}}{{.packageExt}}"

URL where to download the alternative version of Bifröst. Usually we simply will get this from the GitHub Releases of Bifröst.

docs.title: location
docs.text:
File Path Alternative Binary = "<os specific>"

Location to store the downloaded alternative version of Bifröst at.

A file that already exists, will not be downloaded again.

The default value is different, depending on the platform Bifröst runs on:

  • Linux: /var/lib/engity/bifroest/binaries/{{.version}}/{{.os}}-{{.arch}}-{{.edition}}{{.ext}}
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/binaries/{{.version}}/{{.os}}-{{.arch}}-{{.edition}}{{.ext}}
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\binaries\{{.version}}\{{.os}}-{{.arch}}-{{.edition}}{{.ext}}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Bifröst will be configured in the YAML language.

By default, the configuration is taken from the following location:

  • Linux: /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/configuration.yaml
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\configuration.yaml

This location can be changed by the --configuration=<path> flag when executing: 

bifroest run --configuration=/my/config.yaml

docs.title: ssh
docs.text:
SSH

Defines how the SSH connections itself will behave.

docs.title: http
docs.text:
HTTP

Configures optional HTTPS browser access. Disabled by default. A startup failure in any enabled SSH or HTTPS endpoint prevents the service from starting.

docs.title: session
docs.text:
Session

Defines where and how the sessions inside Bifröst are handled.

docs.title: flows
docs.text:
[]Flow

Defines which flows are evaluated for user sessions.

docs.title: environments
docs.text:
Map<Environment>

Reusable environments keyed by name. Each value is an inline object with type and that environment's settings, not a reference or a wrapper. The map key names the definition; do not add a definition-name field inside it. Provider settings such as a local account's name or a Kubernetes Pod's name retain their usual meaning; they do not rename the definition.

docs.title: authorizations
docs.text:
Map<Authorization>

Reusable authorizations keyed by name. Each value is an inline object with type and that authorization's settings, without a separate definition-name field. A flow selects exactly one authorization, either inline or by name, not a list or a chain of providers.

For both maps, a default entry is optional and never created automatically. Omitting a flow's corresponding setting, or setting it to null or '', uses that map's default if defined; otherwise the setting is required. Explicit references to unknown names are configuration errors.

docs.title: auditlogs
docs.text:
Map<Audit log>

Audit logs keyed by name, with their settings directly in each value. A defined, selected logger is active; there is no audit-log enabled setting. A flow with an omitted, null or empty auditlog uses auditlogs.default if defined, otherwise it has no audit logging or recording. No default logger is created implicitly. Unknown explicit references are configuration errors.

docs.title: monitoring
docs.text:
Monitoring

Configures a separate, optional listener for Prometheus metrics and startup, readiness and liveness probes. Disabled by default.

docs.title: housekeeping
docs.text:
Housekeeping

Defines how Bifröst will clean up its sessions and connections.

docs.title: alternatives
docs.text:
Alternatives

Defines how the imp (if needed) behaves to help to bridge context boundaries, for example to enable port-forwarding into an OCI container.

docs.title: startMessage
docs.text:
string Core = ""

If defined this message will be displayed in the log files of Bifröst on startup.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Simple: 

    ssh:
  addresses: [ ":22" ]
  # ...
http:
  # ...
session:
  type: fs
  # ...
flows:
  - name: local
  # ...
environments:
  # ...
authorizations:
  # ...
auditlogs:
  # ...
monitoring:
  # ...
housekeeping:
  # ...
alternatives:
  # ...
startMessage: ""

  2. Local-account host configuration 
    ## Host service for an existing local account on Linux, Windows or macOS.
## Local authentication uses the platform default.
flows:
  - name: local
    authorization:
      type: local
      rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
    environment:
      type: local
      name: "{{.authorization.user.name}}"
      ## If you only want to allow user with group "ssh" to log in, uncomment the following lines:
      ## Unix only: Windows users have no primary group.
      #loginAllowed: |
      #  {{ or
      #    (.authorization.user.group.name | eq "ssh" )
      #    (.authorization.user.groups     | firstMatching `{{.name | eq "ssh" }}` )
      #  }}
  3. Reusable Docker configuration with OpenID Connect authorization

    This example is using the Docker environment with OpenID Connect authorization. 

    environments:
  docker:
    type: docker
    image: alpine
authorizations:
  default:
    type: oidcDeviceAuth
    rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
    issuer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/my-great-tenant-uuid/v2.0
    clientId: my-great-client-uuid
    clientSecret: very-secret-secret
    scopes:
      - openid
      - email
      - profile
      - offline_access
flows:
  - name: docker
    environment: docker
    # authorization is omitted: uses authorizations.default
    discoverAsSlug: docker
    requirement:
      http:
        includedSlug: '^docker$'
    Configure the HTTP endpoint separately to publish /docker. Without an auditlogs.default entry or an explicit flow selection, this example does not log audit events or record sessions.

    To also accept /bla-bla as an alias, use includedSlug: '^(docker|bla-bla)$' while keeping discoverAsSlug: docker. A tab opened through /bla-bla keeps that URL scope when selected; it is not rewritten to /docker.

docs.title: Arch (Architecture)
docs.text: Represents an architecture. Here are all values supported where also a distribution of Bifröst is available for. See distributions for available values.

docs.title: Data types
docs.text: A collection of simple data-types used within Bifröst. More complex ones are defined on their dedicated pages.

docs.title: Authorized Keys
docs.text:
These are usually files in the home directory of each user, located at ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. These files are in the format: 

[<options> ]<key-type> <encoded-public-key>[ <comment>]
...

They contain SSH Public Keys.

Bifröst supports the following OpenSSH authorized_keys options:

Option Effect command="..." Replaces shell, command, and subsystem requests with the configured command. The original command is available as SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND. environment="NAME=value" Adds or replaces an environment variable for the session. May be specified more than once for different names. expiry-time="..." Rejects the key after the configured OpenSSH-compatible timestamp. from="..." Restricts the key to numeric IP addresses, CIDR networks, numeric wildcards, and negated numeric patterns. Hostname patterns are not supported. restrict Disables PTY, port forwarding, and agent forwarding unless individually enabled again. pty, no-pty Enables or disables PTY allocation. port-forwarding, no-port-forwarding Enables or disables local, dynamic, and reverse port forwarding. permitopen="host:port" Restricts local and dynamic port-forwarding destinations. May be specified more than once. permitlisten="[host:]port" Restricts reverse port-forwarding listeners. May be specified more than once. agent-forwarding, no-agent-forwarding Enables or disables access to a forwarded SSH agent. cert-authority Treats the entry as a user certificate authority instead of a directly authorized key. Supported by the simple and local authorizations. principals="name,..." Further restricts a cert-authority entry to certificates containing at least one listed principal. The resolved authorization remoteName (by default the requested SSH username) must still be a certificate principal.

Options not listed above are not supported. A key entry using an unsupported option, such as tunnel, user-rc, x11-forwarding, no-touch-required, or verify-required, is rejected instead of being treated as unrestricted. principals without cert-authority is also rejected.

Warning

Environment variables can change how commands and shells behave. Only configure environment= values that you trust, especially variables such as PATH, shell startup variables, or dynamic-loader settings.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIC80lm5FQbbyRUut6RwZJRbxTLO3W4f08ITDi9fA3+jx me@foo.tld
ssh-rsa  me-legacy@foo.tld

docs.title: Docker Pull Credentials
docs.text:
To pull from an OCI/Docker image registry there can be credentials required. In these cases usually they have to be provided in this format.

Bifröst accept them in the following formats:

  1. Base64 URL encoded JSON of format {"username":"<username>","password":"<password>"} or {"auth":"<base64 encoded auth token>"}
  2. JSON of format {"username":"<username>","password":"<password>"} or {"auth":"<base64 encoded auth token>"} ... which will be:
    1. base64 URL encoded by Bifröst. -> result will be as 1.
  3. A bare auth token ... which will be:
    1. base64 URL encoded,
    2. put into {"auth":"<encoded bare auth token>"} JSON and
    3. finally base64 URL encoded by Bifröst. -> result will be as 1.

docs.title: DSA Restriction
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • none
  • all
  • at-least-1024-bits
  • at-least-2048-bits
  • at-least-3072-bits

docs.title: Duration
docs.text: A duration of time of Go flavor. Examples: 300ms, 6s, 5m, 12h or combined 12h5m6s300ms.

docs.title: ED25519 Restriction
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • none
  • all
  • at-least-256-bits

docs.title: ECDSA Restriction
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • none
  • all
  • at-least-256-bits
  • at-least-384-bits
  • at-least-521-bits

docs.title: Enforceable
docs.text:
Enforceable<T> adds an optional server-enforced value to type T. Without a prefix, the user may change the value. Prefix it with ! to prevent changes. For example, an Enforceable<Duration> accepts 10s or "!10s". Only properties declared with this wrapper support enforcement.

The marker is read after template evaluation, so templates can decide whether to enforce the value. The remaining value follows the inner type's rules. Quote YAML values starting with ! so they are not interpreted as tags.

docs.title: Environment Variable Name
docs.text: The name of an environment variable. It has to fulfill the portable ASCII pattern [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: A map from Environment Variable Name keys to string values. Values can use the template context documented by the property accepting this data type and cannot contain NUL characters.

docs.title: Flow Name
docs.text: Identifies flows. It has to fulfill the regular expression [a-z][a-z0-9]+.

docs.title: File Mode
docs.text: The permissions to access a file in octal notation. See Oracles documentation for more details.

docs.title: File Path
docs.text: A location of a file on the local file system. Like /foo/bar

docs.title: GID
docs.text: The identifier of a local group: a uint32 on Linux, or a textual local SAM group SID on Windows (not an Active Directory object GUID).

docs.title: Host
docs.text: Represents a host(-name), which can be either an IPv4, IPv6 or DNS name.

docs.title: IP Address or Network
docs.text:
A numeric IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a network in CIDR notation. DNS names, ports, wildcards and IPv6 zone identifiers are not supported.

Examples: 127.0.0.1, ::1, 192.0.2.0/24, 2001:db8::/32. IPv6 addresses are written without brackets.

docs.title: Kubeconfig
docs.text: Configuration file in YAML format that defines how to access a Kubernetes cluster. See official Kubernetes documentation for more details.

docs.title: Log Color Mode
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • auto
  • always
  • never

docs.title: Log Format
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • text
  • json

docs.title: Log Level
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • TRACE
  • DEBUG
  • INFO
  • WARN
  • ERROR
  • FATAL

docs.title: Net Address
docs.text: Socket address in format [<Host>]:<port>.

docs.title: Os (Operating System)
docs.text: Represents an operating system. Here are all values supported where also a distribution of Bifröst is available for. See distributions for available values.

docs.title: Password
docs.text: Represents an encoded or plain password that can be evaluated if it does match a requested one.

docs.title: Password Type
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • plain
  • bcrypt

docs.title: Public Keys
docs.text:
A string containing one or more OpenSSH public-key lines. Empty lines and lines beginning with # are ignored. Unlike Authorized Keys, these lines cannot contain options. Certificate-authority configuration also rejects certificate lines because each trust anchor must be a plain public key.

ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAI... organization-user-ca
ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAACAQ... legacy-user-ca

docs.title: Pull Policy
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • ifAbsend: The resource (e.g. an image) is pulled only if it is not already present locally.
  • always: Everytime a context is crated (for example a new environment) the latest version of the resource will be pulled from the remote registry (for example an image). It does not matter if the resource does already exist or not. No matter if the resource (like images) is based on digest or of the digest is the same, the digest is the same, the corresponding sub-resources will not be pulled.
  • never: The resource (like an image) has to be present. Otherwise, the process will fail.

docs.title: Regex
docs.text: Regular expression of Go flavor. You can play around with it at regex.com.

docs.title: RememberMe
docs.text:
Controls whether a client may be remembered for future logins without repeating password/MFA authentication.

Value User choice forbidden Unavailable, including previously saved access. allowed Off by default; users opt in. allowedAndEnabledByDefault On by default; users may opt out. enforced On without opt-out, when technically supported.

Aliases: false, off, no, 0, and empty mean forbidden; true, on, yes, and 1 mean allowed.

In the browser, use Remember this browser. For SSH, send REMEMBER_ME=true or REMEMBER_ME=false, for example ssh -o SetEnv=REMEMBER_ME=true user@host. This controls future access, not the current authentication. enforced ignores opt-out. Logout, revocation, session expiry and current access restrictions still apply.

docs.title: RSA Restriction
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • none
  • all
  • at-least-1024-bits
  • at-least-2048-bits
  • at-least-3072-bits
  • at-least-4096-bits

docs.title: SSH Ciphers
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • aes128-cbc
  • 3des-cbc
  • arcfour
  • arcfour128
  • arcfour256
  • chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com
  • aes128-ctr
  • aes192-ctr
  • aes256-ctr
  • aes128-gcm@openssh.com
  • aes256-gcm@openssh.com

docs.title: SSH Key Exchange
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • diffie-hellman-group1-sha1
  • diffie-hellman-group14-sha1
  • diffie-hellman-group14-sha256
  • diffie-hellman-group16-sha512
  • ecdh-sha2-nistp256
  • ecdh-sha2-nistp384
  • ecdh-sha2-nistp521
  • curve25519-sha256@libssh.org
  • curve25519-sha256
  • diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1
  • diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256
  • mlkem768x25519-sha256

docs.title: SSH Message Authentication
docs.text:
Can be one of:

  • hmac-sha1
  • hmac-sha1-96
  • hmac-sha2-256
  • hmac-sha2-512
  • hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com
  • hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com

docs.title: SSH Public Key
docs.text:
The public variant of an SSH keypair of a user.

Please refer to the good documentation at GitHub how to create SSH (public) keys.

docs.title: UID
docs.text: The identifier of a local user: a uint32 on Linux, or a textual local SAM user [SID](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Identifier on Windows (not an Active Directory object GUID).

docs.title: URL
docs.text: Represents a classical URL to reference resources (for example) in the internet, like https://bifroest.engity.org.

docs.title: Flows
docs.text:
A flow combines an authorization with an environment. Different flows can serve different users, hosts or browser access links.

Flows are tried in configuration order:

  1. Is the incoming transport enabled for this flow?
  2. Does the request meet its requirements?
  3. Does authorization succeed?
  4. Can the request use the configured environment and a compatible session?

A denied authorization can try the next flow; an authorization error stops the attempt. A published HTTP link selects exactly one flow and never falls through to another flow if access is denied.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
Flow Name

Unique flow name, used in logs and stored sessions.

Warning

Changing a flow's name breaks its existing sessions.

docs.title: title
docs.text:
Plain text = ""

Optional display title, defaulting to name. At most 255 UTF-8 bytes without control or formatting characters. A shell's terminal title can override it in that shell's tab.

docs.title: auditlog
docs.text:
Audit log Name

Name of an entry in the root auditlogs map. Omitted, null and '' select auditlogs.default only if it is defined; otherwise this flow has no audit logging or recording. An explicit unknown name is a configuration error. Selecting a defined logger activates it; no enabled flag is needed.

docs.title: ssh
docs.text:
SSH transport

Controls incoming SSH access, independently of HTTP.

docs.title: http
docs.text:
HTTP transport

Controls browser access, the requesting-name prompt and terminal keepalive.

Note

Enabling the root HTTP endpoint makes every flow HTTP-eligible by default. Set http.enabled: false on flows that should remain SSH-only.

docs.title: discoverAsSlug
docs.text:
string = ""

Publishes an HTTP access link for this flow on its allowed hosts. An empty value publishes nothing. Only HTTP-enabled flows publish links.

A slug has one or two case-sensitive segments of ASCII letters, digits or hyphens, each 1–64 bytes long; examples are servers/Example and bla-bla. Leading or trailing slashes, empty segments and URL-encoded values are not allowed.

The link still requires authorization and all configured requirements. Two flows cannot publish the same slug on the same configured domain. Disjoint domains may use the same slug.

The published slug must match this flow's requirement.http.includedSlug and must not match excludedSlug. A contradiction is a configuration error at startup; publishing a link does not widen the allowed slug scope.

docs.title: requirement
docs.text:
Requirement

Rules a request must satisfy before authorization.

docs.title: authorization
docs.text:
Authorization or name

An inline authorization or the name of an entry in the root authorizations map. If omitted, authorizations.default must be defined.

Inline authorization and environment:

flows:
  - name: local
    authorization:
      type: local
    environment:
      type: local
      name: "{{.authorization.user.name}}"

Referenced authorization and environment:

authorizations:
  local-users:
    type: local
environments:
  host:
    type: local
    name: "{{.authorization.user.name}}"
flows:
  - name: local
    authorization: local-users
    environment: host

docs.title: environment
docs.text:
Environment or name

An inline environment or the name of an entry in the root environments map, as shown above. If omitted, environments.default must be defined.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = true

Accepts incoming SSH authentication for this flow. false does not disable HTTP or SSH used to connect to a downstream target.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = true

Allows HTTP authentication and discovery for this flow. The root HTTP endpoint must also be enabled. false leaves SSH unchanged.

docs.title: requestUser
docs.text:
bool = true

With true, the browser and API require a nonblank requesting name. With false, the browser sends an empty name. This is useful for OIDC flows that identify users through the IdP. Named and nameless flows remain separate; methods needing a name cannot guess one instead.

Name requirements still apply: ^sso$ does not match an empty name; ^$ does. The requesting name is not the verified principal or the target account.

docs.title: keepAlive
docs.text:
Enforceable<Duration> Authorization = "15s"

Browser terminal and management-channel keepalive interval, from 1s to 5m. Users can change it in Connection settings, unless the value is enforced.

The template is evaluated after authentication using the current session context. An enforced value overrides saved browser preferences. Keepalive preserves only the network connection; it does not extend session or RememberMe timeouts.

Editable interval
http:
  keepAlive: 10s
Enforced interval based on the authenticated user
http:
  keepAlive: '{{ if eq .authentication.principal "alice" }}10s{{ else }}!20s{{ end }}'

docs.title: Requirement
docs.text: Requirements are checked before authorization. General name rules apply to SSH and HTTP. Transport-specific rules apply in addition: all applicable rules must match.

docs.title: includedRequestingName
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Include rule for the requesting name, such as alice in ssh alice@host. Empty means unrestricted.

docs.title: excludedRequestingName
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Exclude rule for the requesting name. Empty excludes nothing.

docs.title: ssh
docs.text:
SSH requirements

Additional rules for incoming SSH connections.

docs.title: http
docs.text:
HTTP requirements

Additional rules for browser access.

Note

Regular expressions match substrings unless anchored. Use ^alice$ to match the complete name, rather than also matching alice-admin.

docs.title: SSH requirements
docs.text: These properties belong to requirement.ssh.

docs.title: includedRequestingName
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Additional include rule for the SSH requesting name. Empty means unrestricted.

docs.title: excludedRequestingName
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Additional exclude rule for the SSH requesting name. Empty excludes nothing.

docs.title: HTTP requirements
docs.text: These properties belong to requirement.http.

docs.title: includedRequestingName
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Additional include rule for the HTTP requesting name, which may be empty.

docs.title: excludedRequestingName
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Additional exclude rule for the HTTP requesting name.

docs.title: includedHost
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Include rule for the canonical host: lowercase, without port or trailing DNS dot. For example, APP.EXAMPLE.:443 becomes app.example. IPv6 literals keep their brackets.

docs.title: excludedHost
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Exclude rule for the canonical host.

docs.title: includedSlug
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Include rule for the slug without a leading slash. The root / has slug "".

docs.title: excludedSlug
docs.text:
Regex = ""

Exclude rule for the slug.

When both slug rules are empty or omitted, only the root / matches. Otherwise normal regex rules apply: an empty include with a nonempty exclude allows every slug except those excluded. Use ^docker$ to allow only /docker.

For name and host rules, empty includes do not restrict access and empty excludes exclude nothing. Host rules only narrow the endpoint's domain list. Discovery links do not bypass these requirements. Host and user checks remain authoritative during authentication; anonymous discovery does not inspect user accounts, keys or sessions, or contact an identity provider.

docs.title: Different SSH login names
docs.text:
flows:
  - name: sso
    requirement:
      includedRequestingName: ^sso$
    authorization:
      type: oidcDeviceAuth
      # ...
    environment:
      type: local
      # ...

  - name: local
    authorization:
      type: local
      # ...
    environment:
      type: local
      # ...

docs.title: A browser-only OIDC link
docs.text:
This flow publishes https://app.example.org/servers/Example without asking for a login name. Configure the HTTPS endpoint separately. The IdP must support device authorization and, by default, refresh tokens. Its verified principal must map to an allowed local account; configure the principal mapping accordingly.

flows:
  - name: browser
    ssh:
      enabled: false
    http:
      requestUser: false
    discoverAsSlug: servers/Example
    requirement:
      includedRequestingName: '^$'
      http:
        includedHost: '^app\.example\.org$'
        includedSlug: '^servers/Example$'
    authorization:
      type: oidcDeviceAuth
      rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
      issuer: https://identity.example.org
      clientId: bifroest
      clientSecret: example-only
    environment:
      type: local
      name: '{{ .authentication.principal }}'

docs.title: Housekeeping
docs.text: Bifröst periodically removes expired sessions and resources that are no longer needed. Cleanup remains conservative when persisted state cannot be restored safely.

docs.title: Cleanup guarantees
docs.text:
Session storage is deleted only after the session, environment, and authorization were disposed successfully. Transient or unknown errors retain the session for a later retry. Permanently unusable local authorization tokens can be removed during an audited disposal.

Disposal is idempotent. An already disposed entry may be inspected again while retained, and pending resource cleanup is still attempted, but an unchanged disposal is not reported as a new successful change. Disposal does not itself delete the retained session entry or shorten keepExpiredFor.

For an OIDC flow, lost access can dispose a session before its retention period ends. Disposal removes the locally stored token after successful cleanup; Bifröst does not need to revalidate that token with the provider before deletion. A temporary provider outage cannot indefinitely retain an otherwise expired session. A session with a known ValidUntil remains stored until that time plus keepExpiredFor, even if already disposed. Storage failures still prevent deletion. Audit failures prevent it under failurePolicy: strict; bestEffort may instead disable the audit log and continue. OIDC disposal does not revoke tokens at the provider.

Sealed session Recordings become eligible only after their retention period and every selected target's durable acknowledgement and success-audit marker. Housekeeping verifies and marks the signed receipt before deleting the artifact, then removes the receipt state. An interruption resumes this order without recreating deleted content. See Recording remote delivery and retention and the housekeeping.recording.delete.* events.

docs.title: Removed flows
docs.text:
Sessions whose flow no longer exists are preserved because Bifröst can no longer interpret their environment and authorization tokens safely. Their resources are excluded from automatic orphan cleanup, and the skip is logged as housekeeping.orphaned-session.cleanup.skipped.

If a flow keeps its name but changes environment type, sessions with an old or unrecognized environment token are also left untouched. Bifröst logs a warning with the flow and session ID instead of disposing the session or letting the new environment discard a token that may still require account, process, or profile cleanup. Restore the original environment configuration to finish its cleanup, or inspect the session and its resources before removing anything manually. Such sessions remain stored until an operator resolves the mismatch, even after the retention period. Older sessions without an environment token have no persisted type information; Bifröst cannot detect a type change for them.

docs.title: Corrupt sessions
docs.text: Without automatic repair, corrupt entries are preserved and reported individually. Automatic repair is limited to configured flows; one corrupt entry does not block other sessions or environment cleanup. Even with automatic repair enabled, a corrupt session with a nonempty environment token is preserved for operator inspection rather than discarded with the token.

docs.title: every
docs.text:
Duration = "10m"

How often the housekeeping should run.

docs.title: initialDelay
docs.text:
Duration = 0

How long should be waited upon start of the application before the first run. If 0 it is also blocking, even before the first connection will be accepted.

docs.title: autoRepair
docs.text:
bool = true

If true the service will try to repair potentially corrupt or broken states by itself, as long as this is safely possible.

docs.title: keepExpiredFor
docs.text:
Duration = "336h"

For how long a disposed session will be kept. The session will no longer be usable, but it might be helpful for audit reasons.

Note

336h = 14 days

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
The optional root monitoring block provides a separate operational listener. It does not require HTTP browser access, a management flow or an interactive login. See Monitor a Bifröst instance for Prometheus and Kubernetes examples.

Metric collection is active when monitoring is enabled or at least one management flow is configured. metrics show queries the same measurements over management SSH, without opening a monitoring port or requiring a monitoring bearer token. Only monitoring.enabled starts the HTTP monitoring listener.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = false

Starts the monitoring listener. When disabled or omitted, no monitoring listener starts and no monitoring token or certificate files are read.

docs.title: addresses
docs.text:
[]Net Address = ["localhost:9090"]

Addresses to listen on. At least one is required when enabled. The default is loopback-only; Kubernetes HTTP probes need an explicitly configured address reachable through the Pod IP. Port 9090 is configurable and must not conflict with Prometheus or another local listener.

Warning

Metrics include configured flow, authorization, environment, audit-log and remote-target names, and HTTP certificate domains. Keep the listener on a private network, restrict its peers, and do not expose it through a public Ingress or LoadBalancer. A bearer token does not encrypt HTTP traffic; use TLS or another encrypted transport outside a trusted network.

docs.title: allowedRemoteHosts
docs.text:
[]IP Address or Network = []

Allowed peers. An omitted, null or empty value allows every peer that can reach the listener. With entries, a peer must match at least one. Empty entries are ignored.

The filter applies to all endpoints and uses the direct connection's peer address, not Forwarded or X-Forwarded-For. Include the actual node/probe and scraper source ranges in Kubernetes. A proxy is itself the peer.

docs.title: bearerToken
docs.text:
string = ""

Optional RFC 6750 bearer token protecting only /metrics. Cannot be combined with bearerTokenFile. /ready and /status remain token-free but are still subject to the peer filter.

docs.title: bearerTokenFile
docs.text:
File Path = ""

Reads the metrics bearer token from a local file at startup, suitable for a mounted Kubernetes Secret. The token may contain at most 4096 bytes, excluding a trailing line ending. Empty or invalid files prevent startup. Restart Bifröst after rotating the token.

docs.title: tls
docs.text:
TLS

Optional TLS using supplied certificate/key pairs. Without TLS, the listener serves HTTP.

docs.title: readHeaderTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "10s"

Request-header and request-read timeout. Must be positive.

docs.title: idleTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "1m"

Idle HTTP keep-alive timeout. Must be positive.

docs.title: gracefulShutdownTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "30s"

Maximum time for monitoring requests to finish on shutdown. 0s closes them immediately.

docs.title: maxHeaderBytes
docs.text:
uint32 = 1048576

Maximum request-header size, from 1 to 16777216 bytes.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text: These properties belong to monitoring.tls.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = false

Enables TLS. Requires at least one supplied certificate/key pair. No ACME, automatic issuance or generated fallback certificates are supported.

docs.title: certificates
docs.text:
[]Certificate

PEM certificate/key pairs, using the same file-property names as HTTP certificates. Certificates are read at startup; restart Bifröst after replacing them.

docs.title: Certificate
docs.text: Each entry in monitoring.tls.certificates has these properties.

docs.title: certificateFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local PEM certificate-chain file. Use a certificate trusted by your scraper and covering its connection name or IP.

docs.title: privateKeyFile
docs.text:
File Path

Matching protected PEM private-key file, owned by the Bifröst service account. Its key must be distinct from SSH, audit-signing, SFTP and audit-encryption keys. Certificate and key validation use the same requirements as HTTP TLS. For Kubernetes on Linux, mount the TLS key with owner-only permissions, such as defaultMode: 0400, and ownership that lets the service account read it.

Example
monitoring:
  enabled: true
  addresses: ["192.0.2.10:9090"]
  allowedRemoteHosts: ["192.0.2.20"]
  bearerTokenFile: /run/secrets/monitoring-token
  tls:
    enabled: true
    certificates:
      - certificateFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/monitoring.crt
        privateKeyFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/monitoring.key

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints accept GET and HEAD. They do not perform test logins or target/backend health checks.

Path Purpose Response /status Minimal process liveness. External dependency failures do not make it fail. 200: ok /ready New-access readiness; usable for startup and readiness probes. 200: ready503: not ready /metrics Operational metrics; requires the configured bearer token, if any. 200: Metrics in OpenMetrics Format

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Application metric names start with bifroest_. Counters and histogram observations start again with each process; gauges describe current or explicitly observed state. An event series appears after its first observation. Standard go_* and, where supported, process_* metrics are also provided.

Flow-related metrics use flow, authorization, auditlog and environment. The latter three are configured definition names, or empty for an unnamed inline/absent definition. Audit-log metrics use auditlog; delivery metrics additionally use configured target and kind (audit or recording). Shared components are counted once, not once per referring flow. No username, principal, session/Recording ID, target address, error text, claim or session content is a label.

Metric Type Meaning bifroest_ready Gauge 1 when ready for new access, otherwise 0. bifroest_connections_active Gauge Open SSH transport connections, including authentication attempts, direct SSH and SSH tunnels. Excludes monitoring and browser HTTP requests. bifroest_connections_unauthenticated Gauge Currently open SSH connections without successful authentication. HTTP asset/discovery connections are not unauthenticated SSH connections. bifroest_connections_rejected_total Counter Admissions rejected by connection, per-session, tunnel, WebSocket or SSH protection limits; bounded transport and reason. SSH reasons include startups, connections, channels, channels_per_connection, sessions_per_connection, reverse_forwards and reverse_forwards_per_connection. ssh_tunnel distinguishes SSH limits reached through a tunnel from direct ssh. Global SSH-library limits apply per serving listener; Bifröst's connection budget remains aggregated. bifroest_connections_closed_without_authentication_attempt_total Counter SSH connections closed without offering an authentication method other than none, with reason: peer_closed, timeout, protocol_error or closed. A public-key offer counts as an attempt, not necessarily a success. Not applied to ordinary HTTP traffic. bifroest_session_connections_active Gauge Registered live authenticated SSH and browser-terminal connections, per flow. bifroest_sessions_active Gauge Distinct Bifröst sessions referenced by those live connections, per flow. Not all retained sessions in storage. bifroest_tasks_active Gauge Running shell, command and subsystem tasks, per flow; not Bifröst sessions or idle SSH session channels. bifroest_authentication_flow_evaluations_total Counter Provider evaluations per flow, with transport, method, phase, result and error_category. An accepted public-key/candidate is only an eligibility probe. bifroest_authentication_flow_evaluation_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of those evaluations, excluding observer/audit work. Interactive authentication includes user waiting time. bifroest_authentication_completions_total Counter Explicit authentication completion/compatibility decisions, with transport, method, result and error_category. This is not a count of published browser credentials or established SSH handshakes. bifroest_authentication_attempts_total Counter Once per authentication attempt result, not per evaluated flow; transport, method and result (success, denied, error or abandoned). Public-key eligibility, polling and discovery are not successes or separate logins. Failed attempts without one resolved flow have empty flow labels. bifroest_access_denials_total Counter Post-login PTY, forwarding, subsystem/task and management-policy denials, with fixed operation and bounded reason. Not every HTTP 401/403 is a policy denial or failed login. bifroest_auditlog_enabled Gauge 1 for a configured logger not disabled after a best-effort failure. bifroest_auditlog_disabled Gauge 1 when a configured logger was disabled after a best-effort failure. No series is invented for an unconfigured logger. bifroest_recording_configured Gauge Whether recording is configured for the audit log, independently of later failures. bifroest_auditlog_errors_total Counter Failures reported to the logger's failure policy, with bounded error_category. bifroest_recording_errors_total Counter Recording failures; these can also increment the enclosing audit-log error counter. bifroest_recording_spool_bytes Gauge Accounted spool bytes, including outstanding storage reservations. Omitted when accounting is unavailable or uncertain. bifroest_recording_spool_limit_bytes Gauge Configured spool limit. bifroest_recording_spool_accounting_valid Gauge Whether spool usage is available and trustworthy. bifroest_auditlog_minimum_free_bytes Gauge Configured journal filesystem free-space reserve, not measured filesystem free space. bifroest_auditlog_available_bytes Gauge Last measured space available on the journal filesystem; not the recording spool. Use only with a valid, recent space observation. bifroest_auditlog_space_observation_valid Gauge Whether the latest journal-space observation succeeded. Overdue observations and a stopped observer report 0. Failed observation does not change the audit failure policy. bifroest_auditlog_space_observation_timestamp_seconds Gauge Unix timestamp of the last successful space observation, sampled approximately every 15 seconds. bifroest_auditlog_details_suppressed_total Counter Unauthenticated audit details aggregated or suppressed, with reason="rate_limit" or reason="journal_reserve". Counts details, not summary records. bifroest_remote_delivery_errors_total Counter Worker retry failures, including delivery and local-state failures. bifroest_remote_delivery_worker_pending Gauge 1 while a sequential worker has an observed outstanding delivery; otherwise 0. Not a complete backlog count. bifroest_remote_delivery_pending_observed_seconds Gauge Time since the worker first observed its current outstanding delivery. Not the oldest stored artifact's age; resets when that operation resolves. bifroest_cleanup_runs_total Counter Cleanup attempts with operation and result, including individually handled failures. bifroest_cleanup_last_run_success Gauge Whether the last observed operation succeeded, per cleanup label set. bifroest_cleanup_last_success_timestamp_seconds Gauge Unix timestamp of the last successful operation since process start. bifroest_cleanup_problems Gauge Unresolved session inspection/cleanup problems observed during the last housekeeping scan, per flow. An empty flow groups unknown/removed flows. bifroest_cleanup_last_scan_timestamp_seconds Gauge Time of the last housekeeping observation, including failed scans; use it to identify stale problem counts.

Flow evaluation results are accepted, denied or failed; completion results are success, denied or failure. These measurement points are separate and must not be added together as login counts. No-matching-flow attempts do not invent a flow evaluation or completion. Public-key phases are candidate and verified; other ordinary methods use an empty phase.

Transports identify SSH (ssh) versus browser authentication (http); SSH tunnels remain ssh. Error categories are system, config, network, user, permission, expired or unknown; successful observations use unknown. Cleanup operations are housekeeping, session_inspection, session_dispose, session_delete, orphan_cleanup and recording_retention. A successful overall housekeeping pass does not erase a failed individual operation's series. Problem counts are observations, not a full inventory if a scan failed. Unknown/removed flow names are not exported.

docs.title: Active ages
docs.text:
The following are gauges, not completed-lifetime histograms. For each prefix, _age_observations counts known live creation times and _age_sum_seconds is their combined age; _oldest_age_seconds, _youngest_age_seconds and _average_age_seconds describe their current ages. With no known live creation times, count and sum are zero and extrema/average are absent. Age is not idle time.

Prefix Scope bifroest_sessions Active sessions per flow. Age starts at the original session creation, including after reconnecting. bifroest_session_connections Registered live authenticated connections per flow. Reconnecting starts a new connection age. bifroest_connections Connection age with transport="ssh" or transport="http". HTTP includes physical TLS sockets and hijacked WebSockets; SSH includes logical SSH tunnels. Do not add these layers together.

For a weighted average across instances, divide the sum of _age_sum_seconds by the sum of _age_observations, rather than averaging per-instance averages. A retained session without a live registered connection is not active. Scraping does not scan session storage.

docs.title: Workload HTTP, TLS and channels
docs.text:
These metrics exclude the monitoring listener, its scrapes and its health probes. Requests, physical sockets and long-lived channels are separate: HTTP/2 multiplexes requests on one socket; an SSH tunnel also owns a logical SSH connection. HTTP metrics use only fixed route names/groups, known methods and bounded status codes. Unrecognized paths use route="unknown"; unrecognized methods use method="unknown". Raw paths, queries, Origins and peer addresses are never labels. Request flow is empty until a verified flow is actually known; physical HTTP sockets are never assigned a flow.

Metric Type Meaning bifroest_http_connections_opened_total Counter Accepted physical HTTP/TLS sockets. bifroest_http_connections_active Gauge Open sockets, including hijacked WebSockets until their actual transport closes. bifroest_http_connections_closed_total Counter Socket closures with bounded I/O/end reason. bifroest_http_tls_handshakes_total Counter result="success" or result="aborted", with a bounded reason for aborted handshakes. Includes failed or timed-out handshakes before any HTTP request. bifroest_http_requests_total Counter Requests reaching the HTTP handler, including authority, path and origin rejections, with route, method, status and known flow. Malformed HTTP rejected before handler dispatch is not a request observation. bifroest_http_requests_active Gauge Currently executing handlers, including streams, by route and method. bifroest_http_request_duration_seconds Histogram Ordinary handler duration. Successfully opened WebSockets, SSH streams and dedicated artifact transfers are excluded. bifroest_http_transfer_duration_seconds Histogram Dedicated HTTP artifact-transfer duration, separate from ordinary API latency and WebSocket channel lifetime. bifroest_http_request_body_bytes_total / bifroest_http_response_body_bytes_total Counter Read/written HTTP body bytes; excludes TLS/framing overhead and hijacked WebSocket frames. Uses the request labels. bifroest_http_rejections_total Counter Security/protection-budget rejections, with route and fixed reason, including authority, origin, CSRF, body, request/login, socket and message/wire budgets. bifroest_http_channels_opened_total / bifroest_http_channels_active Counter / Gauge Opened/current terminal or management WebSockets and SSH tunnels, with kind. Opening the transport does not prove successful in-channel authentication. bifroest_http_channel_open_failures_total Counter Requests to channel routes that did not open a channel, with kind and HTTP status. bifroest_http_channels_closed_total Counter Channel endings with kind and bounded reason; an established channel may still fail authentication or protocol validation. bifroest_http_channel_duration_seconds Histogram Open channel lifetimes, separate from ordinary API latency. bifroest_http_tls_certificate_expiration_timestamp_seconds Gauge Earliest Unix expiry time in the currently published certificate chain, per configured domain. bifroest_http_tls_renewal_errors_total Counter Failed renewal rounds of the existing HTTP certificate manager. Does not enable ACME on monitoring.

Rising rejection or handshake-abort rates can indicate scans, slow clients or overload, but also ordinary health checks and client/network failures. Use rates and sustained error ratios together with audit logs; these metrics are not an IDS and must not trigger liveness restarts merely because an external backend fails.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Add this block to an existing Bifröst configuration to enable loopback-only monitoring on port 9090:

monitoring:
  enabled: true

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
Defines audit logs in the root auditlogs map, separately from the regular application log. The map key is the logger's name; its value contains the settings below, without a name or enabled field. A flow selects a logger by name.

A defined, selected logger is active. An omitted, null or empty flow auditlog selects auditlogs.default if defined; otherwise no audit logging or recording runs for that flow. No default definition is created implicitly, and an explicit unknown reference is a configuration error. Session recording remains a separate opt-in on the selected logger through recording.enabled.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Audit logs may share a signing key and identity file, but must use non-overlapping journal directories. Recording repositories must also be separate. Identity files must be outside all journal and Recording directories. Names do not change default paths: configure different repository paths explicitly when defining multiple logs.

docs.title: failurePolicy
docs.text:
string = "strict"

Controls what happens when this audit log or its session-recording repository fails:

  • strict preserves fail-closed behavior. Initialization errors prevent startup, and runtime persistence errors abort the affected operation.
  • bestEffort logs the first failure, disables this audit log and its recording until restart, but lets the SSH operation continue. Fix the cause and restart Bifröst; persistence does not automatically recover.

Only strict and bestEffort are accepted. Remote-delivery outages continue to use their documented asynchronous retry behavior and do not by themselves disable the local audit log.

docs.title: identityFile
docs.text:
File Path = "<os specific>"

Signing key for the journal and optional Recording. Multiple audit logs can use the same identityFile or separate files containing the same key. They then have the same producer ID; trusting that ID trusts the shared signing identity, not one specific audit-log name.

Bifröst creates an Ed25519 key when the logger is initialized only if none of the repositories using that identity file contains prior state.

If history exists, a missing or invalid signing key prevents startup. Existing keys must be regular, at most 1 MiB, owned by the Bifröst user, and neither symlinked nor hard-linked:

  • Unix: mode 0400 or 0600.
  • Windows: a protected DACL limited to the owner, SYSTEM, and optionally OWNER RIGHTS.

The default value is different, depending on the platform Bifröst runs on:

  • Linux: /etc/engity/bifroest/auditlog-key
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/auditlog-key
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\auditlog-key

docs.title: directory
docs.text:
File Path = "<os specific>"

Local audit-log directory. It contains the journal, delivery cursors, and temporary work data. Bifröst manages it exclusively; do not modify or rotate its files externally.

The platform defaults are:

  • Linux: /var/lib/engity/bifroest/auditlog
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/auditlog
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\auditlog

docs.title: minimumFreeBytes
docs.text:
uint64 = 268435456

Filesystem space reserved for authenticated and other essential audit events. 0 uses the secure default of 256 MiB rather than disabling the reserve.

When the reserve is reached, Bifröst suppresses pre-authentication detail and counts it in bounded aggregates. A signed journal-reserve marker and pending/final aggregates may still use the emergency reserve. Authenticated events remain synchronous and fail closed; a dedicated filesystem is recommended because other processes can consume the reserved space.

docs.title: encryptionPublicKey
docs.text:
SSH Public Key

Optional OpenSSH Ed25519 or RSA public age recipient key, also used by Recording. Bifröst encrypts confidential fields independently for each event:

  • No recipient: signed .baudit; private fields are readable after decompression.
  • With a recipient: signed .beaudit; private fields are compressed and encrypted. Only name, optional domain and outcome, plus signed envelope data such as time, record ID, chain and producer remain visible. See the exact field boundary.

With recording enabled, the same recipient selects .becast for recorded output. Multiple audit logs and their Recordings may use the same recipient, including the same encryptionPublicKeyFile.

Encryption does not cover all local state

A Recording lifecycle outbox can contain signed, unencrypted flow and correlation data even with .beaudit. Protect the entire Recording repository and its backups.

Use exactly one recipient and keep its private key offline. It must differ from all server keys, including host, signing, static SSH-environment and SFTP keys; also check dynamically rendered identity paths. A journal with records cannot change recipients: use a new empty journal and retain the old private key for its evidence.

docs.title: encryptionPublicKeyFile
docs.text:
File Path<SSH Public Key>

Loads the single encryption public key from an OpenSSH public-key file when the auditlog is initialized. This is an alternative to encryptionPublicKey; the two properties cannot be combined. The file must exist and contain exactly one supported public key without authorized-key options or certificates.

docs.title: recording
docs.text:
Session recording

Configures shell and exec recording, local retention, and optional artifact delivery. Recording is disabled by default; recording.enabled: true adds it to the selected audit log. The default strict failure policy remains fail-closed.

docs.title: targets
docs.text:
[]Remote target

Optional destinations for sealed audit segments. Recording may inherit these targets or select its own. See remote targets.

docs.title: Journal
docs.text:
The local journal is the authoritative, crash-safe source of the audit log. Remote targets replicate sealed journal segments and do not replace local persistence.

Use an access-controlled local filesystem and do not modify managed paths while Bifröst runs. The filesystem is trusted: owners, ACLs and link checks are not Bifröst's defense against concurrent external mutation. Signatures, chains, quotas, structural validation and crash recovery still apply; unsupported links can be rejected as invalid repository state.

See audit events for the recorded security transitions, their structured fields, privacy guarantees, and failure behavior.

docs.title: Storage and recovery
docs.text:
• Records are signed and flushed. .baudit and .beaudit segments rotate around 16 MiB; signed hashes link them to head.cbor under <auditlog-directory>/<producer-id>/. See the format and vectors.
  • Startup repairs uncommitted tails but rejects invalid committed data and lost records. Large recovery scans can leave .bifroest-work after a crash; remove stale work only while Bifröst is stopped. Read-only verification uses an OS temporary directory instead.
  • audit export, audit verify and merge can read while Bifröst runs. They verify the signed committed state; later writes are not part of that result. Locally, export and verify use the default configuration and the selected auditlog name. Offline, both accept a complete journal copy through --source and an independently trusted --expectedProducerId without a configuration.
  • Export and merge verify before writing redacted, unsigned JSONL. --with-sensitive includes private fields and needs the offline decryption key for .beaudit.
  • Remote targets deliver only sealed segments, never the signed head or active file. A single downloaded segment is not verifiable as a complete journal. Keep the full journal and an independently trusted chain tip to detect a missing remote suffix.

docs.title: Basic audit logs
docs.text:
1. Define the default audit log of Bifröst:

    /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml
    auditlogs:
  default: {}
flows:
  - name: foo
    ## 'default' auditlog is used by default
    # auditlog: default

    # ...

  2. Start and use Bifröst...

    Bifröst writes unencrypted event segments named *.baudit to the default auditlog directory. The directory also contains signed head.cbor and other managed state; retain the whole journal for verification.

  3. Read the recorded events of Bifröst: 

    bifroest audit export default

# Verified, redacted JSONL from a signed checkpoint on stdout.

    The exported JSONL is an unsigned view, not a substitute for the signed journal. Even redacted metadata needs protection; the clear .baudit files also contain confidential fields after decompression. To include those fields, explicitly add --with-sensitive to audit export and protect its plaintext output.

    To check the journal without JSONL, use audit verify: bifroest audit verify default. It reports outer or full verification on success.

docs.title: Encrypted audit events
docs.text:
1. On an offline and trustworthy workstation, generate the recipient key pair:

    bifroest key generate \
  --identityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key \
  --publicFile   /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key.pub

    /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key should never reach Bifröst. It is only for the recipient, to be able to decrypt the auditlog, if needed.

  2. Transfer only the public key to Bifröst's host: /etc/engity/bifroest/audit-recipient.pub

  3. Configure Bifröst:

    /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml
    auditlogs:
  default:
    encryptionPublicKeyFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/audit-recipient.pub
    # Only for a NEW empty journal; existing .baudit history cannot switch.
    # Bifröst creates /etc/engity/bifroest/auditlog-key on first start.
flows:
  - name: foo
    # ...

  4. Start and use Bifröst.

    Bifröst creates the signing identity and journal automatically when they contain no history. It writes encrypted .beaudit segments; signed outer metadata remains visible.

  5. Read events, redacted:

    bifroest audit export default

# Redacted JSONL from a signed checkpoint; private fields stay encrypted.

  6. Or, fully decrypted:

    1. On the Bifröst host, obtain the producer ID from the server's signing key and retain it through a trusted channel:

      bifroest audit producer-id \
   default
# Save this 64-hex value independently;
# never derive it from the journal.

    2. For a stable complete evidence copy, stop Bifröst and copy /var/lib/engity/bifroest/auditlog to /srv/audit-evidence/auditlog on the offline workstation. Day-to-day redacted reading in step 5 does not require a stop.

      Keep head.cbor, all sealed segments and any active.beaudit together. Remote targets only contain sealed segments and cannot replace this copy.

    3. Export confidential events on the offline workstation. No configuration file or server signing key is needed:

      Offline workstation
      bifroest audit export \
  --source /srv/audit-evidence/auditlog \
  --expectedProducerId "<64-hex-producer-id>" \
  --decryptionIdentityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key \
  --with-sensitive \
  --output /srv/audit-evidence/sensitive.jsonl

      The decrypted JSONL is unsigned and not encrypted and must be protected like sensitive data.

      To verify without exporting events, use bifroest audit verify --source /srv/audit-evidence/auditlog --expectedProducerId "<64-hex-producer-id>" --decryptionIdentityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key --require-full. Without the private key, encrypted journals can only be verified at outer scope. The offline auditlog label defaults to default.

docs.title: Audit events
docs.text: For each selected audit logger, Bifröst writes structured events for security-relevant SSH and browser transitions of the active flow. A flow without an explicit logger or a defined auditlogs.default writes no audit events or recordings. Events contain controlled classifications and technical correlation IDs rather than request contents.

docs.title: Event model
docs.text:
Every event has a name. All other fields are optional and are present only when they apply to that event.

Field Description name Stable event type documented in the event catalog. domain Event category: authentication, connection, housekeeping, port-forwarding, or session. outcome Result: success, denied, failure, or canceled. Start events omit this field. flow Configured flow that selected the audit log. connectionId UUID correlating events from one connection or management operation. sessionId UUID of the persistent Bifröst session, when one is available. operationId UUID correlating the events belonging to one task, forwarding operation, or housekeeping action. recordingId Canonical UUIDv4 identifying one session recording. recordingDigest Lowercase SHA-256 digest of the canonical signed Cast content, cryptographically bound by the recording seal. It is not a hash of the outer native .bcast or .becast container file. target Configured audit-log target name for a Recording delivery transition. It contains no destination address, credentials, or remote path. authenticationMethod public-key, password, keyboard-interactive, or browser-remember-me. authenticationPhase candidate before public-key possession is proven or verified after its proof has been checked. authorizationKind Authorization implementation that produced the result, for example simple or local. sessionTask shell, exec, sftp, or subsystem. sessionSubsystem Subsystem name for an sftp or subsystem task; at most 256 UTF-8 bytes, without NUL. reason Stable machine-readable reason code whose values are documented for each event. errorCategory Controlled error class: unknown, system, config, network, user, permission, or expired. exitCode Non-negative task exit code, including zero. bytesRead, bytesWritten Aggregate transport byte counts in the direction documented for the event. durationMillis Completed operation duration in milliseconds. count Positive number of security-relevant occurrences represented by an aggregate event. pty, agentForwarding, forcedCommand Boolean task properties without their request contents.

The table describes the complete logical event, not what an observer can read from its native container:

  • Public event fields: name, optional domain and outcome. Record ID and time remain visible in the signed envelope.
  • Private map: flow, reason, target, correlation IDs and all other event fields. It is compressed in .baudit and additionally encrypted in .beaudit.
  • Default JSONL omits the private map even for .baudit, but still exposes identifying provenance. JSONL is unsigned; protect it and the original evidence.

Events with the same connectionId belong to one connection or management operation. Events with the same sessionId can span SSH and browser connections to one persistent session. An operationId has meaning within its event lifecycle and must be interpreted together with name.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Authentication is evaluated flow by flow. A flow that does not match the request requirements or does not support the requested authentication method is skipped and produces no event. Evaluation stops after the first flow accepts the request.

docs.title: authentication.flow.evaluated
docs.text:
Written after one flow has actually evaluated an authentication request.

Fields: domain is authentication; outcome, flow, connectionId, and authenticationMethod identify the evaluation. authorizationKind and sessionId are present when the authorization result supplies them. authenticationPhase is present for public-key authentication. errorCategory is present when evaluation failed with an error.

Outcomes:

  • success: the flow accepted the authentication request.
  • denied: the flow rejected the request, including user-classified authorization errors.
  • failure: evaluation failed for another reason.

For public keys, candidate means that the key or certificate was evaluated before proof of private-key possession. User certificates are evaluated again with verified after their signature has been verified. An accepted candidate does not by itself mean that authentication succeeded.

Unauthenticated evaluation details are subject to the bounded SSH audit limits. This includes every public-key candidate, including accepted candidates, and denied or failed password and keyboard-interactive evaluations. Accepted password and keyboard-interactive results and every public-key verified result bypass these limits.

docs.title: authentication.flow.evaluations-suppressed
docs.text:
A signed aggregate written when detailed unauthenticated authentication.flow.evaluated records are suppressed. It never changes the authentication result.

Fields: domain is authentication; reason, count, and durationMillis describe the suppressed batch. For rate-limit, outcome identifies the common outcome represented by the batch. Aggregation can span flows that reference the same audit log, so flow, authentication method, connection IDs, and remote addresses are intentionally omitted. For journal-reserve, outcome is omitted because the batch can contain mixed outcomes.

Reasons:

  • rate-limit: the per-source or service-wide token bucket had no detail token available.

  • journal-reserve: the configured minimum free filesystem space would have been crossed by a suppressible write.

  • The first rate-limited suppression is signed immediately with count: 1. Later counts are aggregated in memory and flushed periodically or at orderly shutdown. A hard crash can lose only unflushed counts, not the first signed marker.

  • If the journal reserve is reached while a rate-limit aggregate is pending, that aggregate keeps its reason and outcome and uses the emergency reserve. Only later suppressed evaluations count as journal-reserve. While the reserve is active, recovery is probed when new unauthenticated evaluations arrive; markers do not repeatedly consume it.
  • Final aggregates during orderly shutdown bypass minimumFreeBytes as bounded emergency writes. If one fails, Bifröst still closes other resources but reports an incomplete audit flush.

docs.title: authentication.completed
docs.text:
Written when an authorization accepted by a flow either completes successfully or is denied because its session is incompatible with the selected environment. For public keys, success is written only after the SSH signature has been verified.

This event is not a summary of every failed authentication attempt. It is omitted when no flow accepts the request, public-key possession cannot be proven, or an error prevents Bifröst from reaching one of the final results described above. Evaluated flows are still represented by their authentication.flow.evaluated events where applicable.

Fields: domain is authentication; outcome, flow, connectionId, authenticationMethod, and authorizationKind identify the final result. sessionId is present when the authorization has a session.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • success: authentication completed successfully; reason is omitted.
  • denied: the credentials were accepted by the flow, but its session was incompatible with the selected environment; reason is session-incompatible.

docs.title: session.pty.decided
docs.text:
Written before Bifröst answers a PTY allocation request.

Fields: domain is session; outcome, flow, connectionId, sessionId, and authorizationKind identify the decision. reason and errorCategory are present when applicable.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • success: both authorized-key and environment policies permit the request.
  • denied with authorized-key-policy: the active authorized-key policy forbids PTY allocation.
  • denied with environment-policy: the environment does not support or permit the requested PTY.
  • denied with invalid-request: session recording cannot represent the requested terminal type or dimensions.
  • failure with environment-policy: evaluation of the environment policy failed; errorCategory classifies the failure.

The event does not contain the terminal type, terminal dimensions, or terminal modes.

docs.title: session.agent-forwarding.decided
docs.text:
Written before Bifröst answers an SSH agent-forwarding request.

Fields: domain is session; outcome, flow, connectionId, sessionId, and authorizationKind identify the decision.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • success: the active authorization permits agent forwarding.
  • denied with authorized-key-policy: the active authorized-key policy forbids agent forwarding.

The event does not contain agent messages, keys, or socket paths.

docs.title: session.recording.started
docs.text:
Written after the first recording content and recovery head are durable, before notice, banner or target output. SFTP and direct forwarding do not produce recording lifecycle events.

If the audit write reports an error, target execution does not start. Bifröst finalizes the recording as failed and attempts session.recording.failed with reason audit-write. Both events can exist if the backend committed before reporting an error.

Fields: domain is session; flow, connectionId, sessionId, operationId, recordingId, and sessionTask correlate the recording with its shell or exec task. pty records whether the session has a PTY. outcome is omitted.

docs.title: session.recording.completed
docs.text:
Written only after a completed recording is sealed, synchronized, verified and atomically published. Correlation fields match session.recording.started; outcome: success, durationMillis, exitCode and recordingDigest describe the immutable result.

The signed outbox binds the Cast and outer artifact digests before publication in a non-replayable prepared state. Verified publication promotes it to pending; only then can startup replay the event. An audit-write failure leaves the sealed artifact intact but fails the SSH operation closed.

docs.title: session.recording.incomplete
docs.text:
Written only after an incomplete recording has been sealed, synchronized, verified, and atomically published. The correlation fields are the same as for session.recording.started; durationMillis and recordingDigest describe the immutable result.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • canceled with context-canceled: the SSH task context was canceled.
  • canceled with deadline-exceeded: the SSH task deadline expired.
  • failure with invalid-exit-code: execution returned no valid exit code.
  • failure with session-error: another task error prevented normal completion; errorCategory classifies it.
  • failure with startup-recovery: startup recovered an active recording that had not completed sealing before the previous process stopped.

Startup recovery seals unfinished recordings as incomplete. The signed lifecycle intent holds correlation data needed to finish BECast without its private decryption key.

  • Already durable terminal events and receipts are preserved, not replaced.
  • prepared is not replayable until its artifact is published and verified.
  • pending is replayed at least once. A crash after audit commit can duplicate the same event, but cannot silently lose it.

docs.title: session.recording.failed
docs.text:
Written when recording creation, capture, checkpointing, publication or the required start audit write fails. Correlation fields match session.recording.started; outcome: failure and errorCategory classify the result.

  • reason: recording-create, recording-capture, recording-seal or audit-write.
  • recordingDigest appears only if a failed artifact was still sealed and published. A create failure has no preceding session.recording.started event.

docs.title: session.recording.delivery.failed
docs.text:
Written after the first failed attempt for a Recording and target. domain: session, outcome: failure, recordingId, target and operationId identify the episode; errorCategory classifies it. Flow, connection, session, paths, endpoint and digest are omitted: they are unnecessary here and not all safely recoverable after restart.

The failure intent and operation ID are stored in the signed delivery receipt before the event is attempted. Further publication attempts are blocked until the event has been recorded and its durable receipt marker has been written. Later failures in the same delivery episode do not produce more events, including after restart.

docs.title: session.recording.delivery.succeeded
docs.text:
Written after a target has accepted the exact artifact and its signed local acknowledgement is durable. domain is session; outcome is success; and recordingId, target, and operationId match the delivery episode and its optional session.recording.delivery.failed event. A direct success has no preceding failure event.

The signed receipt keeps the success event pending until it is recorded. Startup replays it without republishing the artifact. Flush and retention require both the target acknowledgement and durable success-audit marker. A crash between audit and marker commits can replay an identical event, not silently discard it.

docs.title: session.task.started
docs.text:
Written immediately before Bifröst begins service execution of a shell, exec, SFTP/subsystem task or management operation. If this event cannot be recorded, the task does not start.

Fields: domain is session; flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind, operationId, and sessionTask identify the task. pty, agentForwarding, and forcedCommand describe Boolean task properties. outcome is omitted.

The event records the requested task category. Applying an authorized-key forced command does not expose that command or change sessionTask; only forcedCommand: true indicates that the policy was applied.

docs.title: session.task.completed
docs.text:
Written when a previously started task finishes. Its operationId, flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind, and sessionTask match the corresponding session.task.started event.

Fields: domain is session; outcome and durationMillis describe completion. exitCode, reason, and errorCategory are present when applicable.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • success: execution completed and exitCode contains the process result. A non-zero exit code is still a successfully completed task.
  • canceled with context-canceled: the task context was canceled.
  • canceled with deadline-exceeded: the task deadline expired.
  • failure with invalid-exit-code: execution returned neither an error nor a valid exit code.
  • failure: task execution failed; errorCategory classifies the failure.

docs.title: session.disconnect.started
docs.text:
Written before an authorized management command disconnects a session. domain is session; flow and sessionId identify the target session, while connectionId identifies the initiating management connection. Its authentication and task events identify the administrator. operationId pairs the start and completion.

The events are recorded according to the management and target flow's audit configurations, once if both use the same auditlog. A strict start-audit failure prevents the action. Invalid, ambiguous or self-targeting requests fail before these events; the management task lifecycle still records the failed command.

docs.title: session.disconnect.completed
docs.text: Written after disconnection returns, with the same identifiers as its start event. durationMillis records elapsed time. outcome: success means the operation completed; outcome: failure and errorCategory indicate failure, possibly after partial changes.

docs.title: session.dispose.started
docs.text: Written before a management action revokes a session, disconnects its connections and runs configured environment and authorization cleanup. Fields and audit routing match session.disconnect.started.

docs.title: session.dispose.completed
docs.text: Written after disposal returns, with the same identifiers as its start event. Completion fields and outcomes match session.disconnect.completed. Disposal does not delete retained session metadata, audit logs or Recordings. A failure can occur after revocation or after some resources have already been removed.

docs.title: port-forwarding.direct.decided
docs.text:
Written when direct-forwarding request processing reaches a policy decision or rejects an invalid request. A successful decision follows request parsing and both policy checks; malformed requests and earlier policy denials are recorded at the point where processing stops. The event is always recorded before Bifröst attempts to open the destination connection.

Fields: domain is port-forwarding; outcome, flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind, and operationId identify the decision. reason and errorCategory are present when applicable.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • success: policy permits the request; this does not mean that the destination or SSH channel was opened successfully.
  • denied with authorized-key-policy: the active authorized-key policy forbids the destination.
  • denied with environment-policy: the environment policy forbids forwarding.
  • failure with invalid-request: the SSH request payload or destination was invalid.
  • failure with environment: the target environment could not be prepared.
  • failure with environment-policy: evaluation of the environment policy failed.

docs.title: port-forwarding.direct.open-failed
docs.text:
Written after a successful port-forwarding.direct.decided event when Bifröst cannot establish the destination connection or accept the SSH channel. No port-forwarding.direct.started or port-forwarding.direct.completed event follows for that operation.

Fields: domain is port-forwarding; outcome, flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind, and operationId correlate the failed open with its decision. reason identifies the result. errorCategory is present for failed open attempts, but omitted when the environment explicitly denies the destination.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • denied with destination-rejected: the environment explicitly rejected the destination connection.
  • failure with destination-connect: opening the destination connection failed.
  • failure with channel-accept: accepting the SSH channel failed.

docs.title: port-forwarding.direct.started
docs.text:
Written after both the destination connection and SSH channel have been established, immediately before Bifröst starts bidirectional streaming. If this event cannot be recorded, streaming does not start.

Fields: domain is port-forwarding; flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind, and operationId correlate the start with the preceding decision. outcome is omitted.

docs.title: port-forwarding.direct.completed
docs.text:
Written when a previously started direct-forwarding stream ends.

Fields: domain is port-forwarding; outcome, flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind, and operationId correlate completion with the decision and start events. bytesRead counts source-to-destination bytes, bytesWritten counts destination-to-source bytes, and durationMillis measures the streaming duration. reason and errorCategory are present when applicable.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • success: bidirectional streaming ended without an error.
  • canceled with context-canceled: the forwarding context was canceled.
  • canceled with deadline-exceeded: the forwarding deadline expired.
  • failure: streaming failed; errorCategory classifies the failure.

docs.title: port-forwarding.reverse.decided
docs.text:
Written after Bifröst evaluates a reverse-forwarding request.

Fields: domain is port-forwarding; outcome, flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind, and operationId identify the decision. reason and errorCategory are present when applicable.

Outcomes and reasons:

  • success: policy permits the request.
  • denied with authorized-key-policy: the active authorized-key policy forbids the bind address.
  • denied with invalid-bind: the requested bind address or port is invalid.
  • denied with environment-policy: the environment policy forbids reverse forwarding.
  • failure with environment: the target environment could not be prepared.
  • failure with environment-policy: evaluation of the environment policy failed.

This event records only the policy decision, not whether a listener was successfully created or a forwarded stream established. The reverse listener binds in the selected environment (Local host, Docker container, Kubernetes Pod, or SSH target sshd), not generally on the Bifröst host.

docs.title: connection.closed
docs.text:
Written when an authenticated SSH connection ends. A pre-authentication connection cannot be assigned to one flow audit log and therefore produces no connection.closed event.

Fields: domain: connection; flow, connectionId, sessionId, authorizationKind and reason: disconnected identify the connection. durationMillis covers its full lifetime.

  • bytesRead: SSH client to Bifröst; bytesWritten: Bifröst to SSH client, measured at the wrapped SSH transport.
