  • No outcome: the disconnect callback cannot reliably distinguish success from failure.

docs.title: Housekeeping
docs.text: Housekeeping events are not associated with an active SSH connection. They therefore contain no connectionId or authorizationKind.

docs.title: housekeeping.session.dispose.started
docs.text:
Written before housekeeping disposes the session state, environment, and authorization resources of an expired session. If this event cannot be recorded, disposal is not attempted.

Fields: domain is housekeeping; flow, sessionId, and operationId identify the disposal attempt. reason is expired for the initial expiry path when the session is not yet selected for deletion. reason is retention-elapsed when housekeeping has selected the deletion path, either because the retention threshold elapsed or because the session was already marked as disposed. outcome is omitted.

docs.title: housekeeping.session.dispose.completed
docs.text:
Written after the disposal attempt returns. Its flow, sessionId, operationId, and reason match the corresponding housekeeping.session.dispose.started event.

Fields: domain: housekeeping; durationMillis measures the attempt. outcome: success means disposal completed, even if nothing needed changing. failure has an errorCategory.

A persisted token may be removed only when its authorizer safely classifies it as permanently unusable (malformed local data, removed configuration or user). Transient, network, system or unclassified restore failures do not authorize removal.

docs.title: housekeeping.session.delete.started
docs.text:
Written before housekeeping deletes an expired or already disposed session from persistent session storage. If this event cannot be recorded, deletion is not attempted.

Fields: domain is housekeeping; flow, sessionId, and operationId identify the deletion attempt. reason is retention-elapsed, which identifies the deletion path but does not by itself prove that the full configured retention duration elapsed: an already disposed session also enters this path. outcome is omitted.

docs.title: housekeeping.session.delete.completed
docs.text:
Written after the persistent session deletion returns. Its flow, sessionId, operationId, and reason match the corresponding housekeeping.session.delete.started event.

Fields: domain is housekeeping; durationMillis measures the deletion attempt. outcome is success only when deletion completed without an error. On failure, errorCategory classifies the error.

docs.title: housekeeping.recording.delete.started
docs.text:
Written before housekeeping deletes a sealed session Recording whose configured retention period has elapsed. If this event cannot be recorded, deletion is not attempted.

Fields: domain is housekeeping; recordingId and operationId identify the logical deletion operation. The operation ID is stable across crash recovery, so this event may be repeated before the durable completion marker exists. reason is retention-elapsed. outcome is omitted. The event contains no Recording file name, path, digest, or content.

docs.title: housekeeping.recording.delete.completed
docs.text:
Written after the artifact is removed and its signed receipt reaches durable completion-pending. The receipt itself is removed only after this event succeeds. An ambiguous audit result or failed final cleanup retries the same event, not the deletion. recordingId, operationId and reason match the start event.

Fields: domain: housekeeping. On success, durationMillis: 0 keeps retries identical. On failure, durationMillis measures the failed attempt, errorCategory classifies it and the receipt remains for retry.

docs.title: housekeeping.orphaned-session.cleanup.skipped
docs.text:
If a persisted session's flow is missing, housekeeping cannot safely interpret its environment or authorization tokens. It preserves the whole session for operator recovery, even past retention; it neither reads tokens nor disposes or deletes that session.

  • The original audit-log assignment is unknown. The identical skip event goes to every active audit log, never a guessed replacement; without active logs, only a normal log entry is possible.
  • Fields: domain: housekeeping; flow is the unknown original flow, sessionId the preserved session, reason: missing-flow, outcome: denied. No operation ID, token contents, environment details or retention timestamps are emitted.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
Bifröst's built-in audit events never contain:

  • Passwords, keyboard-interactive answers, access or persisted authorization tokens, private keys, or public-key material.
  • Commands, arguments, original or forced command text, or environment values.
  • SFTP paths, file names, protocol payloads, or file contents.
  • Terminal types, dimensions, or modes.
  • Agent messages, keys, or socket paths.
  • Raw errors, wrapped causes, or formatted error messages.
  • Direct-forwarding destinations, reverse bind addresses, or client-claimed origin addresses.

Error events expose only documented reason codes and broad errorCategory values:

  • .beaudit encrypts private event fields in segments; name, domain, outcome, time and verification metadata remain visible and signed.
  • .baudit stores private fields in clear form, but the default JSONL export still omits them.
  • The local Recording lifecycle outbox can store private event fields as signed, unencrypted JSON until completion.

Protect local repositories, backups, containers and exports. See the exact container boundary.

docs.title: Audit-event persistence failures
docs.text:
• strict: local writes are synchronous. A failed pre-action write denies that action and closes only its SSH connection; the service does not retry the event or shut down.
  • bestEffort: the first local failure disables the whole audit log and its recording until restart. The SSH operation may continue without further audit writes.
  • Suppression is not a write failure: token-bucket exhaustion or the journal reserve replaces only suppressible pre-authentication details with bounded signed aggregates. Successful authentication is not denied. Under strict, failure to inspect free space or write a chosen detail, marker or aggregate still closes the causing connection.
  • After-action failure: a completed action cannot be undone. strict reports the failure and closes its connection; bestEffort disables the audit log.
  • Housekeeping: a failed start-event write prevents its session action under strict. Under bestEffort, housekeeping may proceed without start/completion events. Failed missing-flow skip audits never cause the orphaned session to be modified; housekeeping continues with later sessions. Unrelated SSH connections and the service remain running.
  • Remote delivery: outages leave sealed artifacts in the local spool for retry. Failed delivery-transition audits pause only that Recording and target, not other connections or targets.

See failure policy and session-recording failures.

docs.title: Session recording
docs.text: Session recording is disabled by default. Configure it under a selected audit log to capture one signed asciicast v3 for each SSH or browser shell or exec task, alongside the audit journal.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = false

Enables session recording for flows that select this audit log. The journal is already active for a selected logger; this flag adds the Recording repository and signed output artifacts.

docs.title: directory
docs.text:
File Path = "<os specific>"

Local recording repository. Keep it on an access-controlled filesystem, separate from session storage, audit journals and key files. Bifröst manages it exclusively; do not modify it or rotate its files externally.

The default depends on the operating system:

  • Linux: /var/lib/engity/bifroest/recordings
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/recordings
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\recordings

The local filesystem is trusted; repository signatures do not protect against an operator or attacker who can alter managed paths concurrently.

docs.title: compression
docs.text:
Compression

Compression profile for recorded event chunks.

docs.title: chunkSizeBytes
docs.text:
uint64 = 262144

Target chunk size before compression, from 1 to 1048577 bytes. An indivisible event group can exceed this target.

docs.title: flushInterval
docs.text:
Duration = "2s"

Maximum time between checkpoints while content is pending; must be positive.

docs.title: flushSizeBytes
docs.text:
uint64 = 1048576

Pending output threshold for a checkpoint; must be positive.

docs.title: maximumSpoolBytes
docs.text:
uint64 = 107374182400

Maximum local spool, including active and sealed recordings, receipts, and recovery work (default 100 GiB). Must be at least chunkSizeBytes and flushSizeBytes. If the spool is full, recording fails closed; startup never deletes evidence just to fit the limit.

docs.title: retainFor
docs.text:
Duration = "720h"

How long an eligible sealed recording remains locally (default 30 days). 0s stops new automatic deletions but not one already begun. See retention.

docs.title: notice
docs.text:
String = ""

Optional notice before an interactive PTY shell. It can use {{.recording.id}} and {{.recording.startedAt}}; Bifröst adds no newline. The notice becomes recorded output and does not appear for exec or non-PTY tasks. Do not rely on it as the only notice where policy requires one for those tasks.

docs.title: targets
docs.text:
[]Remote target = "inherit"

Selects remote destinations for sealed recordings:

  • inherit uses every target configured in the parent audit log.
  • false disables remote recording delivery while leaving audit-log target delivery unchanged.
  • A nonempty list defines independent recording targets using the same S3, SFTP, and WebDAV schemas as the audit log.

Every selected target is required. Settle outstanding delivery before changing destinations or disabling Recording; otherwise pending artifacts remain in the local spool. See remote target behavior.

docs.title: level
docs.text:
string = "default"

Compression profile for chunked Zstandard encoding. default is currently the only supported value.

docs.title: Captured data and privacy
docs.text:
• PTY tasks capture terminal output and resize events; non-PTY tasks capture stdout and stderr. SFTP and forwarding payloads are not recorded. A forced command is recorded as an exec task.
  • Raw keyboard input is not captured. Echoed commands and secrets printed by programs can still appear in the output. Treat recordings and exported Casts as sensitive; encrypted containers also expose public metadata.
  • Recording is terminal playback, not a byte-for-byte SSH capture. With the default failurePolicy: strict, a local recording failure aborts the affected task. With bestEffort, Bifröst disables the audit log and recording until restart. See failure policy.

docs.title: Formats and keys
docs.text:
Recording inherits its signing identity and optional age recipient from the parent audit log. These keys may be shared across audit logs; each Recording repository must still have its own directory. See the audit-log key configuration.

  • Without encryptionPublicKey or encryptionPublicKeyFile, Bifröst stores signed, compressed native .bcast artifacts.
  • With an encryption recipient, Bifröst stores signed CBOR .becast artifacts whose compressed event groups are independently encrypted with age.

Encrypted inspection or verification without the private age key checks only the signed outer envelope, not decrypted content or claimed status. recording verify with a matching key checks the full content without exporting a Cast; --require-full fails rather than accepting outer-only verification. Full export also verifies the content. Even encrypted artifacts expose metadata such as recording ID and timing; protect them. See the native format and test vectors for wire details.

Switching between .bcast and .becast requires a new empty Recording directory. Changing the audit recipient also requires a new empty audit-log directory. Older recording-only repositories cannot switch to audited recording in place: use a new empty Recording directory. Preserve old evidence and decryption keys. If the signing key is lost, Bifröst refuses to regenerate it over existing history.

docs.title: Storage and recovery
docs.text:
• active/ holds in-progress recordings; sealed/ holds immutable .bcast or .becast files. Startup seals interrupted recordings as incomplete. Integrity failures in accepted evidence fail closed; there is no manual repair command.
  • quarantine/ and .bifroest-work/ hold rejected and in-progress recovery work. Do not manually move these files into sealed/.
  • .delivery/ holds signed receipts. Its receipt.lifecycle outbox holds signed, unencrypted flow names, correlation IDs and digests until the event is recorded. Protect the entire repository and its backups with filesystem permissions/ACLs; signatures protect integrity, not confidentiality.

Recovery replays pending terminal audit events at least once; a crash after commit can produce an identical duplicate. See recording lifecycle events.

docs.title: Remote delivery and retention
docs.text:
Signed receipts bind sealed bytes to selected remote targets. Delivery retries asynchronously; changing a target cannot redirect an outstanding artifact. See remote delivery.

With targets, retainFor begins after the last durable acknowledgement and requires success-audit markers. Without targets, it begins at sealing. Bifröst deletes only local recordings, not remote copies; set remote retention separately. retainFor: 0s stops new automatic deletions.

docs.title: Export and playback
docs.text:
• recording ls and recording show read verified metadata from a configured repository locally or through the SSH management flow. Lists use bounded pages and stream verified entries by default.
  • recording export verifies the signature and content before writing a full, never redacted Cast; --with-sensitive is required. Protect session.cast and open it with an asciicast v3 player.
  • recording play verifies and replays captured terminal output directly, with --with-sensitive and optional --speed.
  • recording verify checks a locally selected UUID against the configured signing identity, or an offline or downloaded original against an independently trusted producer ID, without outputting Cast content. It reports whether verification was outer or full.
  • The management client downloads signed originals for client-side verification, export and playback when the authorized flow grants recordings.download. Remote delivery targets store sealed originals, not plaintext Casts. For offline metadata without export, use recording inspect; see the native format for verification details.

docs.title: Clear recording
docs.text:
1. Add recording to the explicitly defined default logger. Flows use it unless they select another audit log:

    /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml
    auditlogs:
  default:
    recording:
      enabled: true

  2. Start Bifröst and use a shell or exec task. After it ends, find <recording-uuid>.bcast under recording.directory/sealed/. An optional recording notice shows the ID only for interactive PTY shells. The logger also writes audit events correlating the Recording with its session.

  3. On the running Bifröst host, export the already sealed .bcast to a file outside the repository. The local signing identity is used automatically; no configuration path or producer ID needs to be repeated:

    bifroest recording export \
  --with-sensitive \
  --output session.cast \
  default <recording-uuid>

    To verify it without a Cast export, run bifroest recording verify default <recording-uuid>.

docs.title: Encrypted recording
docs.text:
1. For new, empty audit and Recording directories, configure an offline age recipient on the parent entry. Bifröst then writes .becast instead of .bcast and an encrypted .beaudit journal:

    /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml
    auditlogs:
  default:
    encryptionPublicKeyFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/audit-recipient.pub
    recording:
      enabled: true

  2. On the Bifröst host, get the signing producer ID from the local signing key and transfer it independently to the offline workstation. Copy the already sealed .becast there without stopping Bifröst; do not copy the signing private key:

    bifroest audit producer-id default
# Independently retain this 64-hex ID; do not take it from the .becast file.

  3. On the offline workstation, decrypt and export the copied artifact. The recipient's private key stays offline:

    bifroest recording export \
  --expectedProducerId "<trusted-64-hex-producer-id>" \
  --decryptionIdentityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key \
  --with-sensitive \
  --output session.cast \
  session.becast

    To verify the encrypted original without creating a Cast, run bifroest recording verify --expectedProducerId "<trusted-64-hex-producer-id>" --decryptionIdentityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key --require-full session.becast. Without the private key, verification is outer-only unless --require-full makes it fail.

docs.title: Remote targets
docs.text:
Remote targets copy sealed originals, not exports:

  • Audit segments: .baudit or .beaudit under <producer-id>/<segment-file-name>.
  • Selected session recordings: .bcast or .becast under <producer-id>/<recording-uuid>.<suffix>.

The audit journal remains authoritative and retains its segments. Remote targets never receive head.cbor, the active segment, JSONL or a decrypted Cast. A downloaded segment alone is not a complete journal for the audit CLI. Keep the complete local journal for verification and an independently trusted chain tip to detect missing remote history.

Clear originals contain confidential content after decompression; encrypted originals expose signed public metadata. Protect every destination and configure its retention independently.

docs.title: Available targets
docs.text:
Each target needs a unique name within its audit log and selects an implementation with type:

  • S3 stores segments in AWS S3 or a compatible object store.
  • SFTP stores segments on an SSH-authenticated SFTP server.
  • WebDAV stores segments in an HTTPS WebDAV collection.

docs.title: Delivery behavior
docs.text:
• Each target has an independent worker. Segments are delivered in order; failures retry with backoff and a fresh timeout without blocking local audit writes or other targets.
  • Filesystem notifications trigger delivery, backed by a periodic scan. If notifications fail, polling continues with a warning.
  • On shutdown, Bifröst seals a non-empty active segment and allows up to five seconds for delivery. Undelivered segments remain local for the next start.

docs.title: Delivery identity
docs.text:
A signed cursor under <auditlog-directory>/.delivery/ binds the last confirmed segment to its target name and effective destination:

  • Credentials and timeouts can rotate without resetting it. Changing the endpoint, namespace, bucket, prefix, directory, destination user or SFTP host-key trust under the same name fails closed. Use a new target name to deliver the full history to a replacement destination.
  • For SFTP, host-key trust depends on the knownHosts entries or contents of knownHostsFile, not its path. Switching to acceptAllHostKeys also changes the destination identity.
  • Before the next delivery and again after restart, Bifröst reconstructs and verifies the predecessor chain against the cursor. Removing a confirmed local segment fails closed: a cursor alone cannot reconstruct the chain or prove a remote copy still exists.

docs.title: Recording receipts
docs.text:
Before publishing a sealed recording locally, Bifröst stores a signed receipt under its repository's .delivery/. It permanently binds the artifact's digest and size to the selected targets and destination fingerprints at sealing time. Later target changes cannot redirect that artifact.

At startup:

  • A sealed artifact without its matching receipt fails closed.
  • A receipt without its artifact fails closed, unless durable retention deletion already began.
  • If both receipt and artifact disappear, detection requires an independent inventory.

Receipts also hold the outbox for session.recording.delivery.failed and session.recording.delivery.succeeded. All receipts count toward maximumSpoolBytes; temporary copies left by atomic replacement are recovered before admitting more spool growth.

docs.title: Recording delivery
docs.text:
• One sequential worker per selected target retries asynchronously with backoff and jitter; notifications have a periodic safety scan.
  • The first failure in an episode is durably recorded and audited before another attempt. A successful publication needs both a signed acknowledgement and success audit event. Startup replays a pending success event without republishing.
  • If acknowledgement persistence fails, the running worker does not immediately republish; restart can repeat publication. Targets must reject conflicting bytes and support idempotent retries.
  • Changing or removing a target with outstanding delivery (or an enabled audit obligation) fails at startup. Completed historical targets do not block changes.
  • Shutdown allows up to five seconds for acknowledgements and audit events. Unfinished work remains in the local spool for restart.

docs.title: Recording retention
docs.text:
recording.retainFor defaults to 30 days. It starts at sealing without targets, or at the latest durable target acknowledgement with targets. Each selected target's success event must also be durably marked before deletion.

Housekeeping verifies the signed receipt and artifact, marks deletion durably, deletes the local artifact before the receipt, and retries later if verification, deletion or audit-start fails. retainFor: 0s stops new deletions, not one already begun. Remote copies and local audit-log segments are never deleted by Recording retention.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
An S3 target with bucket company-bifroest-audit and prefix bifroest-auditlog stores a sealed segment at:

s3://company-bifroest-audit/bifroest-auditlog/<producer-id>/segment-00000000000000000001-<segment-hash>.beaudit

The placeholders are not trust anchors. Preserve the exact bytes; the remote file name alone cannot establish producer identity.

docs.title: S3
docs.text: The S3 target stores sealed segments in AWS S3 or a compatible HTTPS object store. Objects use the key <prefix>/<producer-id>/<sealed-segment-file>. Each target has its own explicitly configured credentials.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

The unique, path-safe name of this target within the audit log.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
string = "s3"

Selects the S3 target implementation. Type names are case-insensitive when read; Bifröst writes the canonical value s3.

docs.title: publishAttemptTimeout
docs.text:
duration = "2m"

Positive deadline for one complete attempt: hashing, conditional upload, conflict check and cleanup. Timeout cancels the request; the next retry gets a fresh deadline.

docs.title: bucket
docs.text:
string

The destination bucket. It must follow the AWS general-purpose bucket naming rules.

docs.title: region
docs.text:
string = 

"{{ env \`AWS_REGION\` | default (env \`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION\`) }}"

The SigV4 signing region. This value supports Bifröst string templates without a context object. AWS_REGION takes precedence over AWS_DEFAULT_REGION; a non-empty result is required when the target is initialized.

docs.title: prefix
docs.text:
string = ""

An optional object-key prefix without a leading or trailing slash. Empty and relative path components are rejected.

docs.title: endpoint
docs.text:
URL

Optional absolute HTTPS endpoint without user information, path, query or fragment. Omitted: use AWS S3 for region; bucket and region bind the destination identity. Other providers require an explicit endpoint; AWS endpoint override environment variables are ignored.

Identify the destination

An explicit endpoint also requires destinationIdentity or expectedBucketOwner. Otherwise the same endpoint could select another namespace when credentials change, so startup fails closed.

docs.title: pathStyle
docs.text:
bool = false

If true, addresses the bucket in the URL path instead of as a hostname. Enable this only when required by the selected S3-compatible service.

docs.title: expectedBucketOwner
docs.text:
string

Optional twelve-digit AWS account ID sent with both PutObject and conflict-checking GetObject requests. AWS rejects the request when the bucket belongs to another account. Omit this AWS-specific protection for services that do not support it.

docs.title: destinationIdentity
docs.text:
string = ""

Stable, non-secret tenant or namespace ID for S3-compatible endpoints without expectedBucketOwner. At most 256 bytes, no control characters. Changing it under an existing target name fails closed. Never use a credential or session token here.

docs.title: accessKeyId
docs.text:
string = 

"{{ env \`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID\` | default (env \`AWS_ACCESS_KEY\`) }}"

Non-empty access key ID; supports a string template. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID takes precedence over AWS_ACCESS_KEY. Configure this and secretAccessKey together, or leave both at their defaults.

docs.title: secretAccessKey
docs.text:
string = 

"{{ env \`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\` | default (env \`AWS_SECRET_KEY\`) }}"

Non-empty secret access key; supports a string template. AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY takes precedence over AWS_SECRET_KEY. Prefer an environment variable or file template over plaintext YAML.

docs.title: sessionToken
docs.text:
string = 

"{{ env \`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN\` }}"

Optional session token; supports a string template. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN default applies only when both access and secret keys also use their defaults. Set it explicitly for custom credentials.

docs.title: Credentials and identity
docs.text:
Access key, secret key and session token are excluded from the durable destination identity; a complete temporary credential set may rotate without resetting the cursor. Use destinationIdentity or expectedBucketOwner to pin a credential-selected namespace.

Credential template results are not trimmed. Avoid trailing newlines in secret files. Bifröst does not use AWS profiles, instance metadata, web identity or other default credential providers.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
• PutObject uses If-None-Match: *; multipart uploads and overwrites are not used.
  • If the object already exists, GetObject must confirm both size and SHA-256. Different bytes are rejected.
  • S3-compatible services must support SigV4, conditional writes, SHA-256 checksums and GetObject. Verify these capabilities before choosing OVHcloud, MinIO, Ceph or Wasabi.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The credentials need only these S3 actions on the configured bucket and prefix:

  • s3:PutObject to publish a sealed segment conditionally.
  • s3:GetObject to verify an object after a conditional-write conflict.

No s3:ListBucket, s3:DeleteObject or multipart-upload permission is needed. SSE-KMS may also require kms:GenerateDataKey for writes and kms:Decrypt for conflict checks.

docs.title: AWS
docs.text:
With AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY set for the Bifröst process, the default templates keep the target concise:

auditlogs:
  default:
    targets:
      - name: aws-archive
        type: s3
        bucket: company-bifroest-audit
        prefix: bifroest-auditlog
        expectedBucketOwner: "123456789012"

docs.title: S3-compatible (OVH)
docs.text:
This OVHcloud-style example uses an explicit endpoint and target-specific credential sources. Other targets can reference different environment variables or files in the same way.

auditlogs:
  default:
    targets:
      - name: ovh-archive
        type: s3
        bucket: company-bifroest-audit
        region: gra
        endpoint: https://s3.gra.io.cloud.ovh.net
        destinationIdentity: company-production-project
        accessKeyId: '{{ env `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` }}'
        secretAccessKey: '{{ env `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` }}'

docs.title: SFTP
docs.text: The SFTP target stores sealed segments below an existing absolute directory. Bifröst creates one child directory per producer and writes files as <directory>/<producer-id>/<sealed-segment-file>. The server must support the OpenSSH hardlink@openssh.com extension.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

The unique, path-safe name of this target within the audit log.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
string = "sftp"

Selects the SFTP target implementation. Type names are case-insensitive when read; Bifröst writes the canonical value sftp.

docs.title: publishAttemptTimeout
docs.text:
duration = "2m"

Positive deadline for hashing, connection, upload, read-back check and hard-link publication. On cancellation Bifröst closes the SSH connection. If an upload or link may have happened, it opens one fresh connection for one cleanup attempt, separately limited to five seconds. Failed cleanup remains retryable by deterministic temporary-file name.

docs.title: address
docs.text:
string

The SSH server as host, host:port, or [IPv6-address]:port. An omitted port defaults to 22.

docs.title: user
docs.text:
string

The SSH user. This value supports Bifröst string templates without a context object and must render to a non-empty value without control characters.

docs.title: directory
docs.text:
string

The existing absolute POSIX path on the SFTP server. Empty and relative path components are rejected. / is valid when the SFTP account is confined to an appropriate server-side root.

docs.title: knownHosts
docs.text:
string

Inline OpenSSH known_hosts entries used to verify the server host key.

docs.title: knownHostsFile
docs.text:
File Path

Explicit OpenSSH known_hosts file (maximum 16 MiB). Bifröst never reads user or system files implicitly. It can be combined with knownHosts; changes require a target restart.

docs.title: acceptAllHostKeys
docs.text:
bool = false

Disables server host-key verification. This cannot be combined with knownHosts or knownHostsFile and should only be used in controlled test environments.

Warning

Setting acceptAllHostKeys: true makes the target connection vulnerable to on-path attacks.

docs.title: identityFiles
docs.text:
list of File Paths

One or more unencrypted OpenSSH or PEM private keys, tried in order. Paths are static, not templates; keys must differ from audit signing and encryption keys. Files must be regular, owned by the Bifröst user and at most 1 MiB:

  • Unix: no group or other access.
  • Windows: protected DACL allowing only the owner and SYSTEM.

docs.title: password
docs.text:
string = ""

The SSH password. This value supports Bifröst string templates without a context object. Prefer an environment variable or the file template function over storing it directly in YAML. Template results are used exactly as rendered and are not trimmed.

Exactly one authentication method is required: either password or at least one identityFiles entry.

docs.title: connectTimeout
docs.text:
duration = "10s"

TCP, SSH and SFTP setup timeout. 0s disables this additional limit; negative values are rejected. The earlier of this and publishAttemptTimeout wins.

docs.title: Delivery identity
docs.text: Host-key trust binds to inline knownHosts entries, knownHostsFile contents (not its path), and the acceptAllHostKeys setting. Changing trust under the same target name rejects an existing cursor or outstanding Recording receipt. Moving an unchanged file does not; SSH credentials may rotate without changing the destination identity.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
• Upload to a deterministic hidden temporary name, verify its bytes, then publish with hardlink@openssh.com version 1. No rename or overwrite. The server must also support permission changes via SETSTAT and FSETSTAT.
  • Producer directories use mode 0700, temporary files 0600. An existing final file is accepted only if permissions, size and SHA-256 match.
  • Retries reuse a verified temporary file. Only an invalid temporary file with the known deterministic name is removed before a later retry; conflicting final content is never replaced.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The SFTP account needs to inspect the root; create producer directories; set directory and temporary-file modes; and exclusively create, write, read, hard-link and delete temporary files. It does not need listing, final-file deletion, overwrite or rename permissions. Restrict it to the configured directory where possible.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
auditlogs:
  default:
    targets:
      - name: sftp-archive
        type: sftp
        address: sftp.example.com:22
        user: audit-writer
        directory: /srv/audit/bifroest
        knownHostsFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/archive-known_hosts
        identityFiles:
          - /etc/engity/bifroest/archive-key

docs.title: WebDAV
docs.text: The WebDAV target stores sealed segments below an existing HTTPS collection. Bifröst creates one child collection per producer and writes objects as <endpoint>/<producer-id>/<sealed-segment-file>. The server must support atomic same-collection moves without overwriting existing objects.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

The unique, path-safe name of this target within the audit log.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
string = "webdav"

Selects the WebDAV target implementation. The aliases web-dav and web_dav are accepted; Bifröst writes the canonical value webdav.

docs.title: publishAttemptTimeout
docs.text:
duration = "2m"

Positive deadline for hashing, upload and read-back verification. Timeout cancels in-flight requests. If a temporary object may exist, Bifröst makes one cleanup attempt under a separate five-second deadline before retry backoff.

docs.title: endpoint
docs.text:
URL

Existing collection as an absolute HTTPS URL. No user information, query, fragment, relative components or encoded path separators. A missing trailing slash is normalized; additional CAs use SSL_CERT_FILE.

docs.title: username
docs.text:
string = ""

Optional HTTP Basic username, supporting a string template. Configure with password, or omit both for anonymous access. The rendered username must be non-empty and contain no colon or control character.

docs.title: password
docs.text:
string = ""

Optional HTTP Basic password, supporting a string template. Configure with username; both rendered values must be non-empty. Prefer an environment variable or file template over plaintext YAML.

Credential template results are not trimmed. Basic authentication forbids control characters, so password files must not contain a trailing newline.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
• Upload under a deterministic .bifroest-upload-*.tmp name, verify via GET, then publish with atomic MOVE and Overwrite: F. Final content is never overwritten.
  • Retries reuse a matching temporary object; an invalid one is deleted by its exact name and uploaded again later. An existing final object is accepted only after size and SHA-256 match; any associated temporary object is cleaned up.
  • Servers must support MKCOL, conditional PUT, GET, atomic MOVE and DELETE. Bifröst never follows redirects, lists collections or treats ETags as checksums.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The WebDAV account needs to create producer collections and create, read, move and delete temporary objects. It also needs to read final objects for conflict verification. It does not need listing or permission to overwrite/delete final segments. Restrict access to the configured collection where possible.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
auditlogs:
  default:
    targets:
      - name: webdav-archive
        type: webdav
        endpoint: https://dav.example.com/audit/
        username: '{{ env `WEBDAV_USERNAME` }}'
        password: '{{ file `/run/secrets/webdav-password` }}'

docs.title: Authorizations
docs.text:
Everything in Bifröst starts here. Firstly, a user must be authorized. Bifröst supports different types of authorizations you can choose from to adjust to your needs.

Each flow selects one authorization, either inline or from the root authorizations map. An omitted authorization uses authorizations.default only if defined.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
1. local: Local
  2. oidcAuthorizationCode: OIDC Authorization Code
  3. oidcDeviceAuth: OIDC Device Authorization
  4. simple: Simple
  5. htpasswd: Htpasswd
  6. bifroest: Bifröst delegation
  7. none: None

The resulting identity is available through Context Authentication.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Using local authorization: 
    type: local
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
  2. Using OpenID Connect Device Authorization: 
    type: oidcDeviceAuth
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
issuer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/my-great-tenant-uuid/v2.0
clientId: my-great-client-uuid
clientSecret: very-secret-secret
scopes:
   - openid
   - email
   - profile
   - offline_access
  3. Using Simple authorization: 
    type: simple
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
entries:
  - name: foo
    password: plain:bar

docs.title: Bifröst authorization
docs.text: Authorizes access delegated by another Bifröst instance. This authorization accepts only OpenSSH user certificates carrying Bifröst's signed delegation evidence. Password and keyboard-interactive authentication are always rejected.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Authorization Type = "bifroest"

Has to be set to bifroest to enable Bifröst delegation authorization.

docs.title: trustedUserCAs
docs.text:
Public Keys

OpenSSH public keys of the immediately upstream Bifröst certificate authorities. At least this property or trustedUserCAsFile is required.

docs.title: trustedUserCAsFile
docs.text:
File Path<Public Keys>

Same as trustedUserCAs, but loaded from one file when the authorization is initialized. Both properties can be used together. A configured file must exist, contain at least one valid public key, and be no larger than 4 MiB.

docs.title: audiences
docs.text:
list of strings

Accepted delegation audiences. If omitted, only the name of the local flow is accepted. An explicitly configured non-empty list replaces that default; an explicitly empty list is invalid.

docs.title: maxCertificateValidity
docs.text:
Duration = "15m"

Maximum interval from the evidence issuance time to the certificate's immutable ValidBefore boundary. Certificates exceeding this limit are rejected.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The presented credential has to satisfy all of these conditions:

  • It is a current OpenSSH user certificate signed by a configured immediately upstream CA.
  • The requesting name is one of its principals.
  • Its only critical option is bifroest-delegation@bifroest.engity.org with an empty value.
  • It contains canonical bifroest.authorization-evidence/v1 under evidence-v1@bifroest.engity.org.
  • The final evidence hop matches the certificate CA, subject key, serial, key ID, validity, target user and effective forwarding capabilities.
  • The final audience is accepted and the original authorization was authenticated.
  • The evidence is at most 4 KiB, has at most eight hops and contains no repeated subject-key fingerprint.
  • Every downstream hop can only shorten validity and remove PTY, port-forwarding or agent-forwarding capabilities.

The evidence is verified again after the client proves possession of the certificate subject key. No session is created before that proof succeeds.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: This authorization produces a context of type Authorization Bifröst.

docs.title: Entry Gateway to Target Gateway
docs.text:
Bifröst A sits between the Internet and the internal network. It authenticates alice with simple; internal Bifröst B is not Internet-accessible and trusts delegations from A.

  1. Configure A:

    /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml
    flows:
  - name: to-target
    authorization:
      type: simple
      rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
      entries:
        - name: alice
          password: plain:change-me
    environment:
      type: ssh
      address: target.example.org
      user: '{{ .session.created.remote.user }}'
      knownHostsFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/known_hosts
      certificate:
        audience: from-entry
        extensions:
          permit-pty: ""
          permit-port-forwarding: ""
          permit-agent-forwarding: ""

    Warning

    The plain password is only for this minimal example. Use a password hash or another authorization in production.

  2. Configure B with an existing local alice account: /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml

    flows:
  - name: from-entry
    authorization:
      type: bifroest
      trustedUserCAsFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/trusted-cas
    environment:
      type: local
      name: '{{ .authentication.principal }}'

  3. Run on B: 

    bifroest key export host \
  --identityFile /etc/engity/bifroest/key \
  --address target.example.org

  4. To trust B, run on A: 

    echo "<output of command executed on B>" | bifroest key import host \
  --knownHostsFile /etc/engity/bifroest/known_hosts

  5. Export A's CA before its first start: 

    bifroest key export ca \
  -c /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml \
  to-target

    Note

    bifroest key export ca creates A's missing CA without creating a .pub companion file. The same CA is used when A starts.

  6. To trust the CA of A, run on B: 

    echo "<output of command executed on A>" | bifroest key import ca \
  --trustedCAsFile /etc/engity/bifroest/trusted-cas

  7. Start B: 

    bifroest run -c /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml

  8. Start A: 

    bifroest run -c /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml

B verifies A's CA signature, the from-entry audience, the signed evidence and possession of A's persistent client-key.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Htpasswd authorization
docs.text: Authorizes a user request via credentials stored in htpasswd format.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Authorization Type = "htpasswd"

Has to be set to htpasswd to enable the htpasswd authorization.

docs.title: rememberMe
docs.text:
RememberMe = "forbidden"

Controls saved browser and SSH access.

docs.title: remoteName
docs.text:
string Authorization Request = "{{.remote.user}}"

Name used for case-sensitive lookup in the htpasswd file or inline entries. The original requesting name remains unchanged in flow requirements and audit records; see the example.

docs.title: file
docs.text:
File Path = "<os specific>"

A file where each line contains an entry in htpasswd format.

The default value varies depending on the platform Bifröst runs on:

  • Linux: /etc/engity/bifroest/htpasswd
  • Darwin: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/htpasswd
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\htpasswd

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
/etc/engity/bifroest/htpasswd
foo:$apr1$zapgfl56$eXIHR/wBYFypkUEXWdCZN/
bar:$apr1$wqkvo7c2$dqi5g.hK67jLMY4SJzrjq.

docs.title: entries
docs.text:
string

This is similar to file, but does contain the htpasswd entries directly inside the configuration.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
authorization:
  type: htpasswd
  rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
  entries: |
    foo:$apr1$zapgfl56$eXIHR/wBYFypkUEXWdCZN/
    bar:$apr1$wqkvo7c2$dqi5g.hK67jLMY4SJzrjq.

docs.title: Format
docs.text: htpasswd is a format created for Apache HTTP Server to enable an easy way to configure Basic Authentication for web servers. Nowadays, it is used in more web server projects than just the Apache HTTP Server and also in other project types like Bifröst. The reason: There is a huge toolset available to create those files.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
1. Apache HTTP Server command line tool which can be easily installed on many systems such as:
    • Ubuntu: 
      sudo apt-get install apache2-utils -y
    • Fedora/RedHat: 
      sudo apt install apache2-utils -y
  2. Helm for Kubernetes function
  3. Ansible module
  4. Terraform/OpenTofu plugin
  5. ...

docs.title: Context
docs.text: This authorization will produce a context of type Authorization Htpasswd.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Using dedicated file from default location: 
    type: htpasswd
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
  2. Using dedicated file from custom location: 
    type: htpasswd
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
file: /etc/foo/bar
  3. Using embedded entries: 
    type: htpasswd
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
entries: |
  foo:$apr1$zapgfl56$eXIHR/wBYFypkUEXWdCZN/
  bar:$apr1$wqkvo7c2$dqi5g.hK67jLMY4SJzrjq.

docs.title: Login name with an SSH suffix
docs.text:
Authenticate SSH login foo@bar against htpasswd entry foo, while keeping HTTP login names unchanged:

type: htpasswd
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
file: /etc/engity/bifroest/htpasswd
remoteName: >
  {{- if eq .connection.transport "ssh" -}}
    {{- regexReplaceAll "@[^@]+$" .remote.user "" -}}
  {{- else -}}
    {{- .remote.user -}}
  {{- end -}}

Flow requirements still match the original name: use requirement.ssh.includedRequestingName: '@bar$' for this suffix and, for example, requirement.http.includedSlug: '^docker$' for the browser link. Connect with ssh -l 'foo@bar' bifroest.example.org, or open /#docker and enter foo. Sharing credentials across flows does not merge their sessions.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Local authorization
docs.text:
Authorizes a user request via the local user database of the host on which Bifröst is running.

Note

On Linux, this authorization requires Bifröst to run with root permissions. On Windows, the default authorizedKeys path uses .user.homeDir, which requires LocalSystem to resolve the user's profile via S4U. For a custom path without .user.homeDir, Bifröst only needs permission to read the file. The Windows local environment also requires LocalSystem to start processes as the local account.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Authorization Type = "local"

Has to be set to local to enable the local authorization.

docs.title: rememberMe
docs.text:
RememberMe = "forbidden"

Controls saved browser and SSH access. Resumption requires key-possession proof, the same account name and UID/SID, and current account and access checks. Missing required checks deny resumption; no password is saved or replayed. Registered SSH keys need not appear in authorized_keys. Windows requires LocalSystem and local SAM accounts; see Compatibility.

Warning

Saved access skips repeated password/MFA authentication. With PAM, the account stack must enforce the required restrictions; auth is not repeated.

docs.title: remoteName
docs.text:
string Authorization Request = "{{.remote.user}}"

Account name used for native lookup and credential checks. The original requesting name remains unchanged in flow requirements and audit records. Mapping creates no account and grants no OS rights; see the example.

docs.title: trustedUserCAs
docs.text:
Public Keys

OpenSSH public keys of certificate authorities that may sign user certificates for existing local users. The resolved remoteName must be included in the certificate's principals; by default this is the requesting name.

docs.title: trustedUserCAsFile
docs.text:
File Path<Public Keys>

Same as trustedUserCAs, but loaded from one file when the authorization is initialized. Both properties can be used together. A configured file must exist, contain at least one valid public key, and be no larger than 4 MiB.

docs.title: authorizedKeys
docs.text:
[]File Path<Authorized Keys> Authorization Request = 

["{{.user.homeDir}}/.ssh/authorized_keys"]

Contains files with the format of classic authorized keys, in which Bifröst will look for SSH Public Keys.

The request's .connection and the selected native .user are available; .remote.user remains the original requesting name.

An entry with the cert-authority option treats its key as a user certificate authority for that local user. The optional principals="..." option restricts it further. An empty authorizedKeys list does not disable certificate authentication through trustedUserCAs or trustedUserCAsFile.

User certificates must be current, signed by the selected CA, have the resolved remoteName as a principal, and contain no critical options. Missing permit-pty, permit-port-forwarding, or permit-agent-forwarding certificate extensions disable the corresponding capability. Authorized-key options can only restrict these capabilities further.

docs.title: password
docs.text:
Password

See below.

docs.title: pamService
docs.text:
string = "<os and edition specific>"

If set to a non-empty value, this PAM service will be directly used during the authorization process instead of /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow.

Fresh PAM logins must pass authentication and account checks. Account denial, a required password change or an account-phase prompt rejects login; Bifröst does not change passwords or open a PAM session. The direct peer is supplied as PAM_RHOST.

On macOS this property must be non-empty. For supported platforms and editions, see Compatibility.

docs.title: Default settings
docs.text: linux/extended darwin/generic anything else sshd sshd empty

docs.title: Password
docs.text:
• On Linux, passwords are validated via /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow when pamService is empty, or via PAM when it is set.
  • On macOS, a non-empty PAM service is required; there is no local password-repository fallback.
  • On Windows, password and keyboard-interactive authentication validate the password of an existing local SAM account. Windows account restrictions (such as disabled accounts or denied network logon) still apply. Domain and Microsoft Entra accounts are not supported by local authorization.

docs.title: allowed
docs.text:
bool Context Password Authorization Request = true

If true, the user is allowed to use passwords via classic password authentication.

docs.title: interactiveAllowed
docs.text:
bool Context Interactive Authorization Request = true

If true, the user is allowed to use passwords via interactive authentication.

docs.title: emptyAllowed
docs.text:
bool Context * Authorization Request = false

If true, the user is allowed to use empty passwords.

Danger

Allowing empty passwords is not recommended.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: This authorization will produce a context of type Authorization Local.

docs.title: Using OpenSSH Certificates
docs.text:
type: local
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
trustedUserCAsFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/trusted-user-cas
authorizedKeys:
  - "{{.user.homeDir}}/.ssh/authorized_keys"

docs.title: Using Local accounts
docs.text:
flows:
  - name: local
    authorization:
      type: local
      rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
    environment:
      type: local
      name: '{{ .authorization.user.name }}'
      uid: '{{ .authorization.user.uid }}'

docs.title: RememberMe with PAM
docs.text:
Use an existing PAM service whose account stack enforces the required access restrictions:

type: local
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
pamService: bifroest

docs.title: Login name with an SSH suffix
docs.text:
Authenticate SSH login foo@bar as the existing account foo, while keeping HTTP login names unchanged:

type: local
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
remoteName: >
  {{- if eq .connection.transport "ssh" -}}
    {{- regexReplaceAll "@[^@]+$" .remote.user "" -}}
  {{- else -}}
    {{- .remote.user -}}
  {{- end -}}

Flow requirements still match the original name: use requirement.ssh.includedRequestingName: '@bar$' for this suffix and, for example, requirement.http.includedSlug: '^docker$' for the browser link. Connect with ssh -l 'foo@bar' bifroest.example.org, or open /#docker and enter foo.

docs.title: None authorization
docs.text:
Always authorizes a user regardless of the password used, even if no password or SSH key is provided.

Danger

This authorization enables a high security risk.

There are only very rare cases where this makes sense. Only in cases like creating a demo server does it make sense to use it. See our demonstration/training use case as a ligable example

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: This authorization will produce a context of type Authorization Simple.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: type: none

docs.title: Compatibility

docs.title: Simple authorization
docs.text: Authorizes a user request via stored credentials.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Authorization Type = "simple"

Has to be set to simple to enable simple authorization.

docs.title: rememberMe
docs.text:
RememberMe = "forbidden"

Controls saved browser and SSH access. Current entry and key restrictions still apply.

docs.title: remoteName
docs.text:
string Authorization Request = "{{.remote.user}}"

Name used to select an entry before checking credentials. The original requesting name remains unchanged in flow requirements and audit records; see the example.

docs.title: trustedUserCAs
docs.text:
Public Keys

OpenSSH public keys of certificate authorities that may sign user certificates for every entry in this authorization. The resolved remoteName must be included in the certificate's principals; without a custom mapping this is the requested SSH username.

docs.title: trustedUserCAsFile
docs.text:
File Path<Public Keys>

Same as trustedUserCAs, but loaded from one file when the authorization is initialized. Both properties can be used together. A configured file must exist, contain at least one valid public key, and be no larger than 4 MiB.

docs.title: entries
docs.text:
[]Entry

Each entry will be inspected to check if a remote user should be authorized.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
One of the following properties normally has to match in combination with name:

  • authorizedKeys
  • authorizedKeysFile
  • password
  • passwordFile

An entry containing only name can additionally be authenticated by a user certificate signed by trustedUserCAs or trustedUserCAsFile.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

Account name matched against the resolved remoteName, using the existing case-insensitive simple-entry lookup.

Like: ssh <name>@my-great-domain.tld to match this entry.

docs.title: authorizedKeys
docs.text:
Authorized Keys

Contains SSH Public Keys in the format of classic authorized keys.

An entry with the cert-authority option treats its key as a user certificate authority for this simple entry. The optional principals="..." option restricts it further.

docs.title: authorizedKeysFile
docs.text:
File Path<Authorized Keys>

Similar to authorizedKeys, but in a dedicated file.

docs.title: password
docs.text:
Password

Password (if user uses interactive or password authentication method) to be evaluated against.

docs.title: passwordFile
docs.text:
File Path<Password>

Same as password, but is receiving the value from this file.

If both properties are defined and have values, password will be used.

docs.title: createPasswordFileIfAbsentOfType
docs.text:
Password Type

If this property is provided and passwordFile is defined, but does not exist, the file will be generated with a random password of this type.

The result will be printed into the startup logs of Bifröst.

This feature usually only makes sense for cases where you want to create dummy configurations of Bifröst to demonstrate some functionality, like we're utilizing it in our demonstration configurations: contrib/configurations/simple-inside-docker.yaml.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: This authorization will produce a context of type Authorization Simple.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Using plain password: 
    type: simple
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
entries:
  - name: foo
    password: plain:bar
  2. Using authorized keys: ```yaml type: simple rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault entries:
    • name: foo authorizedKeys: | ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIC80lm5FQbbyRUut6RwZJRbxTLO3W4f08ITDi9fA3+jx foo@foo.tld ```
  3. Using an OpenSSH user certificate authority: 
    type: simple
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
trustedUserCAs: |
  ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIExampleOrganizationCA
entries:
  - name: foo

User certificates must be current, signed by the selected CA, have the resolved remoteName as a principal, and contain no critical options. Missing permit-pty, permit-port-forwarding, or permit-agent-forwarding certificate extensions disable the corresponding capability. Authorized-key options can only restrict these capabilities further.

docs.title: Login name with an SSH suffix
docs.text:
Authenticate SSH login foo@bar against entry foo, while keeping HTTP login names unchanged:

type: simple
rememberMe: allowedAndEnabledByDefault
remoteName: >
  {{- if eq .connection.transport "ssh" -}}
    {{- regexReplaceAll "@[^@]+$" .remote.user "" -}}
  {{- else -}}
    {{- .remote.user -}}
  {{- end -}}
entries:
  - name: foo
    passwordFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/passwords/foo

Flow requirements still match the original name: use requirement.ssh.includedRequestingName: '@bar$' for this suffix and, for example, requirement.http.includedSlug: '^docker$' for the browser link. Connect with ssh -l 'foo@bar' bifroest.example.org, or open /#docker and enter foo. Sharing credentials across flows does not merge their sessions.

docs.title: OpenID Connect (OIDC) authorization
docs.text: Authenticates users through an external identity provider (IdP). MFA and passkeys remain with the IdP; Bifröst's environment determines where the session runs.

docs.title: Choose a flow
docs.text:
Authorization Code Device Authorization Bifröst HTTP connection Required, also for SSH Not required for SSH User experience Familiar browser redirect; often simpler SSO Separate verification page and code; potentially less convenient IdP compatibility Broad OIDC support Requires explicit Device Authorization support Login protection PKCE S256, browser binding and explicit SSH approval Device-code verification and approval at the IdP

Authorization Code can offer security advantages with a suitable setup; neither flow is automatically safer. WebUI access requires HTTPS with either flow.

For a complete setup, see the OIDC login guide.

docs.title: Authorization Code
docs.text:
Enable the HTTP connection and register its /login/callback URL at the IdP.

type: oidcAuthorizationCode
issuer: https://idp.example.org/realms/company
clientId: bifroest
clientSecret: YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET
scopes: [ openid, profile, offline_access ]

Authorization Code properties and examples

docs.title: Device Authorization
docs.text:
Enable Device Authorization for the IdP client. SSH does not need a Bifröst HTTP listener.

type: oidcDeviceAuth
issuer: https://idp.example.org/realms/company
clientId: bifroest
clientSecret: YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET
scopes: [ openid, profile, offline_access ]

Device Authorization properties and examples

Both examples use the default refresh checks. The IdP must issue a refresh token; use the scopes and client settings required by your provider.

docs.title: OIDC Authorization Code
docs.text: Authenticates through an IdP browser redirect with PKCE S256. Compared with Device Authorization, this often provides simpler SSO and broader IdP compatibility. PKCE and browser binding can offer security advantages, depending on the setup.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Enable the HTTP connection, including for SSH logins.
  • Register a confidential web client at the IdP with Authorization Code and PKCE S256 enabled.
  • Register https://<domain>/login/callback as the exact callback URL; see domain.

Browser sign-in for SSH

You can use the browser just to confirm an SSH login, without offering access through the WebUI. Users confirm their login in the browser, then return to their SSH client to work.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
• SSH: Open your own login link; it redirects to the IdP automatically. After signing in, select your SSH client's two-character code from three choices, or decline. A wrong choice or decline aborts the login.
  • WebUI: Choose OIDC. Login opens in a separate tab, without code selection; use the fallback link if popups are blocked. The tab closes automatically when possible, keeping the original application and its sessions intact.

The WebUI login tab or fallback link must stay in the initiating browser profile. A temporary Secure, HttpOnly, host-only cookie binds the original attempt before any IdP redirect; a forwarded link cannot authenticate a different browser's attempt. This cookie is required even without RememberMe and never grants workload access on its own. SSH may still use a browser on another device with its explicit code confirmation.

Never approve someone else's SSH login link. Pending browser logins are memory-only; a Bifröst restart or loss of the initiating WebUI tab requires a new login.

Browser success means the original login passed Bifröst's access, session and required audit checks, not just the IdP login. Code selection is an active confirmation, not MFA: guessing succeeds with probability 1/3 and it cannot prevent deliberate phishing. Configure MFA or passkeys at the IdP.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Authorization Type = "oidcAuthorizationCode"

Set to oidcAuthorizationCode.

docs.title: ssh
docs.text:
SSH

Settings for SSH clients; ignored by the WebUI.

docs.title: rememberMe
docs.text:
RememberMe = "forbidden"

Controls saved browser and SSH access. Current session and refresh checks still apply.

docs.title: issuer
docs.text:
URL Core

Issuer URL supplied by the IdP, for example https://idp.example.org/realms/company.

The issuer and discovered authorization/token endpoints must use HTTPS. For a private CA, configure SSL_CERT_FILE in the Bifröst service environment.

docs.title: clientId
docs.text:
string Core

Client ID registered at the IdP.

docs.title: clientSecret
docs.text:
string Core

Secret for that client. Keep it in protected configuration, not source control.

Token-endpoint method Selection client_secret_basic Preferred; also used when metadata omits authentication methods client_secret_post Used when explicitly advertised and Basic is unavailable

Cross-origin redirects from the token endpoint are not followed.

docs.title: scopes
docs.text:
[]string Core = ["openid", "profile", "email"]

Scopes requested from the IdP. Must include openid.

Default refresh checks require a refresh token. Add your provider's required scope and client settings, often offline_access; Bifröst does not add it automatically.

docs.title: domain
docs.text:
Host = "<first http.domains entry>"

Selects one of the configured http.domains. Omit the scheme, port and path.

The callback is https://<domain>/login/callback. A non-standard port comes from the first HTTP listener. Register this exact URL at the IdP; an ephemeral listener port (:0) is not supported.

docs.title: loginTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "2m"

Maximum time for the login, including browser approval. Must be greater than zero and at most 10m. SSH also applies its remaining handshakeTimeout.

The same deadline covers final target validation and required audit recording. A delayed WebUI claim or audit completion cannot grant access after expiration.

docs.title: retrieveIdToken
docs.text:
bool = true

Exposes verified ID-token claims as .authorization.idToken.

The ID token is always verified, even when this setting is false.

docs.title: retrieveUserInfo
docs.text:
bool = false

Retrieves .authorization.userInfo. Its subject must match the authenticated identity.

docs.title: forceDisposeSessionOn
docs.text:
string = "lostAccess"

Controls session disposal after OIDC access is lost.

Value Behavior lostAccess Requires a refresh token. Disposes the session when the grant is rejected or verification exceeds maxUnverifiedFor. never Does not dispose the session because of failed refresh checks.

docs.title: refreshToken
docs.text:
Refresh Token

Settings for refresh checks. A refresh token is required when either proactive refresh or lostAccess is enabled.

docs.title: loginMessage
docs.text:
string = ""

Optional template for the SSH login instruction; ignored by the WebUI. An empty value uses the standard one-sentence instruction. .url is the Bifröst login link, .code the two-character comparison code and .codeRequired is true.

Example
ssh:
  loginMessage: 'Sign in with code "{{ .code }}": {{ .url }}'

docs.title: mode
docs.text:
string = "proactive"

Value Behavior proactive Refreshes the session's grant before access-token expiry. never Disables proactive refresh; lostAccess checks remain active.

To disable refresh checks entirely, set both forceDisposeSessionOn and refreshToken.mode to never.

docs.title: atLifetimePercent
docs.text:
integer = 70

Percentage of access-token lifetime at which to refresh, from 1 through 99.

docs.title: fallbackEvery
docs.text:
Duration = "15m"

Positive interval between refresh attempts when token lifetime is unavailable.

docs.title: maxUnverifiedFor
docs.text:
Duration = "30m"

Maximum time without successful verification during an IdP outage. Must be positive. With lostAccess, exceeding this deadline disposes the session.

docs.title: Access and logout
docs.text:
• Refresh checks the grant, not necessarily current user/group claims or loginAllowed.
  • Newly returned ID tokens must retain the session's issuer and subject. Unverifiable rotated credentials remain unusable until verified.
  • Without a new ID token, existing claims are usable only until their token expires.
  • Local session disposal does not revoke tokens at the IdP. User disablement is not guaranteed to invalidate existing refresh grants.

See off-boarding deadlines for connection and session lifetime limits.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Provides an Authorization OIDC context.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Use the default refresh policy and select a configured HTTP domain:

type: oidcAuthorizationCode
issuer: https://idp.example.org/realms/company
clientId: bifroest
clientSecret: YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET
scopes: [ openid, profile, offline_access ]
domain: gateway.example.org
loginTimeout: 2m

For a complete SSH and WebUI configuration, see the OIDC login guide.

Changing an existing flow's grant requires a new login; it does not migrate saved access.

docs.title: OIDC Device Authorization
docs.text:
The SSH client or WebUI displays an IdP verification link and code. Users complete the login on the IdP's verification page.

Compared with Authorization Code, the separate verification step can be less convenient. Not every IdP supports this grant; check the provider and client settings.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Enable Device Authorization for the IdP client. A Device Authorization endpoint is required.
  • Register a client ID and secret with the IdP.
  • SSH: No Bifröst HTTP connection or callback URL is required.
  • WebUI: Enable the HTTP connection and choose Interactive to sign in.

Follow the IdP's verification instructions. Unlike Authorization Code, this flow has no separate Bifröst SSH approval page.

The WebUI shows this step in its login dialog and immediately tries to copy the code. Open the verification page with the button or Enter; if copying is blocked, enter the displayed code manually. Providers offering a complete verification URL do not require manual code entry. Ordinary keyboard-interactive prompts still use the authentication terminal.

docs.title: Command line interface (CLI)
docs.text: Use bifroest to run the server, inspect its state, manage SSH keys, and work with signed audit journals and session recordings.

docs.title: Find a command
docs.text:
Command Purpose serve Run the Bifröst server. test Run offline configuration tests and write text, JSON or JUnit results. flow List configured flows and inspect their settings. session Inspect sessions; remotely disconnect or dispose of them. metrics Query operational metric snapshots through management SSH. audit Inspect audit logs and events; verify, export or merge journals. recording Find, inspect, verify, export and play session recordings. key Generate keys and exchange SSH trust material. id Convert UUID and Base58 representations locally. service Install and control the Windows service or macOS LaunchDaemon. version Show version and build information.

Each executable command's reference documents its syntax, arguments, flags, output, examples and availability.

docs.title: Choose how to call it
docs.text:
• On the Bifröst host: bifroest session ls reads the configured local storage.
  • From an administrator's workstation: bifroest @bifroest-admin session ls uses the integrated SSH client.
  • Through a standard SSH client: ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'session ls' runs a command in the authorized management flow.
  • With copied evidence: bifroest recording verify --expectedProducerId PRODUCER_ID session.bcast verifies a local artifact.

Read Invocation and data sources for configuration paths and the difference between an execution mode and a file input. Remote access documents SSH targets, authentication and client settings.

docs.title: General flags
docs.text:
The executable's general flags are:

  • --help
  • --log.level
  • --log.format
  • --log.colorMode

Command-specific flags such as --format, --configuration and --output are documented on the commands that accept them. Direct SSH uses the server's log settings.

For more background, see Output and errors and Trust and verification.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
For a complete setup followed by actual commands, choose an end-to-end guide:

  • Manage a Bifröst host remotely.
  • Test a configuration before deployment.
  • Record, find and replay a session.
  • Verify encrypted evidence on a workstation.

For help with an installed version, use bifroest --help or bifroest recording play --help.

docs.title: bifroest --help
docs.text: Shows command-line help for Bifröst or for a selected command path.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest [<command>...] --help bifroest @target <command>... --help

docs.title: command
docs.text: command is an optional sequence such as audit verify or key export public. Without it, Bifröst shows the root help.

docs.title: --help
docs.text:
-hbool = false

Shows help without running the selected command. For a remote target, help describes the commands and flags available to the integrated management client and does not open an SSH connection. See general flags.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
bifroest --help
bifroest audit verify --help
bifroest @bifroest-admin recording play --help

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text: Remote access uses the same command names as the local CLI. For a complete server and client configuration, follow Manage a Bifröst host remotely. The management environment reference describes the server-side properties.

docs.title: Select a target
docs.text:
The integrated client accepts @[USER@]HOST[:PORT] as the first argument:

bifroest @bifroest-admin session ls
bifroest @management@bifroest.example.org flow ls --format=json
bifroest @[::1]:2222 audit ls
bifroest @bifroest-admin metrics show bifroest_connections_active

@target selects remote execution for the entire command. Unsupported commands and flags fail instead of falling back to local execution. A target in a later position is rejected. Management commands do not support @file argument expansion.

docs.title: SSH client and trust
docs.text:
The client is integrated into the Bifröst binary; it needs no separate ssh executable. It reads SSH host aliases and the settings HostName, User, Port, IdentityFile, IdentityAgent and UserKnownHostsFile. A trusted host key must already be present in known_hosts; unknown keys are not automatically accepted.

UserKnownHostsFile selects one local file; the client default is ~/.ssh/known_hosts. Quote paths containing spaces in the SSH configuration, for example UserKnownHostsFile "C:/Users/Alice Example/.ssh/known_hosts" on Windows. Use a single trust file for the integrated client rather than a list of files in this setting.

Unsupported proxy directives such as ProxyJump and ProxyCommand fail explicitly. Other complex OpenSSH configurations may need to be simplified for this client.

docs.title: Isolated client configuration
docs.text:
The integrated parser supports a subset of OpenSSH configuration syntax. In particular, Match final is not interpreted; configurations containing it fail explicitly. To use the integrated client on a host whose normal SSH configuration needs unsupported rules, select a separate file with --sshConfig PATH (short option -F):

Administrator workstation: bifroest-ssh.conf
IgnoreUnknown X-*

Host bifroest-admin
    HostName bifroest.example.org
    User management
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/bifroest-management
    UserKnownHostsFile ~/.ssh/known_hosts
Administrator workstation
bifroest @bifroest-admin --sshConfig ./bifroest-ssh.conf session ls
bifroest @bifroest-admin -F ./bifroest-ssh.conf audit ls

The selected file replaces the normal user and system SSH configuration. Its explicit Include directives are still processed. Login identities, host trust and the X-* artifact settings below are all taken from this same source. A missing or invalid selected file causes an error; it never falls back to another configuration, ignores an unsupported Match rule, or accepts an unknown host key. These options belong to the integrated client and are not available through direct management SSH.

docs.title: Authentication agents
docs.text:
On Unix-like systems, agent authentication uses SSH_AUTH_SOCK. On Windows, the client tries the OpenSSH agent named pipe for at most five seconds, then Pageant's native interface. Canceling the command also closes an OpenSSH-agent connection waiting for a response.

When both Windows agents are running, set X-SSHAgent pageant in the matching Host block to select Pageant. It cannot be combined with IdentityAgent. Modern Pageant versions can also expose an OpenSSH-compatible named pipe through IdentityAgent.

The agent authenticates the SSH connection. Audit and Recording decryption use separate local private-key files. In a container, provide the agent socket or login identity, SSH configuration and trusted host keys as needed.

docs.title: Authentication prompts
docs.text:
Passphrases for encrypted SSH identities, passwords and keyboard-interactive answers are read from the invoking terminal. Prompts and visible answers are written to stderr; secret answers are hidden. Each answer is limited to 64 KiB; exceeding that limit causes an explicit error rather than truncation. Press Ctrl+C to cancel a prompt without pressing Enter. The original terminal settings are restored when the prompt finishes or is canceled.

For non-interactive commands, provide an SSH agent or a usable identity file. The client does not read passwords from a pipe or from command output.

docs.title: Artifact settings
docs.text:
The integrated client recognizes these additional SSH settings:

Setting Meaning X-ExpectedProducerId Independently trusted signing producer ID for downloaded evidence. X-AuditPrivateKey Local private-key file for encrypted audit event fields. X-RecordingPrivateKey Local private-key file for encrypted Recordings. X-SSHAgent Explicit pageant selection for SSH login.

Use IgnoreUnknown X-* when sharing this configuration with OpenSSH. Artifact commands can override producer trust with --expectedProducerId and decryption keys with --decryptionIdentityFile. A server-supplied or artifact-embedded producer ID is not an independent trust anchor; see Trust and verification.

docs.title: Direct SSH
docs.text:
A standard SSH client can execute a command in the authorized management flow:

ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'session ls'
ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'recording show default RECORDING_UUID'

The flow does not start a shell or provide PTY, SFTP or forwarding access. Commands use the service's loaded configuration. Each command page states whether direct SSH is supported and which flags differ from the integrated client.

Direct SSH cannot use decryption keys stored on a separate workstation. It can verify signed outer metadata and clear content on the server. Use the integrated client for local decryption of downloaded evidence.

docs.title: Permissions and downloads
docs.text:
Operation Management right Session, flow, auditlog and Recording metadata Corresponding sessions.read, flows.read, auditlogs.read or recordings.read metrics show metrics.read session disconnect / session dispose sessions.disconnect / sessions.dispose Public audit events and direct-SSH redacted export/merge auditlogs.events Client-side audit verify/export/merge or sensitive audit events auditlogs.download for the original journal Client-side recording verify/export/play recordings.download for the original Recording Direct-SSH verification without content export auditlogs.verify / recordings.verify Direct-SSH sensitive audit output auditlogs.events and auditlogs.download Direct-SSH Recording export/play recordings.download Public key export public/ca/host keys.read

These are rights in the authorized flow's access tree, not client-granted privileges. --with-sensitive controls disclosure; it does not grant server permissions. flows.credentials additionally permits unredacted flow show output. Verification and export performed locally after an authorized original download do not grant additional server operations.

The default access object includes session control but excludes credentials and downloads. An explicit object grants only its listed rights. Session actions apply across flows and do not imply session-read access. Disposal runs configured cleanup and can remove workload resources.

Public key exports select configured server identities and write their output on the CLI machine. See Export server public keys remotely for a complete configuration. key generate and key import remain local-only; server trust files are maintained through normal configuration management.

Remote artifact commands download the selected audit journal or original Recording and verify it on the CLI machine. Private decryption keys stay there. An audit download is limited to 1 GiB of journal files; Recording downloads are subject to the Recording size limits. A live journal that changes during the download can cause an error and require a retry.

docs.title: Configure a workstation alias
docs.text:
1. Configure an authorized management flow and provision the server's host key through a trusted channel.

  2. Add the host to the workstation's SSH configuration:

    ~/.ssh/config
    IgnoreUnknown X-*

Host bifroest-admin
    HostName bifroest.example.org
    User management
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/bifroest-management
    UserKnownHostsFile ~/.ssh/known_hosts

  3. Query server state:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin session ls
bifroest @bifroest-admin audit ls --format=json

For producer-ID pinning and decryption-key configuration, follow Verify encrypted evidence on a workstation.

docs.title: Output and errors
docs.text: Command results are written to stdout. Logs and error messages are written to stderr. Logging flags such as --log.format do not select the result format.

docs.title: Result formats
docs.text:
Unless a command page states otherwise, commands that accept --format support these values:
