Value Result table Human-readable tables, details or status lines; the default. json A JSON result object or array. yaml A YAML result object or sequence. cbor A CBOR result object or array.

The command page documents the result's content. Lists use tables, details use key/value output, verification prints its scope, and audit producer-id prints the ID in the default format.

metrics show accepts only table (default), json and openmetrics.

Some commands have a fixed output:

Command Output audit export and audit merge JSON Lines: one event with its metadata per line. recording inspect One JSON inspection object. recording export Signed asciicast v3 content. recording play Replayed terminal output. Key export commands OpenSSH public-key, CA or known_hosts material.

These commands do not accept --format. --output, where supported, chooses a destination file rather than a serialization format.

docs.title: Sensitive output
docs.text:
Audit event queries and JSONL exports are redacted by default. --with-sensitive includes confidential fields; encrypted journals additionally need the matching decryption key. A Recording export or playback always contains the complete captured terminal content and requires --with-sensitive.

Configuration detail commands redact arbitrary strings. The management right flows.credentials applies to flow show, not to all settings queries. See the relevant command page and Trust and verification.

docs.title: Completion and errors
docs.text:
A failed command returns a nonzero exit status. Check that status before accepting output as complete.

Local configuration-loading errors include the file path and parser or validation details, with line and column information where available. Known credential fields (passwords and password files, client credentials, remote storage credentials, registry credentials and environment variables) replace value-bearing errors with a field-specific ***redacted*** diagnostic. Other fields retain their detailed errors: a secret accidentally placed in an unrelated field is not automatically recognized. Treat captured stderr and logs as potentially sensitive.

  • recording ls streams each selected entry after verifying it. A later failure leaves partial output; JSON or CBOR can remain unfinished. Accept the page as complete only when the command succeeds.
  • Audit export and merge verify all selected sources before publishing output. A corrupt source produces no event output and leaves an existing destination file unchanged.
  • Recording export verifies before publishing content. An existing destination is replaced only with a complete, verified export. Playback verifies its input before replaying terminal events.

Remote failures are reported on stderr where possible. A local output failure, cancellation or lost connection aborts the operation. The repository can change between listing pages; see recording ls.

The integrated client also forwards server diagnostics to local stderr when a command succeeds, for example when session inspection skips a corrupt entry. It retains at most the first 16 KiB and marks truncated diagnostics. If the local diagnostic output fails, the command returns an error.

docs.title: Save a structured session listing
docs.text:
1. Configure the remote alias as described in Remote access.

  2. Capture the result and accept it only when the command succeeds:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin session ls --format=json > sessions.json

    Handle the exit status in the calling script. The shell opens sessions.json before Bifröst starts; choose a separate output location. See protected destinations.

docs.title: bifroest serve
docs.text:
Starts Bifröst with the selected configuration and runs until the process receives a termination signal. On Windows, the command also acts as the service entry point when launched by the Service Control Manager.

bifroest serve

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
bifroest serve [flags]

run is an alias of serve.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path<Configuration> = "<os specific>"

Configuration file to load.

The default depends on the platform:

  • Linux: /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml
  • macOS: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/configuration.yaml
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\configuration.yaml

docs.title: --serviceName
docs.text:
string = "engity-bifroest"

Windows only. Name registered with SCM; supplied by service install.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Logs are written to stderr. Startup failure returns a nonzero exit status. An interrupt requests shutdown.

docs.title: Start a configured server
docs.text:
1. Prepare a valid host configuration, or the two-flow configuration from the management guide.

  2. Run Bifröst as the intended service user with the required host permissions:

    bifroest serve --configuration /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml

    For an installed system service, use its service manager instead of starting a second process on the same address and repositories.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

For installation and control through the platform service manager, see service.

docs.title: bifroest test
docs.text:
Run offline tests against YAML configuration without starting the service, authenticating credentials or creating target resources. The current testing scope is limited; selected is not a complete access grant.

To write a suite, start with Test a configuration. The testing reference describes the Lua API and supported policy behavior separately from this command's invocation.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest test [flags] <suites>...

docs.title: suites
docs.text:
One or more suite files or directories. Directories are searched recursively for *_bftest.lua. File/directory symlinks are followed, including outside the starting directory; physical inputs are deduplicated and directory cycles terminate. Sources execute in sorted canonical-path order. --suite is not a flag.

A valid matching Lua file that registers no suite produces a warning on stderr; syntax/runtime/resource failures are errors, even when filters select no tests.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general executable flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Fallback YAML file for suites without configuration; relative to the invocation directory. Otherwise the platform configuration path is used. This does not override suite YAML. See configuration selection.

docs.title: --includes
docs.text:
string

Repeatable Go regular expression matched against suite.name/test.name. Includes are OR-combined; without includes, all names match. Matching is by substring unless anchored. Invalid expressions and an empty final selection return 2. Filters choose tests, not which candidate source files are loaded.

docs.title: --excludes
docs.text:
string

Repeatable name filter using the same syntax. Any matching exclusion wins over includes. Name exclusions are not platform-skipped outcomes.

docs.title: --verbose
docs.text:
-vbool = false

Show every package, suite and test, including passing and platform-skipped cases. Without it, show failures/errors and per-directory summaries.

docs.title: --json
docs.text:
File Path

Write the JSON report, replacing an existing regular report and creating missing parent directories.

docs.title: --junit
docs.text:
File Path

Write the JUnit XML report, with the same replacement/parent behavior. JSON and JUnit need distinct destinations. Symlinks, nonregular destinations, reserved suite filenames and captured inputs/aliases are protected. Multiple outputs are not an atomic transaction.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Text goes to stdout; warnings and operational diagnostics go to stderr. The final RESULT counts tests, not assertions. Physical source directories form packages, including for single-file runs. See reports for package ordering, verbose output, timings and skip/error representation.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 At least one test selected; all selected tests passed without loading errors. 1 At least one assertion failed. 2 No tests found/selected, invalid input/regex, unsupported or unmodeled dependency, policy/runtime/resource/report failure.

Code 2 takes precedence over 1. A report failure retains its destination and original cause, even after text has been printed. Completed result reports do not cause a redundant generic executable error log.

docs.title: Test your configuration and publish CI reports
docs.text:
bifroest test tests \
  --configuration configuration.yaml \
  --json reports/testing.json \
  --junit reports/testing.xml

docs.title: Select cases across directories
docs.text:
bifroest test tests/team-a tests/team-b/access_bftest.lua \
  --configuration configuration.yaml \
  --includes '^ssh/' \
  --includes '^ops/' \
  --excludes '/legacy$' \
  --verbose

docs.title: Run the repository examples
docs.text:
From a checkout, with its current binary:

bifroest test pkg/test/examples --excludes '^deliberately-red-'

Without the exclusion, the deliberate failure returns 1. See the example catalogue for individual directories.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

The CLI uses its own OS/architecture/version metadata for platform selectors. There are no platform override flags. It also runs in the regular Bifröst image; see the container example.

docs.title: Invocation and data sources
docs.text:
The general command form is:

bifroest [@target] <command> [<subcommand>...] [flags] [arguments]

A remote target, when present, must be the first argument. The command's reference page lists its accepted arguments and flags. Use --flag=false to disable a boolean option whose default is true, for example bifroest service install --start=false.

Uppercase tokens in examples, such as PRODUCER_ID, SESSION_UUID and RECORDING_UUID, are placeholders to replace with values from the preceding steps.

docs.title: Syntax notation
docs.text: Command and subcommand names are literal words, for example recording show or key export host. Angle brackets identify an argument to supply, square brackets mark optional parts, and ... means that values can be repeated. Select an argument in a command's syntax to jump to its description; flags links to that command's options.

docs.title: Execution modes
docs.text:
Mode Example Configuration and state Local CLI bifroest session ls Runs on the CLI machine and reads local configuration, state or file inputs. Integrated remote client bifroest @bifroest-admin session ls Executes supported commands through the server's authorized management flow. Direct SSH ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'session ls' Runs inside the server's management flow using its loaded configuration.

Availability is specified on each executable command's page. Server startup, service installation and key bootstrap commands run locally. The remote-access reference explains SSH configuration and management permissions.

docs.title: Availability tables
docs.text:
Executable command pages show platform support in the same generic/extended notation as the binary distributions. A check means supported, a cross means unsupported, and an empty circle means that the edition is not distributed for that platform.

The invocation table separately shows whether the command supports the local CLI, the integrated @target client and direct SSH. Platform support refers to the machine running that command. For example, the local service commands are available in the macOS and Windows binaries, with no Linux support or remote invocation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Commands that select configured local state accept --configuration PATH (alias -c) where documented. Without it, they load the platform default:

Platform Default configuration Linux /etc/engity/bifroest/configuration.yaml macOS /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/configuration.yaml Windows C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\configuration.yaml

The local CLI needs filesystem permission to read the selected configuration, state and relevant keys. Local session inspection supports filesystem repositories. Through management, the service reads its active session repository.

session disconnect and session dispose are management-only operations that change server state. They are not available against local filesystem storage.

metrics show also requires management access: it queries the running instance, not local storage or a Prometheus server.

--configuration cannot be combined with @target. Direct SSH commands use the running service's configuration and do not accept a replacement configuration file.

docs.title: Repositories and copied evidence
docs.text:
The execution mode and the input source are separate choices:

  • An auditlog name selects a repository from configuration, for example bifroest audit verify default.
  • An audit --source directory selects a complete copied journal, including its signed head and all required segments.
  • A Recording file argument selects a copied .bcast, .becast or signed .cast file, where supported.

Offline file inputs need an independently trusted producer ID; they do not need the server's signing private key or a local server configuration. They are local to the CLI machine and cannot be combined with @target. Remote commands select an auditlog name and, for Recordings, a Recording ID.

For downloaded evidence, output files and decryption-key paths belong to the CLI machine. Remote metadata is queried on the server; remote artifact verification, export and playback download signed originals and verify them on the client. See Trust and verification.

docs.title: General flags
docs.text: These flags configure the executable in local and @target mode; options marked remote-only require a leading target. Direct management SSH uses the server's logging configuration and does not expose the executable's logging or SSH-client flags; --help remains available.

docs.title: --help
docs.text:
-hbool = false

Shows help without executing the selected command. See Help.

docs.title: --log.level
docs.text:
Log Level = "INFO"

Minimum level for log messages.

docs.title: --log.format
docs.text:
Log Format = "text"

Format of log messages; independent of a command's result format.

docs.title: --log.colorMode
docs.text:
Log Color Mode = "auto"

Color mode for logs: auto, always or never.

docs.title: --sshConfig
docs.text:
-FFile Path

Remote-client-only SSH configuration file. It replaces the normal user and system configuration; explicit Include directives in this file remain active. Login, host trust and X-* artifact settings all use the selected file. See isolated client configuration.

docs.title: Inspect a non-default local configuration
docs.text:
1. Prepare a valid Bifröst configuration at /etc/engity/bifroest/staging.yaml.

  2. Inspect the flows selected by that file:

    bifroest flow ls --configuration /etc/engity/bifroest/staging.yaml

  3. Inspect the available options for a different execution mode:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin flow ls --help

    This prints client-side help without opening an SSH connection.

docs.title: Trust and verification
docs.text: Audit and Recording commands verify signed evidence without changing its originals or creating a missing signing identity. Their reference pages specify whether they read a configured repository, a copied file or downloaded evidence.

docs.title: Trust a producer
docs.text:
A valid signature proves cryptographic consistency. To establish who produced the evidence, the verifier needs an independently trusted signing identity.

Source Trust anchor Configured local repository Its configured signing key; an explicit expected producer ID can replace it where supported. Direct-SSH repository query The running service's signing identity. Copied or client-downloaded evidence Independently obtained --expectedProducerId, or X-ExpectedProducerId for supported remote commands.

The producer ID is a 64-hex identifier of the signing key. Obtain it from audit producer-id through an independently trusted channel and retain it separately. An ID or public key read only from the evidence is not a trust anchor. SSH host-key checking authenticates the connection and is distinct from producer trust.

recording inspect can report untrusted self-consistency explicitly. Recording export/play accept --allowUntrusted as an explicit alternative to producer trust; it cannot be combined with an expected producer ID. Normal verification requires trusted evidence.

docs.title: Outer and full verification
docs.text:
Scope What is verified outer Signed public metadata, structure and encrypted bytes; encrypted private content remains unverified. full The signed container and its decoded content, including decrypted content where applicable.

Clear journals and Recordings can be fully verified without a decryption key. Encrypted evidence needs the matching recipient private key for full verification. --require-full makes a verification command fail rather than accepting outer-only verification.

Signing, SSH-login and encryption keys have different roles. The recipient private key belongs on the verification workstation; only its public key is configured on the server. An SSH authentication agent does not decrypt evidence. Follow the encrypted-evidence guide for a complete setup.

docs.title: Key-file requirements
docs.text:
Loaded signing and decryption private keys must be regular, non-symlink files with exactly one hard link and a size of at most 1 MiB:

  • On Unix, the effective process user must own the file and group/other access must be absent.
  • On Windows, the current process-token owner must own the file, with a protected DACL whose allow entries name only that owner, OWNER RIGHTS, or SYSTEM.

Configured local commands do not regenerate a missing signing key. For supported audit commands, an explicit trusted producer ID permits verification without opening that signing private key. Recording selection by local auditlog name instead uses its configured identity; copied-file and remote selectors accept external producer trust as documented.

docs.title: Complete evidence and live reads
docs.text:
An offline audit source needs the complete journal, including <root>/<producer-id>/head.cbor, all required sealed segments and any active segment. Remote delivery targets store sealed segments rather than a complete journal; a single delivered segment is not an audit CLI source. Recordings are independently sealed .bcast or .becast originals.

Audit commands can run while the service keeps writing. Events added during the operation may be absent from the result. When several journals are read, their results need not represent the same instant. A journal that changes during a read can cause an error and require a retry. Detecting rollback or deletion of recent history needs an independently retained record of the expected latest state in addition to signature verification.

Verification of large journals may require temporary disk space. Use a private temporary location outside the source repositories. An unsuitable or unwritable temporary location causes verification to fail. Treat files left after a forcibly interrupted verification as sensitive and remove them only after confirming that the operation has ended.

docs.title: Protected destinations
docs.text:
Export files must be outside managed journal, Recording and filesystem session-storage directories. Destination checks protect the loaded configuration, signing identities, referenced encryption public keys, SFTP known-hosts files and SFTP identities, as well as supplied decryption identities. They cover active configured entries beyond the selected sources, including their Recording repositories, and apply with --force.

Local metadata and configured evidence-output commands also protect statically configured SSH host keys and SSH-flow login/certificate/CA identities, together with known-hosts files, authorized-keys files and trusted user-CA files. The checks inspect file identities without loading or generating keys. Session-dependent file templates are not evaluated by metadata queries and cannot supply additional protected paths for that query.

The integrated management client also protects its SSH login identities, known_hosts files and the normal primary user and system SSH client configuration files from stdout redirection or use as an export destination. With --sshConfig (-F), it protects the selected primary configuration instead of the unused normal configuration files. Additional files referenced by Include are not automatically inventoried by this destination check.

Redirecting metadata to a separate regular file normally does not require listing unrelated repositories. Hard-linked outputs or ambiguous filesystem aliases can require an inventory check; insufficient access then causes the command to fail before writing. Reading the selected source still requires its normal permissions.

Named output requires an existing immediate parent directory. An existing destination is replaced only with a complete, verified result. Symbolic links, hard links and stdout redirection do not bypass protected-file checks where the alias can be detected; normal pipes remain supported.

A shell redirection using > can truncate its destination before Bifröst starts. Command-side checks cannot undo that truncation. Choose a separate destination, and use the command's --output option when saving an export. Protect managed paths against concurrent untrusted writers; the filesystem is part of the trusted boundary.

docs.title: Exported views
docs.text:
Audit JSON Lines are derived, unsigned views. By default, event fields contain only name, optional domain and outcome, accompanied by timestamps and origin metadata. A redacted export does not redact the underlying clear .baudit journal. Recording exports contain the full, never-redacted signed Cast. Even public metadata can be sensitive.

Preserve original signed evidence. See the audit format, Recording format and signed Cast format for the cryptographic representations.

docs.title: bifroest version
docs.text: Prints the version of the current Bifröst executable. Long output additionally includes build, revision, edition, platform, vendor, and feature information.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest version [flags] bifroest @target version [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --long
docs.text:
bool = true

Controls whether detailed build information is printed. Detailed output is the default. Use --long=false for the short version format; --long (or --long=true) selects detailed output explicitly. This also applies to remote management commands.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Version text on stdout. Long output includes the build, revision, edition, platform, vendor and enabled features. There is no --format flag.

docs.title: Compare workstation and server versions
docs.text:
1. Inspect the workstation binary:

    bifroest version --long=false

  2. With the management alias configured, inspect the server:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin version --long=false

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Remote queries report the server's version and require access.version.read.

docs.title: bifroest audit
docs.text: Inspect configured audit logs, query verified events, or verify and export signed journal evidence. Audit logging is configured separately in the root auditlogs map.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose ls List configured audit logs and their journal, Recording and encryption settings. show Show redacted settings of one audit log. events Query verified events with filters and a result limit. producer-id Print the selected signing producer ID. verify Verify a journal and report outer or full verification. export Verify and export JSON Lines. merge Verify and chronologically merge multiple journals.

Offline journal inputs are supported by verify and export. All evidence commands preserve the signed originals; see Trust and verification.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Configure basic or encrypted audit logging, then query it with audit events.
  • Manage a host remotely with separate workload and administration audit logs.
  • Verify encrypted evidence on a workstation, keeping the recipient private key off the server.

docs.title: bifroest audit events
docs.text:
Shows the newest matching audit events after verifying the journal's captured signed committed state.

bifroest audit events default --limit=20

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest audit events [flags] <name> bifroest @target audit events [flags] <name>

docs.title: name
docs.text: name is the required configured auditlog name. This command queries repositories; it does not accept an offline --source directory. Use audit export for a copied journal.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: --name
docs.text:
string

Exact event-name filter. See the event reference.

docs.title: --flow
docs.text:
string

Exact flow-name filter; requires --with-sensitive because the flow is confidential event data.

docs.title: --since
docs.text:
Timestamp

Inclusive start time in RFC 3339 format, for example 2026-01-02T12:00:00Z.

docs.title: --until
docs.text:
Timestamp

Inclusive end time in RFC 3339 format.

docs.title: --limit
docs.text:
uint = 100

Number of newest matches to return. 0 selects all matches, subject to the result limits below. Name, flow and time filters are applied before this selection.

docs.title: --with-sensitive
docs.text:
bool = false

Include confidential fields. Encrypted journals need a matching local decryption key for this view.

docs.title: --decryptionIdentityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local private-key file for encrypted private fields; repeatable. Available locally and through @target, not direct SSH. Remote keys are only accepted with --with-sensitive; X-AuditPrivateKey supplies the client default.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string

Independently trusted producer ID for sensitive @target queries. Requires --with-sensitive; alternatively provision X-ExpectedProducerId in the SSH configuration. Local queries use the configured signing identity.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The default table shows time, event name, domain, outcome and record ID, plus flow when sensitive output is requested. Structured output contains events with their timestamps and origin metadata. Results preserve journal order within the selected newest matches.

Journal verification includes events excluded by the filters. A selection is limited to 250,000 events and 64 MiB of event data. Exceeding a limit fails the command; narrow the filters or lower --limit in that case. --limit=0 does not disable these bounds.

docs.title: Query events after enabling an audit log
docs.text:
1. Configure and use basic audit logging.

  2. Query public events from that configured journal:

    bifroest audit events default --limit=20 --format=json

  3. Narrow the query to a recorded event name and time window:

    bifroest audit events default \
  --name=connection.closed \
  --since=2026-01-02T12:00:00Z \
  --until=2026-01-02T13:00:00Z \
  --limit=50

    Choose times that cover the generated events. For encrypted, sensitive remote queries, follow the workstation verification guide.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Public remote queries require auditlogs.events. Sensitive queries require auditlogs.download; the integrated client downloads and verifies the journal locally. Direct-SSH sensitive queries require both rights. Direct SSH can read clear private fields but cannot use a workstation's decryption key.

docs.title: bifroest audit export
docs.text:
Verifies the selected journal, then exports events as JSON Lines in journal order.

bifroest audit export default

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest audit export [flags] [auditlogName] bifroest audit export --source PATH --expectedProducerId ID [flags] [auditlogName] bifroest @target audit export [flags] [auditlogName]

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: auditlogName selects a configured journal and defaults to default in the local CLI and integrated client. With --source, it labels the copied journal in exported records. It is not a segment path; a standalone delivered segment is not a complete journal source.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general executable flags. Direct SSH supports only the command options noted above.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local repository configuration; defaults to the platform path. Cannot be combined with --source or @target.

docs.title: --source
docs.text:
File Path

Complete copied local journal, including its signed head and required segments. Requires independent producer trust; no server configuration or signing private key is needed. Unavailable with @target.

docs.title: --encryptionPublicKeyFile
docs.text:
File Path

Expected recipient for an encrypted offline --source. Required for keyless outer verification and when supplying multiple decryption identities. With one private key, its recipient can be derived instead. Unavailable with @target.

docs.title: --decryptionIdentityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local private key for encrypted confidential fields; repeatable. Used only with --with-sensitive. The client can use X-AuditPrivateKey; keys stay on the CLI machine. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --with-sensitive
docs.text:
bool = false

Include confidential fields. Encrypted journals additionally need the matching decryption key. Without this flag, supplied private keys are not loaded for event decryption.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string

Independently trusted 64-hex signing producer ID. Configured local selection otherwise uses its signing key; copied sources require this flag. The integrated client requires it or X-ExpectedProducerId. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --output
docs.text:
File Path = "-"

JSONL destination file, or - for stdout. The immediate parent must already exist. Named output is published only after successful verification and destination checks; remote-client paths are local to the workstation. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --force
docs.text:
bool = false

Replace an existing named output. Protected destinations remain protected. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
One event with its origin and integrity metadata per JSON line. The default public event contains name, optional domain and outcome; --with-sensitive includes private fields. JSONL is an unsigned view of the original evidence. There is no --format selector.

Every selected source is verified before events are published. Events added during a live read may be absent from the result. Export has a 128 MiB JSONL output cap; use audit verify to verify a larger journal without exporting its events.

docs.title: Export a configured journal
docs.text:
1. Enable and use basic audit logging.

  2. Export its public view:

    bifroest audit export default --output /srv/audit-evidence/public.jsonl

    Create the output directory beforehand and keep it outside managed storage.

docs.title: Export confidential encrypted events on a workstation
docs.text:
Follow the encrypted-evidence guide to configure the server, trusted producer and local recipient key, then run:

bifroest @bifroest-admin audit export evidence \
  --with-sensitive \
  --output /srv/audit-evidence/sensitive.jsonl

For disconnected verification, use a complete copied journal with --source, as shown in the offline audit example.

Also accepted as audit decrypt.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local invocation supports configured and copied journals. Client-side remote export requires auditlogs.download, including for redacted exports, because it downloads original signed evidence. Direct-SSH export requires auditlogs.events, plus auditlogs.download for sensitive output.

Direct SSH accepts an explicit auditlog name and --with-sensitive, writes JSONL to stdout and uses the service's configured trust. Sensitive output requires artifact-transfer permission; encrypted private fields require a workstation's client-side decryption instead.

docs.title: bifroest audit ls
docs.text:
Lists the named entries in the selected configuration's auditlogs map.

bifroest audit ls

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest audit ls [flags] bifroest @target audit ls [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One row per auditlog name, ordered by name, indicating whether the audit journal, session recording and encryption are configured. This describes settings, not journal verification or delivery health. Use audit verify to verify a journal.

docs.title: Inspect separate workload and administration logs
docs.text:
1. Configure the two named entries in the management guide.

  2. Read their settings summary:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin audit ls --format=json

  3. Select workload or administration with audit show.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Remote queries require access.auditlogs.read, but no download permission.

docs.title: bifroest audit merge
docs.text:
Verifies every selected journal before producing one chronological JSON Lines stream.

bifroest audit merge workload administration

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest audit merge [flags] <auditlogName>... bifroest @target audit merge [flags] <auditlogName>...

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: One or more required auditlog names. Local inputs can also be complete evidence copies referenced by a dedicated configuration. There is no --source flag on merge. When journals are still being written, their results need not represent the same instant.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general executable flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local repository configuration; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --decryptionIdentityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local private key for encrypted confidential fields; repeat for different recipients. Keys are loaded only with --with-sensitive. The client can use X-AuditPrivateKey. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --with-sensitive
docs.text:
bool = false

Include private event fields. Every encrypted source then needs its matching private key.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string

Trusted producer mapping <auditlogName>=<64-hex-id>; repeat for each independently trusted source. For one selected source, a plain producer ID is also accepted. Configured local sources otherwise use their signing identities. Remote multi-source merge needs explicit trust for every source; X-ExpectedProducerId supplies a default only when one source is selected. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --output
docs.text:
File Path = "-"

JSONL destination file or - for stdout. Its immediate parent must already exist. Named output is published only after successful verification and destination checks, including protection for unselected configured evidence. Client output paths are local to the workstation. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --force
docs.text:
bool = false

Replace an existing named output. Protected destinations remain protected. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
JSON Lines ordered by producer-signed timestamp. Ordering is deterministic when timestamps are equal. A producer's timestamp is not an independently trusted clock. The public view is redacted; sensitive output is plaintext. JSONL is unsigned and there is no --format flag.

All sources must verify before output is published. The merged JSONL result is limited to 128 MiB. See Output and errors.

docs.title: Merge separately configured workload and administration logs
docs.text:
1. Configure the two logs and generate workload and administration connections using the management guide.

  2. On the host, export their public events in chronological order:

    bifroest audit merge workload administration --output /srv/audit-evidence/merged.jsonl

    The destination directory must already exist and remain outside managed storage.

docs.title: Merge complete offline copies without server signing keys
docs.text:
1. Retain each source's producer ID independently. Copy each complete journal to the verification machine.

  2. Point a dedicated configuration at those copies:

    Verification workstation: /srv/audit-evidence/configuration.yaml
    auditlogs:
  first:
    identityFile: /srv/audit-evidence/absent-first-signing-key
    directory: /srv/audit-evidence/first-journal
    recording:
      directory: /srv/audit-evidence/first-recordings
  second:
    identityFile: /srv/audit-evidence/absent-second-signing-key
    directory: /srv/audit-evidence/second-journal
    recording:
      directory: /srv/audit-evidence/second-recordings
session:
  type: fs
  storage: /srv/audit-evidence/session-inspection
flows:
  - name: evidence-inspection
    auditlog: first
    authorization:
      type: none
    environment:
      type: dummy

    This example selects clear journal copies. It is an inspection-only configuration, not a server setup. The placeholder signing-key files are intentionally absent.

  3. Supply both independently retained IDs, replacing FIRST_PRODUCER_ID and SECOND_PRODUCER_ID:

    bifroest audit merge first second \
  --configuration /srv/audit-evidence/configuration.yaml \
  --expectedProducerId first=FIRST_PRODUCER_ID \
  --expectedProducerId second=SECOND_PRODUCER_ID \
  --output /srv/audit-output/merged.jsonl

    With explicit producer trust, the signing private keys are not opened or created. For encrypted copies, also configure each recipient public key, and supply local private keys with --with-sensitive when confidential fields are needed.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Client-side remote merge downloads the selected journals and requires auditlogs.download. Direct-SSH merge requires auditlogs.events, plus auditlogs.download for sensitive output.

Direct SSH accepts auditlog names and --with-sensitive, writes stdout and uses configured server trust. Sensitive output requires artifact-transfer permission. Use the integrated client for decrypting encrypted fields with workstation keys.

docs.title: bifroest audit producer-id
docs.text:
Prints the producer ID derived from a selected signing identity without reading the journal or creating a missing key.

bifroest audit producer-id default

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest audit producer-id [flags] <auditlogName> bifroest @target audit producer-id [flags] <auditlogName>

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: auditlogName is the required configured name. Local use reads the signing private key; management reads the service's active identity.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general executable flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The default output is one lowercase 64-hex producer ID followed by a newline. Structured output contains the producer ID. A missing signing key produces an error and is never regenerated by this command.

The ID can be transferred; the private signing key stays on the server. To establish producer trust, obtain and retain the ID through an independently trusted channel. Merely querying it from the same untrusted source as the evidence does not create an independent trust anchor.

docs.title: Retain producer trust after enabling audit or Recording
docs.text:
1. Configure and start encrypted evidence capture.

  2. As the service user on the Bifröst host, obtain its producer ID:

    bifroest audit producer-id evidence

  3. Retain the value separately and provision it on the workstation as described in the verification guide.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

The name must select a defined audit logger with an existing signing identity. Artifact-transfer permission is not required.

docs.title: bifroest audit show
docs.text:
Shows the settings of one named audit log without exporting its events.

bifroest audit show default

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest audit show [flags] <name> bifroest @target audit show [flags] <name>

docs.title: name
docs.text: name is the required configured auditlog name, as returned by audit ls.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Redacted settings, including the auditlog name, journal and Recording configuration and delivery targets. Declared target names and types remain visible; arbitrary strings such as paths, endpoints, credentials and templates are redacted. Audit-log settings remain redacted even when the management flow grants flows.credentials for flow show. Remote inspection requires auditlogs.read.

docs.title: Check the selected Recording and delivery policy
docs.text:
1. Enable and configure session recording on a named audit log.

  2. Inspect that entry:

    bifroest audit show default --format=yaml

    Use the original configuration reference for the meaning of individual properties; redacted values cannot be recovered from this view.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Artifact-transfer permission is not required.

docs.title: bifroest audit verify
docs.text:
Checks journal integrity and trusted producer identity without exporting events.

bifroest audit verify default

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest audit verify [flags] [auditlogName] bifroest audit verify --source PATH --expectedProducerId ID [flags] [auditlogName] bifroest @target audit verify [flags] [auditlogName]

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: auditlogName selects a configured audit log and defaults to default locally and through @target. With --source, it labels the copied source rather than selecting a directory. Direct SSH requires the name explicitly.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general executable flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local repository configuration; defaults to the platform path. Cannot be combined with --source or @target; unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --source
docs.text:
File Path

Complete local journal copy, including its signed head and required segments. Requires an independently trusted producer ID. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --encryptionPublicKeyFile
docs.text:
File Path

Expected recipient for an encrypted offline --source. Required without a private key or with multiple decryption identities. With one private key, the recipient can be derived instead. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --decryptionIdentityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local private key for full verification of encrypted private fields; repeatable. The client can use X-AuditPrivateKey. Without a key, encrypted verification has outer scope; a supplied non-matching key fails. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --require-full
docs.text:
bool = false

Reject outer-only results. Available in all supported execution modes; direct SSH cannot fully verify encrypted content without a local recipient key, so that combination fails.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string

Independent 64-hex signing producer ID. Configured local selection otherwise uses its signing key. Required for a copied source or provided through X-ExpectedProducerId for the client. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The default status is verified (scope: outer) or verified (scope: full). Structured formats contain the verification result and scope. Success exits with status 0; a verification failure produces no success result.

The command can run while the service keeps writing; later events may be absent from the verified result. A standalone delivered segment is not a complete journal source. See verification scopes and evidence completeness.

docs.title: Verify the configured journal while Bifröst runs
docs.text:
1. Enable basic audit logging and generate an SSH connection.

  2. On the host, run as the service user:

    bifroest audit verify default

docs.title: Require full verification of encrypted remote evidence
docs.text:
1. Configure the recipient, producer pin and local private key using the workstation guide.

  2. Verify without exporting event content:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin audit verify evidence --require-full --format=json

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local invocation supports configured and copied journals. Client-side remote verification downloads the journal and requires auditlogs.download, including outer-only verification. Direct-SSH verification requires auditlogs.verify.

Direct SSH accepts an explicit auditlog name, --require-full and --format. It verifies server-side evidence without downloading it or accepting a workstation decryption key. No artifact-transfer permission is needed for that verification.

docs.title: bifroest flow
docs.text: Inspect the flows in the selected local configuration or in a running management service. These commands read settings; flow configuration defines authorization and the environment used by SSH connections.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose ls List flow names, selected audit logs and authorization/environment types. show Show the settings of one named flow.

Arbitrary configuration strings are redacted in detail output as documented on show.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Follow Manage a Bifröst host remotely to configure an administration flow alongside a local-account flow and inspect both with these commands.

docs.title: bifroest flow ls
docs.text:
Lists configured flows in ascending name order.

bifroest flow ls

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest flow ls [flags] bifroest @target flow ls [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One row per flow, with its name, selected auditlog, authorization type and environment type. This is a configuration listing, not a count of active sessions.

docs.title: Inspect the configured flows remotely
docs.text:
1. Use the server configuration and SSH alias from the management guide.

  2. List the administration and local flows:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin flow ls --format=json

  3. Select a returned name with flow show.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local use reads a configuration file; remote use reads the service's loaded configuration and requires access.flows.read. See Invocation and data sources.

docs.title: bifroest flow show
docs.text:
Shows the settings of one configured flow.

bifroest flow show local

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest flow show [flags] <name> bifroest @target flow show [flags] <name>

docs.title: name
docs.text: name is the required flow name, as returned by flow ls.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Key/value settings by default, or a structured settings object. Arbitrary strings are redacted, including image references, Kubernetes name templates, commands, environment variables and SSH certificate extension values. Structural flow/auditlog names, authorization/environment types, non-string settings and fixed image-pull policies remain visible.

Local inspection always uses this redacted view. Remote inspection requires flows.read; access.flows.credentials additionally permits unredacted flow show output. It is not a client flag and does not affect audit-log detail redaction. A missing flow produces an error.

docs.title: Check how an administration connection is routed
docs.text:
1. Configure the two distinct flows in the management guide.

  2. Inspect the administration flow:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin flow show administration --format=yaml

    The output identifies the management environment and selected administration audit log. Redacted values do not mean that the corresponding setting is absent.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

The selected local configuration or remote service must contain the named flow.

docs.title: bifroest id
docs.text:
Local identifier utilities. These commands do not authenticate, access storage, rewrite evidence or create identifiers.

Command Purpose convert (alias parse) Print conventional UUID and Base58 notation for each input.

docs.title: bifroest id convert
docs.text: Alias: bifroest id parse.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest id convert [flags] <id>...

docs.title: id
docs.text: One or more required IDs, processed in input order. Accepted forms are Base58 of exactly 16 bytes, hyphenated UUIDs (either hex case), compact hex UUIDs, braced UUIDs and urn:uuid:…. The nil UUID is permitted by this conversion utility; resource selectors retain their own nonzero/version/variant restrictions.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
One LF-terminated line per input, no header, spaces or explanatory stdout:

<lowercase-hyphenated-UUID>,<canonical-Base58>

All arguments are validated before output starts. Invalid input reports an error on stderr, returns a nonzero exit status and produces no converted lines. Configuration, keys and repositories are not opened.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest key
docs.text:
Key commands generate and exchange SSH trust material for an SSH environment and Bifröst delegation authorization. Public exports support the management client and direct SSH; generate and import are local-only. key import host --address can additionally retrieve a host key from the CLI machine.

Exchange exported public material and SHA256 fingerprints over an independently trusted channel.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose generate Create a new Ed25519 key pair. export Export public keys, certificate authorities and host trust entries. import Validate and merge public certificate authorities or host trust entries.

Some local bootstrap operations create missing identities. Server-side exports only expose existing public material. Configure server trust files through the host's normal configuration management.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Configure encrypted audit and Recording evidence with a dedicated recipient pair.
  • Configure OpenSSH certificate authentication using CA and host-key exchange.
  • Export server public keys remotely using a separate management flow.

docs.title: bifroest key generate
docs.text:
Creates an Ed25519 private key in OpenSSH format. The command never replaces an existing file and never writes private key material to stdout. Private files use mode 0400 on Unix and a protected DACL on Windows.

If --publicFile is set, the corresponding public key is additionally written as one LF-terminated OpenSSH public-key line.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest key generate [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --identityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Private key file to create.

docs.title: --publicFile
docs.text:
File Path

Optional public key file to create. It has to differ from identityFile and is never replaced. This explicit output does not enable automatic .pub companion files.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: The requested private key and optional public-key file. Private key material is never written to stdout. Existing destination files are not replaced.

docs.title: Create a dedicated evidence-encryption recipient
docs.text:
1. On the trusted workstation, prepare a private directory for the recipient key.

  2. Generate the pair:

    bifroest key generate \
  --identityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key \
  --publicFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key.pub

  3. Transfer only the public key and configure its server-side use following the encrypted-evidence guide. The full audit configuration example also covers disconnected verification.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest key export
docs.text: Export public SSH trust material. The selected subcommand determines which identity supplies the public key and how the result is formatted.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose public Export a local identity's public half or a configured server SSH identity. ca Export the effective certificate authority of a configured SSH flow. host Export host keys as OpenSSH known_hosts entries.

With the local or integrated CLI, --output selects a file on the CLI machine. Direct SSH writes stdout only. Remote export uses existing configured keys and requires access.keys.read. Private identities stay on their source machine.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Configure encrypted evidence with a dedicated recipient public key.
  • Configure certificate authentication using exported CA and host keys.
  • Export server public keys remotely using a configured management connection.

docs.title: bifroest key export ca
docs.text: Exports the public SSH certificate authority of the selected flow. Locally, Bifröst loads the selected configuration and creates a missing private CA. With @target or direct SSH, it exports the running flow's existing CA without creating or changing a key. No .pub companion file is created on the server.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest key export ca [flags] <flowName> bifroest @target key export ca [flags] <flowName>

docs.title: flowName
docs.text: flowName is the name of an SSH-environment flow with certificate authentication enabled.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration to load; defaults to the platform path. Not accepted with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --output
docs.text:
File Path = "-"

Output file on the CLI machine. - writes exactly one LF-terminated OpenSSH public-key line to stdout. Direct SSH always writes to stdout and does not accept output or force.

docs.title: --force
docs.text:
bool = false

Replaces an existing output file.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One OpenSSH CA public-key line, on stdout or in the requested file. Only a local bootstrap invocation can generate a missing effective private CA.

docs.title: Export the CA of an SSH-environment flow
docs.text:
1. Configure the certificate-authenticated openssh flow in the SSH-environment example.

  2. Export the effective public CA:

    bifroest key export ca openssh --output /srv/ssh-trust/bifroest-ca.pub

    Use the actual configured flow name and an existing output directory. Continue with the target's CA setup in that example, or the full Bifröst delegation workflow.

docs.title: Export the running server's CA
docs.text:
1. Configure the gateway flow and management alias in the public-key export guide.

  2. Export its active CA to a file on the workstation:

    Administrator workstation
    bifroest @bifroest-admin key export ca gateway --output gateway-ca.pub

    The management flow must grant keys.read. Direct SSH supports ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'key export ca gateway'.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest key export host
docs.text: Exports known_hosts entries for the supplied address. Locally, --identityFile selects a key to load or create; otherwise the configured host keys are loaded or created. With @target or direct SSH, the running server's active host keys are exported without creating or changing any key.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
bifroest key export host [flags] bifroest @target key export host [flags]

--address labels the exported entries; it does not connect to that address. A remote invocation connects only to the management target.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration to load when identityFile is absent. Defaults to the platform path. Not accepted with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --identityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Specific local host private-key file to load or create. This cannot be combined with configuration and is not accepted with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --address
docs.text:
string

Host represented by the generated entries. Port 22 can be omitted; non-default IPv6 ports use [address]:port.

docs.title: --output
docs.text:
File Path = "-"

Output file on the CLI machine. - writes to stdout. Direct SSH always writes to stdout and does not accept output or force.

docs.title: --force
docs.text:
bool = false

Replaces an existing output file.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: OpenSSH known_hosts entries on stdout or in the requested file. Remote export returns the keys already used by the running Bifröst server; it is not a host-key discovery or unknown-key acceptance command.

docs.title: Provision trusted host keys for a management workstation
docs.text:
1. On the Bifröst host, use its actual configuration and address:

    bifroest key export host \
  --address bifroest.example.org \
  --output /srv/ssh-trust/bifroest-known-hosts

  2. Transfer the public entries over an independently trusted channel and import them on the workstation with key import host.

    The management guide uses these entries for SSH host-key checking. See Bifröst delegation for a complete host-key bootstrap sequence.

docs.title: Export active host keys over an already trusted connection
docs.text:
1. Provision management SSH trust and configure the workstation alias as in the management guide.

  2. Export the server's active public keys:

    Administrator workstation
    bifroest @bifroest-admin key export host \
  --address bifroest.example.org \
  --output bifroest-known-hosts

    The initial management connection still needs a trusted known_hosts entry. This command cannot bootstrap its own unknown host key. Direct SSH supports ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'key export host --address=bifroest.example.org'.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest key export public
docs.text:
Writes exactly one LF-terminated OpenSSH public-key line. Standard output is used by default. An existing destination file is not replaced unless --force is set.

Locally, select a private-key file. With @target or direct SSH, select a configured SSH flow: Bifröst exports its certificate subject identity, or the selected static environment.identityFiles entry. Private keys stay on the source machine; exporting never creates a missing server identity.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest key export public [flags] bifroest @target key export public [flags] <flowName>

docs.title: flowName
docs.text: Required with @target and direct SSH; not accepted locally. The SSH-environment flow whose configured identity is exported. Certificate flows have one subject identity at index 0. Other SSH flows require an explicit, static identityFiles entry; session-dependent paths and implicit host-key fallback are not selected by this command.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --identityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Private key file whose public key is exported. Required locally; not accepted with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --identityIndex
docs.text:
unsigned integer = "0"

Zero-based index in the selected server flow's identityFiles. Available with @target and direct SSH. For a certificate subject identity, only 0 is accepted.

docs.title: --comment
docs.text:
string

Optional OpenSSH public-key comment. Line breaks are not accepted.

docs.title: --output
docs.text:
File Path = "-"

Output file on the CLI machine. - writes to stdout. Direct SSH always writes to stdout and does not accept output or force.

docs.title: --force
docs.text:
bool = false

Replaces an existing output file. Without this flag, an existing file is never modified.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One LF-terminated OpenSSH public-key line, on stdout or in the requested file. The private key is not modified or emitted.

docs.title: Export a recipient's public key after generating its private key
docs.text:
1. Generate a recipient with key generate, or select an existing private identity.

  2. Export its public half on the workstation:

    bifroest key export public \
  --identityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key \
  --output /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key.pub

    Choose a new output path; --force is required to replace an existing public-key file. See the encrypted-evidence guide for server configuration using this public key.

docs.title: Export a configured server identity
docs.text:
1. Configure the gateway certificate flow and workstation alias in Export server public keys remotely.

  2. Export its subject public key to the workstation:

    Administrator workstation
    bifroest @bifroest-admin key export public gateway --output gateway-subject.pub

    For an SSH flow using several static identity files, add --identityIndex=1 to select its second entry. The server does not accept an identityFile path from the client.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest key import
docs.text: Validate public SSH trust material and merge it into the selected trust file. An expected fingerprint can verify that the material matches a key obtained through an independent trusted channel.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose ca Import SSH certificate-authority public keys. host Import OpenSSH host trust entries from a file, stdin or a server.

The command pages document accepted inputs, destinations and fingerprint checks. A failed validation leaves the destination unchanged.

Imports are local bootstrap commands. Select the destination with --trustedCAsFile or --knownHostsFile on the CLI machine.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Follow Bifröst delegation for a complete trust exchange, or the SSH-environment example to provision target trust.

docs.title: bifroest key import ca
docs.text: Validates and merges plain OpenSSH certificate-authority public keys into a local trust file. Certificates, private keys, and authorized-key options are rejected. A fingerprint mismatch leaves the destination unchanged.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest key import ca [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --trustedCAsFile
docs.text:
File Path

Public-key file containing the trusted SSH certificate authorities to update.

docs.title: --input
docs.text:
File Path = "-"

File containing the public CA keys. - reads from stdin. Input is limited to 4 MiB.

docs.title: --expectedFingerprint
docs.text:
string

Expected OpenSSH SHA256 fingerprint of every imported CA, or unknown. Omission implies unknown.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: A CA trust file containing the successfully imported public keys. Input validation or fingerprint failure leaves the destination unchanged; no private key is imported.

docs.title: Import a separately provisioned CA
docs.text:
1. Obtain the CA public key and its SHA256 fingerprint through a trusted channel, as in the delegation example.

  2. Import it, replacing CA_FINGERPRINT with that value:

    bifroest key import ca \
  --trustedCAsFile /etc/engity/bifroest/trusted-cas.pub \
  --input /srv/ssh-trust/bifroest-ca.pub \
  --expectedFingerprint CA_FINGERPRINT

    The service user needs write access to the destination's parent directory.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest key import host
docs.text: Validates and merges normal known_hosts entries from a file, stdin, or an SSH server. Incoming @revoked, @cert-authority, and certificate entries are rejected. A fingerprint mismatch leaves the destination unchanged.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
bifroest key import host [flags]

--address can contact an SSH server to obtain a host key. The imported trust file is local to the CLI machine.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --knownHostsFile
docs.text:
File Path

OpenSSH known_hosts file to update.

docs.title: --input
docs.text:
File Path

File containing entries to import. - or omission reads from stdin. This cannot be combined with address. Input is limited to 4 MiB.

docs.title: --address
docs.text:
string

SSH server from which one negotiated host key is retrieved. Port 22 can be omitted.

docs.title: --expectedFingerprint
docs.text:
string

Expected OpenSSH SHA256 fingerprint, or unknown. It is required with address; omission for file or stdin input implies unknown.

Warning

--expectedFingerprint unknown with --address explicitly trusts a key obtained from an unverified network peer and can expose the connection to an on-path attack. The command also emits a warning to stderr.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: A local known_hosts file containing the successfully imported entries. Invalid entries and fingerprint mismatches leave the destination unchanged.

docs.title: Import trusted entries exported by the server
docs.text:
1. Obtain the server's key export host output through an independently trusted provisioning channel. It can contain several host keys.

  2. Import those already trusted entries on the workstation:

    bifroest key import host \
  --knownHostsFile ~/.ssh/known_hosts \
  --input /srv/ssh-trust/bifroest-known-hosts

    The importing user needs write access to the destination's parent directory. For a single imported key, --expectedFingerprint can additionally check its independently retained fingerprint; one fingerprint cannot match several different keys. The SSH-environment configuration and Bifröst delegation example show complete trust exchanges. Use Remote access to configure a management alias after provisioning host trust.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest metrics
docs.text: Read operational metrics from the running instance through an authorized management flow. No monitoring port or monitoring bearer token is required.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose show Show a snapshot of all available metrics or exact metric families.

See Monitoring for metric names and measurement boundaries.

docs.title: bifroest metrics show
docs.text: Shows a live snapshot from the same data source as the monitoring listener's /metrics endpoint.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
bifroest @target metrics show [flags] [<metric>...]

With a standard SSH client, run ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'metrics show'.

docs.title: metric
docs.text:
Optional exact metric family names from the monitoring reference. Omit them to show all currently available families. Multiple names select the union, including every label set. Repeated names do not duplicate output. Regex, label selectors and PromQL are not supported.

Select a histogram by its base family name, such as bifroest_authentication_flow_evaluation_duration_seconds, not by a _bucket, _sum or _count sample name. The complete histogram is returned.

An unknown name fails the command without metric output. A known family with no current measurements remains absent, including average ages when no objects are active; it is not filled with zero.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json or openmetrics. Other commands' yaml and cbor formats are not supported here.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The default table contains sample names, values and labels. Histograms have bucket, sum and count rows. JSON contains capturedAt, processStartedAt and families; each family uses Prometheus protobuf JSON fields, preserving labels, types, histogram buckets and summary quantiles. Non-finite numbers are strings such as "NaN" or "Infinity", and 64-bit integer fields are decimal strings. OpenMetrics includes HELP/TYPE metadata and one final # EOF line.

Every format includes the snapshot time and process start time; OpenMetrics carries them in a comment. Where process-start observation is unavailable, the startup timestamp is used. The snapshot is not a transaction across concurrent activity. Counters restart with the process; the command does not retain history or calculate rates.

docs.title: Inspect connections without a monitoring port
docs.text:
1. Configure an authorized management flow and workstation alias. A configured management flow enables metric collection even when monitoring.enabled is false.

  2. Query two metric families:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin metrics show bifroest_connections_active bifroest_sessions_active

    The table includes all current label sets for those families.

  3. Export the same selection for scripts:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin metrics show bifroest_connections_active bifroest_sessions_active --format=json
ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'metrics show bifroest_connections_active --format=openmetrics'

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Requires access.metrics.read in the management flow. A metrics-only policy is access: {metrics: true}. Authorized-key and forced-command restrictions still apply.

docs.title: bifroest recording
docs.text: Work with sealed session recordings from a configured repository or a copied artifact. Session recording configuration controls capture, storage, encryption and delivery.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose ls List one bounded page of verified repository metadata. show Show verified metadata for one repository Recording ID. inspect Inspect a local artifact and emit JSON metadata. verify Verify evidence against a trusted producer, without replaying content. export Verify and export the signed asciicast v3 stream. play Verify and replay captured terminal output.

Repository commands select an auditlog name and Recording UUID. File commands accept .bcast, .becast or signed .cast as documented. Remote verification, export and playback download the signed original and run on the CLI machine; see Remote access.

Paging, ID order and streaming behavior are documented on recording ls. Producer trust, decryption and protected output paths are described in Trust and verification.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Record, find and replay a session on the Bifröst host.
  • Verify encrypted evidence on a workstation using a trusted producer ID and a local recipient key.

docs.title: bifroest recording export
docs.text:
Verifies a Recording and exports its exact signed asciicast v3 stream.

bifroest recording export --with-sensitive --output session.cast default RECORDING_UUID

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest recording export [flags] <auditlogName> <recording-uuid> bifroest recording export [flags] --expectedProducerId ID <file> bifroest @target recording export [flags] <auditlogName> <recording-uuid>

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: Configured auditlog name for repository selection. Used together with recording-uuid, locally or through @target.

docs.title: recording-uuid
docs.text: Recording UUID returned by recording ls for the selected auditlog.

docs.title: file
docs.text: One local .bcast, .becast or signed .cast file, as an alternative to repository selection. Format detection uses file content, not its extension. Standard input is unsupported. File inputs cannot be combined with @target.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string

Independently trusted 64-hex producer ID for copied or downloaded evidence. X-ExpectedProducerId provides the client's default. The local name-and-UUID selector uses its configured signing identity and does not accept this flag. Unavailable over direct SSH. See producer trust.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local repository configuration; defaults to the platform path. Cannot be combined with a file input, @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --with-sensitive
docs.text:
bool = false

Required before opening the input for every format and destination. Recording exports are complete and never redacted.

docs.title: --allowUntrusted
docs.text:
bool = false

Explicitly accept cryptographic self-consistency without trusted producer identity. Cannot be combined with an expected producer ID or configured local repository selection. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --decryptionIdentityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local SSH private key for encrypted .becast; repeatable. Ed25519 and RSA identities are supported; the key must match the signed recipient fingerprint. X-RecordingPrivateKey provides the client's default. Keys stay on the CLI machine. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --output
docs.text:
File Path = "-"

Destination file or - for stdout. The immediate parent must already exist. Named output is published only after successful verification and destination checks. In @target mode, the file is on the CLI machine. Direct SSH writes stdout and does not accept this flag.

docs.title: --force
docs.text:
bool = false

Replace an existing named output with the complete verified export. Protected inputs and key files remain protected. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The signed asciicast v3 stream, including captured terminal, stdout and stderr content. Encrypted .becast is decrypted and fully verified before plaintext is published. Clear .bcast and signed .cast need no decryption key. There is no --format selector.

The local input must be a regular, non-symlink file; changing it during export can cause the command to fail. The server does not automatically create plaintext Cast or JSONL copies.

docs.title: Export a Recording from the local repository
docs.text:
1. Generate a Recording with the recording guide.
  2. Find its UUID with recording ls.

  3. Export to a separate path outside managed storage:

    bifroest recording export \
  --with-sensitive \
  --output session.cast \
  default RECORDING_UUID

docs.title: Export and independently inspect encrypted evidence
docs.text:
1. Configure encryption, producer pinning and local keys using the workstation guide.

  2. Download, verify and export the selected original:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin recording export \
  --with-sensitive \
  --output session.cast \
  evidence RECORDING_UUID

  3. Independently inspect the exported Cast with the same trusted producer ID:

    bifroest recording inspect --expectedProducerId PRODUCER_ID session.cast

    PRODUCER_ID is the independently retained 64-hex value. The exported Cast's verified castDigest can be compared with the encrypted original's signed claimedCastDigest; see recording inspect.

docs.title: External playback
docs.text:
Use an external player supporting asciicast v3 and unknown comment lines to play the exported file. The plaintext Cast is sensitive; its signature remains independently verifiable. Delivery targets retain sealed originals at <producer-id>/<recording-uuid>.<suffix>, which can also be copied for offline export with an independent producer ID.

For playback directly in Bifröst, use the separate recording play command.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local invocation supports configured repositories and copied files. Remote export requires access.recordings.download. Direct SSH exports clear Recordings to stdout with --with-sensitive; encrypted content requires the client with a local private key.

docs.title: bifroest recording inspect
docs.text:
Verifies a local Recording artifact and emits its public metadata as one JSON object.

bifroest recording inspect --expectedProducerId PRODUCER_ID session.bcast

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest recording inspect [flags] <file>

docs.title: file
docs.text: file is a required local .bcast, .becast or signed .cast artifact. Content determines the format, not the extension. The input must be regular, non-symlinked and unchanged in identity, size, mode and modification time throughout inspection. Standard input is unsupported.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general executable flags.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string
