Independent 64-hex producer trust anchor. A mismatch fails inspection; a matching value sets signature.trusted to true. Without this flag, inspection verifies self-consistency and reports signature.trusted: false. An artifact-embedded ID is not independent trust.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: One bifroest.session-recording-inspection/v1 JSON object; there is no --format flag. Invalid evidence produces no JSON result. Emitted signature.valid is always true, while signature.trusted records whether an independent matching producer ID was supplied.

docs.title: Verification scope
docs.text:
• Clear .bcast: full verification, including reconstructed Cast content, with verified status and castDigest.
  • Encrypted .becast: outer verification only. claimedStatus and claimedCastDigest are signed outer-seal claims, not verified inner-Cast results. status, castDigest and cast are omitted.
  • Signed .cast: full verification, with a cast object containing event counts rather than session metadata or reasons.

Format values are bcast/v1, becast-cbor/v1 and cast/v3. Native containers also report chunk count and claimed Cast size. Event payloads are not emitted, but public metadata still needs appropriate protection.

docs.title: Output safety
docs.text: Regular-file stdout must not refer to the inspected input. A shell > redirection can truncate a file before the command starts; see protected destinations.

docs.title: Inspect an encrypted original and its full export
docs.text:
1. Obtain a sealed .becast original and retain its producer ID independently using the encrypted evidence workflow.

  2. Inspect the copied original without a decryption key:

    bifroest recording inspect --expectedProducerId PRODUCER_ID session.becast

    The result has outer scope and a signed claimedCastDigest. 3. Fully verify and export with the matching local recipient key:

    bifroest recording export session.becast \
  --expectedProducerId PRODUCER_ID \
  --decryptionIdentityFile /srv/audit-keys/recipient-key \
  --with-sensitive \
  --output session.cast
bifroest recording inspect --expectedProducerId PRODUCER_ID session.cast

    The exported Cast has full scope and a verified castDigest. Compare that digest with the original's claimed digest. See the Recording format and native vectors for format details.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

This command inspects local files. For a configured repository or remote Recording ID, use recording show. For full verification of encrypted content, use recording verify.

docs.title: bifroest recording ls
docs.text:
Lists sealed Recordings in one audit log, streaming entries after verification.

bifroest recording ls default --limit=20

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest recording ls [flags] <auditlogName> bifroest @target recording ls [flags] <auditlogName>

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: auditlogName is the required configured auditlog name. Its Recording repository must be enabled. Only sealed originals are listed; active sessions are listed with session ls.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: --limit
docs.text:
uint = 100

Maximum entries in this page, from 1 through 1,000. 0 is invalid, not an unlimited listing.

docs.title: --after
docs.text:
Recording UUID

Exclusive Recording-ID cursor. Use the last returned ID to request the next page.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: The table shows ID, auditlog, signed status, start time and verification scope. Structured output contains the corresponding metadata entries. Clear Recordings receive full verification; encrypted Recordings receive outer verification without a decryption key. Outer metadata does not establish that the encrypted Cast can be decrypted and fully verified.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Entries are ordered by ascending Recording ID, independently of start time. Each returned entry is cryptographically verified.

The repository can change between pages. A newly created ID before the current cursor appears on a fresh listing; retention can remove an artifact during a request, causing an error and requiring a retry.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Streaming is the default, including when --limit is set. The limit controls the entry count. Entries appear as they are verified; JSON, YAML and CBOR form one result array or sequence when the command completes successfully.

A later verification, connection or output error aborts with nonzero status and leaves already emitted entries as partial output. JSON or CBOR may be unfinished. Check the command's exit status before treating a page as complete. See Output and errors.

docs.title: Find a Recording and continue a listing
docs.text:
1. Generate a sealed Recording using the recording guide.

  2. Read a page:

    bifroest recording ls default --limit=20 --format=json

  3. Replace LAST_RECORDING_UUID with the last returned ID and continue:

    bifroest recording ls default --limit=20 --after=LAST_RECORDING_UUID --format=json

    Through management, prefix the same command with @bifroest-admin. Use a returned ID with recording show or recording play.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Remote metadata queries require access.recordings.read, but no download permission or decryption key.

docs.title: bifroest recording play
docs.text:
Verifies a Recording and replays its captured terminal output at the selected speed.

bifroest recording play --with-sensitive default RECORDING_UUID

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest recording play [flags] <auditlogName> <recording-uuid> bifroest recording play [flags] --expectedProducerId ID <file> bifroest @target recording play [flags] <auditlogName> <recording-uuid>

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: Configured auditlog name for repository selection. Used together with recording-uuid, locally or through @target.

docs.title: recording-uuid
docs.text: Recording UUID returned by recording ls for the selected auditlog.

docs.title: file
docs.text: One local .bcast, .becast or signed .cast file, as an alternative to repository selection. File inputs cannot be combined with @target.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local repository configuration; defaults to the platform path. Cannot be combined with a file input, @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --with-sensitive
docs.text:
bool = false

Required before reading any Recording content. Playback is complete and never redacted.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string

Independently trusted 64-hex producer ID for copied or downloaded evidence. The client can use X-ExpectedProducerId. Configured local selection uses its signing identity instead; direct SSH does not accept this flag.

docs.title: --decryptionIdentityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Matching local private key for .becast; repeatable. The client can use X-RecordingPrivateKey. Keys stay on the CLI machine. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --allowUntrusted
docs.text:
bool = false

Explicitly accept only cryptographic self-consistency for copied or downloaded content. Cannot be combined with an expected producer ID or configured local repository selection. See producer trust.

docs.title: --speed
docs.text:
float = 1

Playback-speed multiplier, greater than zero and at most 100. 2 plays twice as fast. Available in all supported execution modes.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Replayed terminal content on stdout. The input is verified before playback begins. It is not an asciicast file; recording export writes that representation. play does not accept --format, --output or --force.

Remote playback requires recordings.download. The integrated client verifies the downloaded original against the trusted producer and requested Recording ID before reading its content. Cancellation or an output failure stops playback with an error. See protected destinations.

docs.title: Replay a session recorded on the host
docs.text:
1. Enable Recording and generate a session as described in the recording guide.

  2. Find its ID:

    bifroest recording ls default

  3. Replay the selected Recording at twice the original speed:

    bifroest recording play --with-sensitive --speed=2 default RECORDING_UUID

docs.title: Replay encrypted evidence on a workstation
docs.text:
Follow the encrypted-evidence guide to configure the server's public recipient key, independent producer trust and local private key. Then run:

bifroest @bifroest-admin recording play --with-sensitive evidence RECORDING_UUID

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local invocation supports configured repositories and copied files. Direct SSH can play clear Recordings with --with-sensitive and the management flow's artifact-transfer permission. For encrypted content, the integrated client downloads and decrypts the original on the workstation.

docs.title: bifroest recording show
docs.text:
Shows verified metadata for one sealed Recording selected by auditlog name and UUID.

bifroest recording show default RECORDING_UUID

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest recording show [flags] <auditlogName> <id> bifroest @target recording show [flags] <auditlogName> <id>

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: Required configured auditlog name with Recording enabled.

docs.title: id
docs.text: Required Recording UUID, as returned by recording ls.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Details include Recording ID, auditlog, producer ID, format, status, timestamps, encryption state, verification scope, container size and chunk count. Encrypted Recordings expose signed outer metadata; status and other outer-seal claims do not replace full inner-Cast verification. This command does not accept a decryption identity; use recording verify for full verification.

A missing artifact, invalid signature or ID mismatch produces an error instead of metadata.

docs.title: Inspect a Recording found remotely
docs.text:
1. List a repository through the configured management alias:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin recording ls workload

  2. Replace RECORDING_UUID with a returned ID:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin recording show workload RECORDING_UUID --format=yaml

    This reads metadata without downloading the Recording to the workstation.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Remote metadata access requires access.recordings.read, but no download permission. For a copied file, use recording inspect.

docs.title: bifroest recording verify
docs.text:
Verifies a Recording against trusted producer identity without exporting or replaying its Cast.

bifroest recording verify default RECORDING_UUID

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest recording verify [flags] <auditlogName> <recording-uuid> bifroest recording verify [flags] --expectedProducerId ID <file> bifroest @target recording verify [flags] <auditlogName> <recording-uuid>

docs.title: auditlogName
docs.text: Configured auditlog name for repository selection. Used together with recording-uuid, locally or through @target.

docs.title: recording-uuid
docs.text: Recording UUID returned by recording ls for the selected auditlog.

docs.title: file
docs.text: One local .bcast, .becast or signed .cast file, as an alternative to repository selection. File inputs need an independent expected producer ID and no local server configuration. They cannot be combined with @target.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general executable flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local repository configuration; defaults to the platform path. Cannot be combined with a file input, @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --expectedProducerId
docs.text:
string

Independent 64-hex producer ID for copied or downloaded evidence. The client can use X-ExpectedProducerId. Configured local selection uses its signing identity and does not accept this flag. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --decryptionIdentityFile
docs.text:
File Path

Matching local SSH private key for full verification of encrypted .becast; repeatable. The client can use X-RecordingPrivateKey. Keys stay on the CLI machine. Without a supplied key, encrypted verification has outer scope; supplied non-matching keys fail. Unavailable over direct SSH.

docs.title: --require-full
docs.text:
bool = false

Reject outer-only verification. Clear Recordings need no decryption key. Direct SSH cannot meet this requirement for encrypted content using a private key held on the workstation.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The default status is verified (scope: outer) or verified (scope: full). Structured formats contain the verification result and scope. Success exits with status 0; no Cast content is emitted.

Verification checks the trusted producer and, for remote selection, the requested Recording ID. Regular stdout files cannot replace the input, supplied private keys or protected configured state. See Trust and verification.

docs.title: Verify a Recording on its host
docs.text:
1. Generate a Recording and find its UUID using the recording guide.

  2. Verify with the configured signing identity:

    bifroest recording verify default RECORDING_UUID --require-full

docs.title: Verify encrypted remote content locally
docs.text:
1. Configure the encrypted repository, trusted producer and recipient key as in the workstation guide.

  2. Require a full result:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin recording verify evidence RECORDING_UUID --require-full --format=json

    The matching private key is read on the workstation and never transmitted to the service.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local invocation supports configured repositories and copied files. Remote-client verification downloads the original and requires recordings.download, including outer-only verification. Direct-SSH verification requires recordings.verify.

Direct SSH accepts an auditlog name, Recording UUID, --require-full and --format. It verifies server-side evidence without artifact-transfer permission or access to a workstation's private decryption key.

docs.title: bifroest service
docs.text: Service commands install and control Bifröst through the Windows Service Control Manager or macOS launchd.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose install Install the platform service and optionally start it. remove Remove its registration; macOS always stops it first. start Start an installed service. stop Stop the service through the platform manager.

For direct foreground startup, see serve.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Follow host installation for platform configuration and privileges, then use the numbered installation examples.

docs.title: bifroest service install
docs.text:
Installs Bifröst as an automatically started Windows service or macOS LaunchDaemon. On macOS, Bifröst copies its current executable to /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.engity.bifroest and creates /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.engity.bifroest.plist directly from the CLI.

bifroest service install --start=false

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest service install [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --serviceName
docs.text:
string = "engity-bifroest"

Name of the service on Windows. This flag is not available on macOS, where the fixed LaunchDaemon label is com.engity.bifroest.

docs.title: --displayName
docs.text:
string = "Engity's Bifröst"

Display name in Windows service listings. Unavailable on macOS.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path<Configuration> = "<os specific>"

Configuration file used by the installed service. On macOS, the file must be below /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest, owned by root:wheel, have no ACL and use permissions no broader than 0640. The macOS default is /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/configuration.yaml.

The Windows default is C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\configuration.yaml.

docs.title: --start
docs.text:
bool = true

Starts the service immediately after installation. Use --start=false to install it without starting it. The default behavior is equivalent to subsequently calling bifroest service start.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Registers the platform service and, by default, starts it. Errors are logged to stderr and return a nonzero exit status. There is no structured --format output.

docs.title: Install on Windows before starting
docs.text:
1. Prepare the Windows host configuration.

  2. In an elevated PowerShell terminal, install without immediate startup:

    bifroest service install --configuration "C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\configuration.yaml" --start=false

  3. Start the installed service:

    bifroest service start

docs.title: Install a macOS LaunchDaemon
docs.text:
1. Prepare the protected configuration described in macOS host installation.

  2. Install and start the daemon:

    sudo ./bifroest service install

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Requires an elevated Administrator terminal on Windows and root privileges on macOS.

docs.title: bifroest service remove
docs.text: Removes an installed Bifröst service from the Windows Service Control Manager or macOS launchd. On macOS, configuration, state, keys, recordings and logs are preserved.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest service remove [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --serviceName
docs.text:
string = "engity-bifroest"

Name of the service on Windows. This flag is not available on macOS.

docs.title: --stop
docs.text:
bool = true

Stops the service before removing it on Windows. Use --stop=false to remove it without first stopping it. This flag is not available on macOS, where removing a LaunchDaemon always stops and unregisters it first.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Removes the service registration. On macOS, configuration, state, keys, Recordings and logs are preserved. Errors are logged to stderr and return a nonzero exit status.

docs.title: Remove an installed service
docs.text:
1. Select the host where the service was installed and open an elevated terminal.

  2. On Windows, run:

    bifroest service remove

    On macOS, run:

    sudo bifroest service remove

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Requires Administrator privileges on Windows and root privileges on macOS.

docs.title: bifroest service start
docs.text: Starts an installed Bifröst service.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest service start [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --serviceName
docs.text:
string = "engity-bifroest"

Name of the service on Windows. This flag is not available on macOS.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Requests service startup. A service-manager error is logged to stderr and returns a nonzero exit status.

docs.title: Start after an installation without immediate startup
docs.text:
1. Install with service install --start=false.

  2. Start locally in an elevated terminal:

    Windows
    bifroest service start
    macOS
    sudo bifroest service start

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

The service must already be installed. Requires Administrator privileges on Windows and root privileges on macOS.

docs.title: bifroest service stop
docs.text: Stops an installed Bifröst service if it is running.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest service stop [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --serviceName
docs.text:
string = "engity-bifroest"

Name of the service on Windows. This flag is not available on macOS.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Requests service shutdown through the platform service manager. A service-manager error is logged to stderr and returns a nonzero exit status.

docs.title: Stop the installed service
docs.text:
Run locally in an elevated terminal:

Windows
bifroest service stop
macOS
sudo bifroest service stop

Use service start to start it again, or service remove to remove its registration.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Requires Administrator privileges on Windows and root privileges on macOS.

docs.title: bifroest session
docs.text: Inspect session metadata: identity, requesting user, flow, lifecycle state and timestamps. A Bifröst session can be reused by multiple SSH connections; this listing is not a process or network-connection list.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose ls List sessions, with flow, user and state filters. show Show one session selected by UUID. disconnect Close a session's current SSH connections without revoking it. dispose Revoke and disconnect a session, then run its configured cleanup.

Local inspection reads configured filesystem session storage. Remote queries use the running service's session repository. See session configuration for storage and reuse behavior.

Session control is available through @target or direct management SSH and requires sessions.disconnect or sessions.dispose. These rights apply across flows but do not imply sessions.read. A command cannot target its own executing management session.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Manage a Bifröst host remotely sets up a local-account flow and a separate administration connection, then uses session ls to find the workload session.

docs.title: bifroest session disconnect
docs.text: Closes all SSH connections currently associated with the selected session, including their channels and forwarding connections. The session remains valid and its environment and authorization are not disposed. New connections may reuse it under the normal session rules.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest @target session disconnect [flags] <id>

docs.title: id
docs.text: Required session UUID from session ls, not an SSH connection or Recording ID. A missing session, an ID found in multiple flows, or the session executing this management command produces an error before any connections are closed.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general flags supported in the selected invocation mode. Local --configuration is not available.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor. A successful result contains id, flow and action: disconnect.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
bifroest @bifroest-admin session disconnect SESSION_UUID
ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'session disconnect SESSION_UUID --format=json'

Requires access.sessions.disconnect in the management flow. It permits disconnection across flows without granting sessions.read. The action is audited in the management flow and target flow according to their audit configuration. Disconnecting a session with no current connections succeeds without changing its lifecycle state.

To revoke a session and run its configured cleanup instead, use session dispose.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest session dispose
docs.text:
Revokes the selected session, closes all associated SSH connections and runs the normal environment and authorization disposal. The disposed session cannot be reused. Its stored metadata, audit logs and Recordings remain subject to their existing retention rules.

This revokes the session, not the user's login credentials. A new authorized login can create a new session.

Disposal can remove resources

Depending on the environment configuration, disposal can remove containers, Pods or managed accounts and their home directories. The command takes effect immediately, without a confirmation prompt. To close only current connections, use session disconnect.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest @target session dispose [flags] <id>

docs.title: id
docs.text: Required session UUID from session ls, not an SSH connection or Recording ID. A missing session, an ID found in multiple flows, or the session executing this management command produces an error before disposal starts.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes general flags supported in the selected invocation mode. Local --configuration is not available.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor. A successful result contains id, flow and action: dispose.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
bifroest @bifroest-admin session dispose SESSION_UUID
ssh management@bifroest.example.org 'session dispose SESSION_UUID --format=json'

Requires access.sessions.dispose in the management flow. It permits disposal across flows without granting sessions.read. The action is audited in the management flow and target flow according to their audit configuration.

Cleanup failure returns an error, not a success result. Connections are already closed and new connections to this session are rejected by the running service. Resource cleanup starts only after the disposed state has been persisted. Retry the command to finish incomplete cleanup; if persisting the session state itself failed, retry before restarting the service. Repeating disposal of a retained, already disposed session is safe.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text: Local CLI @target Direct SSH

docs.title: bifroest session ls
docs.text:
Lists authorized, non-expired sessions by default.

bifroest session ls

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest session ls [flags] bifroest @target session ls [flags]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: --flow
docs.text:
string

Select sessions whose flow name matches exactly.

docs.title: --user
docs.text:
string

Select sessions whose requesting user matches exactly.

docs.title: --state
docs.text:
string = "active"

active selects authorized sessions whose validity has not expired. new, authorized and disposed match that lifecycle state directly; authorized can therefore include expired sessions. all disables state filtering. Retained state depends on the repository's lifecycle and cleanup.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Rows contain session ID, flow, state, requesting user and creation time, ordered by creation time and then ID. Structured results additionally contain available remote, last-access and validity metadata. Repository inspection can report unreadable entries on stderr.

docs.title: Find a user's sessions in one flow
docs.text:
1. Configure and use the local flow from the management guide.

  2. From the administrator's workstation, query that flow:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin session ls --flow=local --user=alice --state=all --format=json

    Replace alice with the requesting SSH username. --flow=local excludes the separate administration session. 3. Use a returned ID with session show.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local inspection supports filesystem session storage; management queries the running repository and requires access.sessions.read.

docs.title: bifroest session show
docs.text:
Shows one session's metadata without applying the list command's default active-state filter.

bifroest session show SESSION_UUID

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: bifroest session show [flags] <id> bifroest @target session show [flags] <id>

docs.title: id
docs.text: id is the required session UUID returned by session ls. A session ID is distinct from an SSH connection ID or Recording ID.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Includes all general flags.

docs.title: --configuration
docs.text:
-cFile Path

Local configuration file; defaults to the platform path. Unavailable with @target or direct SSH.

docs.title: --format
docs.text:
string = "table"

Result format: table, json, yaml or cbor.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Session ID, flow, lifecycle state, requesting user, remote endpoint and creation time, plus last-access and validity timestamps where available. A missing session or an ID found in multiple flows produces an error.

docs.title: Inspect a session found in a listing
docs.text:
1. Find the session:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin session ls --flow=local --state=all

  2. Replace SESSION_UUID with a returned ID:

    bifroest @bifroest-admin session show SESSION_UUID --format=yaml

    A session may disappear between the two calls if it is removed by normal cleanup.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: Invocation modes
docs.text:
Local CLI @target Direct SSH

Local inspection supports filesystem session storage; management queries the running repository and requires access.sessions.read.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
Connections represent the way users connect to Bifröst. Use SSH with a standard SSH client, or HTTP for browser terminals and management access.

For browser setup and use, see Browser access.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
1. SSH
  2. HTTP

docs.title: SSH connection
docs.text: Defines the behavior of the SSH protocol for a user who is connecting to Bifröst.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = true

Enable direct TCP listeners. Set to false to use only SSH over HTTPS/WSS. SSH authentication and session settings below still apply to tunnels.

docs.title: addresses
docs.text:
[]Net Address = [":22"]

To which address the service will bind and listen to.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
Keys

See below.

docs.title: messages
docs.text:
Messages

See below.

docs.title: idleTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "10m"

For how long a connection can be idle before it will forcibly be closed. The client can send keep-alive packets to extend the idle time. 0 disables this timeout.

docs.title: maxTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = 0

The maximum duration a connection can be open before it will forcibly be closed, regardless of whether it is active. 0 disables this timeout.

docs.title: gracefulShutdownTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "30s"

How long Bifröst waits for active SSH connections and their handlers to finish after shutdown starts and the listeners have been closed. Remaining connections are forcibly closed when this single time budget expires. Shared resources remain open until their handlers have finished cleanup. 0 disables waiting and closes connections immediately.

docs.title: handshakeTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "2m"

The maximum duration from accepting a connection until successful SSH authentication. 0 disables this timeout.

docs.title: sessionRequestTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "30s"

How long an accepted session channel may wait for its initial shell, exec, or subsystem request. When the timeout expires, only the idle session channel is closed; the SSH connection and active sibling channels remain available. 0 disables this timeout.

docs.title: maxAuthTries
docs.text:
uint8 = 6

How many authentication attempts a client can make before the connection is rejected. 0 disables this limit.

docs.title: maxConnections
docs.text:
uint32 = 255

The maximum number of parallel connections on this service. Every additional connection is rejected.

docs.title: maxStartupsStart
docs.text:
uint16 = 10

The number of concurrent unauthenticated connections accepted before random early dropping starts. 0 starts the early-drop calculation with the first unauthenticated connection. This setting has no effect when maxStartupsFull is 0.

docs.title: maxStartupsRate
docs.text:
uint8 = 30

The initial probability, in percent, of dropping a new unauthenticated connection after maxStartupsStart is reached. It must be between 0 and 100; the probability increases toward 100 as maxStartupsFull is approached.

docs.title: maxStartupsFull
docs.text:
uint16 = 100

The hard limit for concurrent unauthenticated connections per SSH listener. When greater than 0, it must be greater than or equal to maxStartupsStart. 0 disables the complete pre-authentication connection limit.

docs.title: maxSessionsPerConnection
docs.text:
uint16 = 10

The maximum number of active SSH session channels per connection. 0 disables this limit.

docs.title: maxChannelsPerConnection
docs.text:
uint16 = 64

The maximum number of active SSH channels of all supported types per connection. 0 disables this limit.

docs.title: maxReverseForwardsPerConnection
docs.text:
uint16 = 16

The maximum number of active reverse-forward listeners per connection. 0 disables this limit.

docs.title: maxChannels
docs.text:
uint16 = 64

The maximum number of active SSH channels across all connections handled by one SSH listener. 0 disables this limit.

docs.title: maxReverseForwards
docs.text:
uint16 = 256

The maximum number of active reverse-forward listeners across all connections handled by one SSH listener. 0 disables this limit.

docs.title: unauthenticatedAudit
docs.text:
Unauthenticated audit

Controls how detailed audit records produced before a client has proven authentication are rate-limited. See below.

Listener-scoped limits are tracked independently for every entry in addresses. All HTTPS/WSS tunnels share one additional limit scope. For example, two configured listen addresses can each serve up to maxChannels active channels and maxReverseForwards reverse-forward listeners. maxConnections is different: Bifröst enforces it across the complete service, including tunnels.

With ssh -R [bind_address:]port:destination_host:destination_port, the reverse listener binds in the selected environment: on the Bifröst host for Local, in the container network namespace for Docker, in the Pod network namespace for Kubernetes, or on the target sshd for the SSH environment. The forwarded destination is reached from the SSH client, not from the listener environment. Omitting the destination (ssh -R [bind_address:]port) lets a supporting SSH client serve SOCKS5 on that reverse listener. For Local, Docker and Kubernetes, an empty bind host uses loopback in that environment; an explicit * requests a wildcard bind, whose network reachability depends on the authorized-key and environment policies and the network configuration. For the SSH environment, the target server's GatewayPorts setting governs the actual bind address. A permitted request does not guarantee a successful bind or network access to the listener.

Note

A client must acknowledge a new forwarded-tcpip channel within one second. Otherwise only the affected forwarded connection fails; the SSH connection and unrelated active channels remain available.

docs.title: proxyProtocol
docs.text:
bool = false

If enabled, Bifröst supports incoming connections using PROXY protocol versions 1 and 2. Only enable this when the SSH listener is exclusively reachable through trusted proxies. The current boolean configuration trusts the source addresses supplied by every peer that can reach the listener.

This setting does not apply to HTTPS/WSS tunnels; their peer address is the direct HTTPS connection's address.

OpenSSH Unix-socket forwarding (direct-streamlocal@openssh.com and streamlocal-forward@openssh.com) is not enabled. Bifröst currently has no cross-environment policy for socket paths, ownership, permissions, and cleanup.

docs.title: banner
docs.text:
string Connection = 

"{{ \`/etc/ssh/sshd-banner\` | file \`optional\` | default \`Transcend with Engity's Bifröst\n\n\` }}"

Banner which will be shown when the client connects to the server even before the first validation of authorizations or similar happens.

docs.title: preparationMessages
docs.text:
Preparation Messages

See below.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
addresses: [ ":22" ]
keys:
  hostKeys: [ /etc/engity/bifroest/key ]
  # ...
messages:
  # ...
idleTimeout: 10m
maxTimeout: 0
gracefulShutdownTimeout: 30s
handshakeTimeout: 2m
sessionRequestTimeout: 30s
maxAuthTries: 6
maxConnections: 255
maxStartupsStart: 10
maxStartupsRate: 30
maxStartupsFull: 100
maxSessionsPerConnection: 10
maxChannelsPerConnection: 64
maxReverseForwardsPerConnection: 16
maxChannels: 64
maxReverseForwards: 256
unauthenticatedAudit:
  interval: 1m
  perSourceLimit: 6
  globalLimit: 24
proxyProtocol: false
banner: "Yeah!"

docs.title: Unauthenticated audit
docs.text: Unauthenticated flow evaluations can be triggered repeatedly by remote clients. Bifröst therefore limits only their detailed audit records; exhaustion of either bucket never rejects authentication. Accepted password and keyboard-interactive results and verified public-key results bypass these limits. A public-key candidate has not yet proved possession of the private key and remains limited even if a flow accepts it.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Suppressed details are represented by signed authentication.flow.evaluations-suppressed aggregate events. Aggregates contain counts but no source address. See audit events for their exact semantics.

docs.title: interval
docs.text:
Duration = "1m"

The token refill and aggregate reporting interval. It must be greater than zero.

docs.title: perSourceLimit
docs.text:
uint16 = 6

Both the per-source token bucket capacity and the number of tokens refilled over one interval. It must be greater than zero. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses share their IPv4 bucket; IPv6 sources are grouped by /64.

docs.title: globalLimit
docs.text:
uint16 = 24

Both the service-wide token bucket capacity and the number of tokens refilled over one interval. It must be greater than or equal to perSourceLimit. This is the authoritative bound against distributed source addresses; the per-source bucket only preserves fairness.

The effective remote address from the SSH context is used. With proxyProtocol: true, this is the source supplied by the trusted proxy. The source cache is bounded; rotating IPv6 prefixes or sending many PROXY source addresses cannot bypass the global bucket or grow memory without bound.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text: Key-type restrictions also apply to browser SSH-key login, including saved public-key access and both the subject and CA keys of user certificates.

docs.title: hostKeys
docs.text:
[]File Path = ["<defaultLocation>"]

Where to store the host keys at. If they do not exist, they will be created as Ed25519 key.

Default Locations:

  • Linux: /etc/engity/bifroest/key
  • Darwin: /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/key
  • Windows: C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\key

docs.title: exchanges
docs.text:
Exchanges = 

["curve25519-sha256@libssh.org", "curve25519-sha256", "diffie-hellman-group16-sha512", "mlkem768x25519-sha256"]

Restrict which key exchanges are allowed to be used.

docs.title: rsaRestriction
docs.text:
RSA Restriction = "at-least-4096-bits"

Restrict which RSA keys are allowed to be used.

docs.title: dsaRestriction
docs.text:
DSA Restriction = "none"

Restrict which DSA keys are allowed to be used.

docs.title: ecdsaRestriction
docs.text:
ECDSA Restriction = "at-least-384-bits"

Restrict which ECDSA keys are allowed to be used.

docs.title: ed25519Restriction
docs.text:
ED25519 Restriction = "all"

Restrict which ED25519 keys are allowed to be used.

docs.title: rememberMeNotification
docs.text:
string Authorization = 

"If you return until {{.session.validUntil | format \`dateTimeT\`}} with the same public key ({{.key | fingerprint}}), you can seamlessly log in again.\n\n"

Shown when the authorization's RememberMe setting permits registration and a client key was remembered after successful login. Returning with that key can skip repeated password/MFA authentication while the session remains valid. Current access checks, including configured OIDC refresh checks, still apply.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
hostKeys: [ /etc/engity/bifroest/key ]
exchanges:
  - curve25519-sha256@libssh.org
  - curve25519-sha256
  - diffie-hellman-group16-sha512
  - mlkem768x25519-sha256
rsaRestriction: at-least-4096-bits
dsaRestriction: none
ecdsaRestriction: at-least-384-bits
ed25519Restriction: all
rememberMeNotification: "If you return until {{.session.validUntil | format `dateTimeT`}} with the same public key {{.key | fingerprint}}), you can seamlessly login again.\n\n"

docs.title: authentications
docs.text:
Authentications = 

["hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com", "hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com"]

Restrict which message authentications are allowed to be used.

docs.title: ciphers
docs.text:
Ciphers = 

["aes256-gcm@openssh.com", "aes256-ctr", "aes192-ctr"]

Restrict which ciphers are allowed to be used.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
authentications:
  - hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com
  - hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com
ciphers:
  - aes256-gcm@openssh.com
  - aes256-ctr
  - aes192-ctr

docs.title: Preparation Messages
docs.text:
In some cases the connection will not be available instantly. For example if the docker environment is used and an image needs to be downloaded first, this could take some seconds. In these cases different parts of Bifröst might trigger these messages being displayed. By default, all of them are displayed as described below.

As this is an array of preparation messages, the first which matches, wins.

docs.title: id
docs.text:
Regex = ".*"

Each preparation proces has a unique ID (like pull-image of the docker environment).

This property defines a regular expression this ID has to match together with flow.

docs.title: flow
docs.text:
Regex = ".*"

Each preparation process will be produces by a flow.

This property defines a regular expression the name of this flow has to match together with id.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
string Preparation Process = "{{.title}}..."

This message is shown when a preparation process starts.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
string Preparation Process = 

"\r{{.title}}... {{.percentage | printf \`%.0f%%\`}}"

This message is shown on each status change of a preparation process.

docs.title: end
docs.text:
string Preparation Process = "\r{{.title}}... DONE!\n"

This message is shown if the preparation process finishes successful.

docs.title: error
docs.text:
string Preparation Process = 

"\r{{.title}}... FAILED! Contact server operator for more information. Disconnecting now...\n"

This message is shown if the preparation process finishes with an error. The direct consequence will be that the connection will be closed by Bifröst immediately.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Show special message for pull-image process (all flows), but default for the rest
preparationMessages:
  - id: ^pull-image$
    # {{.image}} is NOT part of the common set of properties of
    # a Preparation Message it is specific to this message.
    # Please visit the details of each Preparation Message type
    # for details.
    start: "Going to download image {{.image}}..."
    update: "\rGoing to download image {{.image}}... {{.percentage | printf `%.0f%%`}}"
    end: "\rImage {{.image}} downloaded.\n"
    error: "\rFailed to download image {{.image}}.\n"
  - {} # Entry with all default values as mentioned above
Disable messages completely, for all preparation processes
preparationMessages:
  - start: ""
    update: ""
    end: ""
    error: ""

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: linux darwin windows / / /

docs.title: HTTP connection
docs.text:
Provides browser terminals, management and SSH tunnels over HTTP/TLS, plus a login page for OIDC Authorization Code.

This connection type is optional and disabled by default; see Browser access for a setup example.

Workload links use browser fragments, such as /#Shell or /#alice@Shell; see access links and hidden Slugs. Slugs are sent in API request bodies, never in API paths or query strings. Public discovery uses POST /api/v1/discovery with {"slug":"Shell"}. Only / serves the workspace document; workload and management targets remain in its fragment.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: These properties belong to the root http block. domains and tls are required when HTTP is enabled.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = false

Enables HTTPS. There is no unencrypted HTTP fallback.

docs.title: webUi
docs.text:
WebUI

Controls the browser workspace and its API independently of SSH tunnels and the login page.

docs.title: sshTunnel
docs.text:
SSH tunnel

Controls SSH over HTTPS and WSS, without requiring a WebUI login or a direct SSH listener.

docs.title: loginFlow
docs.text:
Login flow

Controls the OIDC login page and its required endpoints independently of the workspace.

docs.title: addresses
docs.text:
[]Net Address = [":443"]

Addresses to listen on; at least one is required when enabled.

docs.title: domains
docs.text:
[]Host

Accepted host names or IP addresses, without schemes, ports, paths or wildcards. Each needs a matching TLS certificate. Flow requirements can restrict this list further.

docs.title: tls
docs.text:
TLS

Existing certificates, ACME, or self-signed TLS for local testing; see TLS.

docs.title: startupTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "2m"

Maximum startup time, including certificate acquisition. Must be greater than zero.

docs.title: readHeaderTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "10s"

Timeout for reading request headers and initial request bodies. Must be greater than zero.

docs.title: idleTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "1m"

Idle HTTP keep-alive timeout, not the session lifetime or terminal keepalive interval. Must be greater than zero.

docs.title: gracefulShutdownTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "30s"

How long to wait for HTTP requests during shutdown. 0s closes them immediately. SSH tunnels use the SSH shutdown grace.

docs.title: maxHeaderBytes
docs.text:
uint32 = 1048576

Maximum request-header size in bytes, from 1 to 16777216 (16 MiB).

docs.title: rememberMe
docs.text:
RememberMe

Controls how long an explicitly remembered browser can remain unused.

docs.title: assetsDirectory
docs.text:
File Path = ""

Override bundled browser files with local files. Missing files use the bundled version. Keep this directory separate from private service storage; changes to its root require a restart.

docs.title: customCss
docs.text:
[]File Path

CSS files loaded after the built-in styles, in the listed order.

Example
customCss: [custom/brand.css]

docs.title: customJs
docs.text:
[]File Path

JavaScript files loaded after the built-in scripts, in the listed order. Only load trusted code: it has the same access as the application.

For example, set the workspace title before the application mounts:

custom/brand.js
addEventListener('bifroest:configure', ({ detail }) => {
  detail.title = 'Operations';
});

docs.title: customHtmlHead
docs.text:
string = ""

Trusted HTML appended to the document head, not a file path.

Example
customHtmlHead: '<meta name="application-name" content="Operations">'

docs.title: customHtmlBody
docs.text:
string = ""

Trusted HTML appended to the document body, not a file path.

docs.title: WebUI
docs.text: These properties belong to http.webUi.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = true

Enable the browser workspace and its API. Disabling it does not disable SSH tunnels or the OIDC login page.

docs.title: SSH tunnel
docs.text:
See SSH over HTTPS with OpenSSH and curl for client setup and connection examples.

These properties belong to http.sshTunnel.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = true

Enable the SSH tunnel for native clients. Existing SSH authentication, host-key verification, SSH flow requirements, limits, auditing, SFTP and forwarding policies apply. Browser-only flows do not grant SSH access.

Transport admission additionally allows at most 1024 simultaneous tunnels, with at most 64 per direct peer IP. Lower SSH limits still apply; forwarded headers do not replace the peer address.

docs.title: Login flow
docs.text: These properties belong to http.loginFlow.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = true

Enable the login page, its resources and required OIDC endpoints, including when http.webUi.enabled is false. OIDC Authorization Code requires this component; configurations that disable it are rejected.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text: TLS terminates directly at Bifröst; an HTTP reverse proxy must not terminate it instead. Existing certificates take priority over ACME.

docs.title: Load balancers and instance routing
docs.text:
Browser access, pending logins and management confirmations belong to the instance that created them. A TCP/TLS load balancer must keep related HTTP requests and channels on that instance.

For SSH Authorization Code logins, coordinate persistence across SSH and HTTPS so browser approval and the IdP callback reach the instance holding the SSH login. Browser-cookie affinity alone cannot establish that relationship; use instance-specific login endpoints when these paths cannot be pinned together.

After a backend failure, the load balancer can route a new connection to a healthy instance, where the user signs in again. Bifröst sessions are not shared between instances. See HA deployment and recovery.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: These properties belong to http.tls.

docs.title: dummy
docs.text:
bool = false

Generate a temporary self-signed certificate for local testing. Cannot be combined with existing certificates or ACME.

Warning

Use trusted certificates or ACME for production, not dummy TLS.

docs.title: certificates
docs.text:
[]Certificate

PEM certificate/key pairs covering the configured domains.

docs.title: acme
docs.text:
ACME

Optional automatic certificate issuance and renewal. Disabled by default.

docs.title: Certificate
docs.text: Each entry in http.tls.certificates has these properties.

docs.title: certificateFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local PEM certificate-chain file.

docs.title: privateKeyFile
docs.text:
File Path

Local PEM private-key file, separate from SSH and audit keys. Do not put the key itself in the configuration.

docs.title: ACME
docs.text: The configured DNS names must resolve to Bifröst, with public TCP port 443 reaching it directly. IP addresses and wildcard certificates are not supported by ACME.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: These properties belong to http.tls.acme.

docs.title: enabled
docs.text:
bool = false

Obtain and renew certificates for domains not covered by existing certificates.

docs.title: acceptTerms
docs.text:
bool = false

true means you accept the terms of the ACME directory, you defined via directoryUrl. In case of Let's Encrypt you can find them at https://letsencrypt.org/repository/. This is mandatory, when ACME is enabled.

docs.title: email
docs.text:
string = ""

Optional contact email address, without a display name.

docs.title: directoryUrl
docs.text:
URL = 

"https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory"

Certificate authority's HTTPS directory. A staging service can be used for testing; its certificates are not browser-trusted.

docs.title: storage
docs.text:
File Path = "<os specific>"

Persistent private directory for ACME account and certificate keys. Preserve it across restarts and keep it separate from public assets and other service storage.

docs.title: Default settings
docs.text: linux darwin windows /var/lib/engity/bifroest/http/acme /Library/Application Support/Engity/Bifroest/http/acme C:\ProgramData\Engity\Bifroest\http\acme

docs.title: RememberMe
docs.text: The authorization's RememberMe setting controls saved access. One non-exportable signing key is shared within this browser profile and origin; permissions remain separate. Resumption requires current authorization and a valid session. Use Log out to revoke saved access.

docs.title: idleTimeout
docs.text:
Duration = "6h"

Maximum inactivity of saved browser access; a successful resume resets it. Must be greater than zero. Shorter session limits still apply.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Enable HTTPS with ACME for your existing flows:

http:
  enabled: true
  domains: [bifroest.example.org]
  tls:
    acme:
      enabled: true
      acceptTerms: true
      email: operator@example.org

To expose only SSH over HTTPS/WSS, keep the HTTPS configuration above and set ssh.enabled, http.webUi.enabled and http.loginFlow.enabled to false. Leave http.sshTunnel.enabled at its default of true.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
linux darwin windows / / /

Browser access requires JavaScript, WebAssembly and WebCrypto; saved access also requires IndexedDB. Private-key import supports PEM/OpenSSH keys up to 64 KiB, not PPK, encrypted PKCS#8 or hardware keys. Native SSH tunnels do not require a browser.

SSH-key browser login also enforces the configured SSH key restrictions, including the subject and CA keys of user certificates.

Browser artifact downloads are limited to 64 MiB per artifact; use the CLI for larger files. Browser terminals provide shells; use SSH for SFTP and port forwarding.

docs.title: curl transport capabilities
docs.text:
Use a current, security-maintained curl build with HTTPS support; WebSocket streaming also requires WSS support. Hover over or activate each asterisk for the expected version's test coverage.

Transport Minimum version HTTPS streaming (HTTP/1.1) 8.15.0 Expected minimum version 8.15.0, not a verified lower bound. Tested with curl 8.18.0 on Linux (OpenSSL) and curl 8.22.0 on Windows (Schannel, via WSL interop). macOS has not been tested natively. WebSocket streaming (WSS) 8.16.0 Expected minimum version 8.16.0, not a verified lower bound. Tested with curl 8.18.0 on Linux (OpenSSL), including real SSH and simultaneous binary transfers. curl 8.22.0 on Windows (Schannel) failed concurrent duplex and is unsuitable for SSH over WSS. macOS has not been tested natively.

docs.title: Context objects
docs.text: Context objects depend on where they are used and are mainly injected into template evaluation. For local account-management templates, see Context Local Environment.

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
1. Alternative Binary

  2. Authentication

  3. Authorization

  4. Authorization Request

  5. Connection

  6. Environment

  7. Container

  8. Core

  9. Local Environment

  10. Local Group

  11. Local User

  12. OIDC Token

  13. OIDC ID Token

  14. OIDC User Info

  15. Preparation Process

  16. Remote

  17. Simple Entry

docs.title: Context Alternative Binary
docs.text: In cases when Bifröst needs to obtain an alternative variant of its binaries, this context provides the required information.

docs.title: os
docs.text:
string

Holds the name of the operating system, such as linux or windows.

docs.title: arch
docs.text:
string

Holds the name of the architecture, such as amd64 or arm64.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
string

Holds the actual version, such as v1.0.0-beta3.

docs.title: ext
docs.text:
string

Holds the extension for the target binary, such as <empty> or .exe.

docs.title: packageExt
docs.text:
string

Holds the extension for the package, such as .tgz or .zip.

docs.title: Context Authentication
docs.text:
.authentication provides a common identity view for authorizations. The original requesting name remains in .remote.user; authorization-specific fields remain in .authorization.

Missing identity information causes an error, not a fallback to the requesting name. During environment acceptance this context describes a candidate; accessing it does not itself prove successful authentication.

docs.title: principal
docs.text:
string

The actor's name or identifier, with these defaults:

Authorization Default principal Local Resolved account name Simple Matched entry name Htpasswd Authenticated name OIDC Verified subject (sub) Bifröst Attested original identity None anonymous (not authenticated)

docs.title: issuer
docs.text:
string

The authority that scopes subject: the verified OIDC issuer, the local authorization namespace, or the originating CA and authorization kind for Bifröst delegation.

docs.title: subject
docs.text:
string

The identity within that authority: UID/SID for Local, the matched entry for Simple, the authenticated name for Htpasswd, and verified sub for OIDC. Bifröst delegation uses the attested original name, not an original OIDC subject.

docs.title: isAuthenticated
docs.text:
bool

Whether an authenticated subject is available. none has empty issuer/subject and isAuthenticated: false; it cannot establish a shared authenticated identity.

docs.title: Principal mapping
docs.text:
The optional authorization.principal template changes the principal, not the issuer, subject or credentials being checked. It can use .authorization.*; .authentication.principal within that template refers to the default above. none does not accept this setting.

The result must be nonempty UTF-8, at most 1,024 bytes, without control characters. Invalid or unavailable values reject the operation. A principal is not automatically an allowed target account: configure the environment's account selection separately.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Use the verified local account name as the principal and select that same account by name and UID/SID:

flows:
  - name: local
    authorization:
      type: local
      principal: '{{ .authorization.user.name }}'
    environment:
      type: local
      name: '{{ .authentication.principal }}'
      uid: '{{ .authorization.user.uid }}'

docs.title: Context Authorization Request
docs.text:
Represents a request for authorization of a remote user/connection.

There are more specialized variants of the authorization request available, based on their actual usage:

  • Public Key
  • Password
  • Interactive

docs.title: connection
docs.text:
Connection

The incoming connection.

docs.title: remote
docs.text:
Remote

The requesting peer and original username.

docs.title: authentication
docs.text:
Authentication

The current authentication candidate; anonymous before a candidate is resolved.

docs.title: Public Key
docs.text: Is used at the attempt to use the authentication method publickey where the user's client presents one of the user's SSH Public Keys.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: All inherited of Context Authorization Request plus:

docs.title: publicKey
docs.text:
SSH Public Key

The provided SSH Public Key of the requesting remote user.

docs.title: Password
docs.text: Is used at the attempt to use the authentication method password where the user's client presents the password the user either handed over directly to the SSH client software via command line, stdin or when the client asks for it.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: All inherited of Context Authorization Request plus:

docs.title: password
docs.text:
string

The provided password.

docs.title: Interactive
docs.text: Is used at the attempt to use the authentication method keyboard-interactive where the user's client give the control to the server to interactively request more information from the user. Usually, this is another way to request either the password or multi-factor-information.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: All inherited of Context Authorization Request, but no other.

docs.title: Context Authorization
docs.text:
Represents a fully authorized connection of a user.

There are more specialized variants of the authorization available, based on which authorization type was used:

Variant Authorization Bifröst Bifröst delegation Htpasswd Htpasswd Local Local OpenID Connect (OIDC) OpenID Connect (OIDC) Simple Simple None None

docs.title: Bifröst
docs.text: Is the result of a successful certificate-based delegation from another Bifröst authorization. The common authorization remote remains the immediately connected SSH peer; use origin for the unchanged original identity.

docs.title: origin
docs.text:
object

The original user, host and authorizationKind from the first Bifröst instance.

docs.title: peer
docs.text:
object

The final, immediately verified hop. It contains the CA and subject-key fingerprints, serial, key ID, upstream session ID and flow, authorization kind, audience, target user, validity boundaries, and effective capability booleans.

docs.title: hops
docs.text:
list of objects

The complete normalized delegation path. Each object has the same fields as peer. The list has at most eight entries.

docs.title: policy
docs.text:
object

The effective ptyAllowed, portForwardingAllowed and agentForwardingAllowed values after all hops.

Passwords, tokens, unrestricted identity-provider claims and arbitrary environment maps are never included in this context.

docs.title: Htpasswd
docs.text: Is the result of a successful authorization via Htpasswd authorization.

docs.title: user
docs.text:
string

Holds the user(name) of the successfully authorized user.

docs.title: Local
docs.text: Is the result of a successful authorization via Local authorization.

docs.title: user
docs.text:
Local User

Holds the successfully authorized user.

docs.title: OpenID Connect (OIDC)
docs.text: Is the result of a successful authorization via OpenID Connect (OIDC) authorization.

docs.title: token
docs.text:
OIDC Token

Holds the token information (like access token, expiry, ...) of the authorized user.

docs.title: idToken
docs.text:
OIDC ID Token

Can hold the ID Token of the authorized user, if configured and available.

docs.title: userInfo
docs.text:
OIDC UserInfo

Can hold the UserInfo of the authorized user, if configured and available.

docs.title: Simple
docs.text: Is the result of a successful authorization via Simple authorization.

docs.title: entry
docs.text:
Simple Entry

Holds a representation of the authorized record of Simple authorization entries.

docs.title: None
docs.text: Is the result of a successful authorization via None authorization.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Context Connection
docs.text: Information about the incoming connection, available as .connection.

docs.title: id
docs.text:
string

The connection UUID, distinct from the session ID.

docs.title: transport
docs.text:
string

Incoming transport: ssh or http.

docs.title: remote
docs.text:
Remote

The requesting username and direct peer IP address.

docs.title: http
docs.text:
object

Present for HTTP and null for SSH:

Property Meaning .connection.http.host Incoming HTTP hostname, without its port. .connection.http.slug Selected slug, case-sensitive; empty for the root.

docs.title: Context Container
docs.text: Represents a Docker/OCI container.

docs.title: id
docs.text:
string

The given ID of the container.

docs.title: image
docs.text:
string

The actual image of the container.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

The given name of the container.

docs.title: flow
docs.text:
Flow Name

The flow this container is connected to. It can be absent if this container isn't and never was connected to any flow.

docs.title: Context Core
docs.text: Represents the core of Bifröst.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
This context does not provide any kind of properties; but all functions can be used.

It has no current connection. Connection-bound request and environment contexts separately expose .connection; startup and background contexts must not fabricate SSH/HTTP metadata to imitate them.

docs.title: Context Environment
docs.text: Used while accepting, preparing or executing an environment.

docs.title: connection
docs.text:
Connection

The incoming connection.

docs.title: remote
docs.text:
Remote

The requesting peer and original username.

docs.title: authentication
docs.text:
Authentication

The current authentication candidate.

docs.title: authorization
docs.text:
Authorization

The authorization candidate or result.

docs.title: session
docs.text:
Session

The associated session, when available.

docs.title: Context Local Environment
docs.text: Used by the local environment when evaluating account-management templates.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Includes the Environment context, plus:

docs.title: user
docs.text:
Local User

The Local User candidate, or null if none is available.

docs.title: Context Local Group
docs.text: Represents a local group on Linux or a local alias on Windows. Linux groups may be resolved by Local authorization; Windows local aliases are available through the Local Environment context.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

The group name on Linux, or the local alias name on Windows.

docs.title: gid
docs.text:
GID

The group's GID: a numeric group ID on Linux, or a textual local alias SID on Windows.

docs.title: Context Local User
docs.text: Represents a local account on Linux, macOS or Windows. Local authorization supports existing local accounts on all three platforms, including local SAM accounts on Windows. A local account candidate is also available in the Local Environment context.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

(User)name of the user.

docs.title: displayName
docs.text:
string

The display name of the user: GECOS on Linux, the Directory Services real name on macOS, or the local SAM full name on Windows.

docs.title: uid
docs.text:
UID

The local account's UID.

docs.title: gid
docs.text:
GID

Unix only. Shortcut for group.gid.

docs.title: group
docs.text:
Local Group

Unix only. The primary group of the user.

docs.title: groups
docs.text:
[]Local Group

The user's supplementary groups on Linux and macOS. On Windows, these are direct local alias memberships; there is no primary group.

docs.title: gids
docs.text:
[]GID

Shortcut for groups.*.gid: numeric IDs on Unix, local group SIDs on Windows.

docs.title: managed
docs.text:
bool or null

true or false when the current flow has a Local Environment, including .authorization.user in that flow. Otherwise null.

docs.title: shell
docs.text:
string

Unix: the account's configured shell. Windows: COMSPEC, falling back to cmd.exe.

docs.title: homeDir
docs.text:
string

Unix: the account home directory. Windows: its actual profile directory; reading this field loads the profile if it does not yet exist and requires Bifröst to run as LocalSystem.

docs.title: Context OpenID Connect (OIDC) ID Token
docs.text: Holds the ID information about a user who was authorized via OIDC, if configured and available.

docs.title: issuer
docs.text:
string

Holds the iss property of the ID Token.

docs.title: audience
docs.text:
string

Holds the aud property of the ID Token.

docs.title: subject
docs.text:
string

Holds the sub property of the ID Token.

docs.title: expiry
docs.text:
datetime

Date when this token will expire. You will never get a token where this value is in the past.

docs.title: issuedAt
docs.text:
datetime

Holds the iat property of the ID Token.

docs.title: nonce
docs.text:
string

Can hold the nonce property of the ID Token.

docs.title: accessTokenHash
docs.text:
string

Can hold the at_hash property of the ID Token.

docs.title: *
docs.text:
any

Any other possible value which was added to the ID Token can be referenced. Like: idToken.groups or idToken.tid. This depends on the Identity Provider itself, see IdP specific documentation.

docs.title: Context OpenID Connect (OIDC) Token
docs.text: Holds the main information about a user who was authorized via OIDC.

docs.title: accessToken
docs.text:
string

Contains the access_token as defined via RFC.

docs.title: tokenType
docs.text:
string

Contains the token_type as defined via RFC.

docs.title: refreshToken
docs.text:
string

Can contain the refresh_token as defined via RFC.

docs.title: expiry
docs.text:
datetime

Can contain the expires_in as defined via RFC.

docs.title: Context OpenID Connect (OIDC) UserInfo
docs.text: Holds the full user information about a user who was authorized via OIDC, if configured and if available.

docs.title: subject
docs.text:
string

Subject - Identifier for the End-User at the Issuer (see spec for more details).

docs.title: profile
docs.text:
string

RL of the End-User's profile page. The contents of this web page SHOULD be about the End-User (see spec for more details).

docs.title: email
docs.text:
email

End-User's preferred e-mail address (see spec for more details).

docs.title: emailVerified
docs.text:
bool

True if the End-User's e-mail address has been verified, false otherwise. When this Claim Value is true, this means that the OP took affirmative steps to ensure that this e-mail address was controlled by the End-User at the time the verification was performed. The means by which an e-mail address is verified is context specific and dependent upon the trust framework or contractual agreements on which the parties are operating (see spec for more details).

docs.title: Context Preparation Process
docs.text: Holds the information about a Preparation Process of Bifröst.

docs.title: connection
docs.text:
Connection

The current incoming connection inherited from the environment request. Its transport remains http for browser execution; it is not the transport of a downstream SSH, Docker or Kubernetes target.

docs.title: id
docs.text:
string

Each preparation process has its own unique ID (like pull-image of the docker environment).

Please refer the documentation of the supported environments for their preparation process kinds.

docs.title: flow
docs.text:
string

Holds the name of flow which context holds this preparation process.

docs.title: progress
docs.text:
float32

In case of update events, this holds the current progress of the whole process in 0.0 to 1.0.

docs.title: percentage
docs.text:
float32

Same as progress but multiplied with 100.0 to be able to be used directly as percentage value. Therefore, the value can be 0.0 to 100.0.

docs.title: error
docs.text:
any

In case of error events, this holds the full error information.

Danger

Should usually not be displayed to end-users because it can contain sensitive system information which should only be exposed inside of log files.

This property should only be used for evaluation what should be displayed instead of displaying itself.

docs.title: *
docs.text:
any

Each preparation process can provide other information, like image in case of a docker pull-image process.

Please refer the documentation of the supported environments for their process kinds.

docs.title: Context Remote
docs.text: Represents a user who is connected to Bifröst.

docs.title: host
docs.text:
Host

Direct numeric peer IP address, without a port, of the incoming connection. For HTTP, this does not come from Forwarded or X-Forwarded-* headers and is not the HTTP host selection; that is .connection.http.host.

docs.title: user
docs.text:
string

Original username supplied by the requesting client, for example foo@bar in ssh -l 'foo@bar' bifroest.example.org. It remains unchanged by authorization's remoteName mapping and is not proof of an authenticated principal.

docs.title: Context Simple Entry
docs.text: Represents a record of the Simple authorization entries.

docs.title: name
docs.text:
string

Holds the user(name) of the successfully authorized user.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: Bifröst executes user sessions within environments. These environments can either be the local environment of the host (on which Bifröst runs on) itself or even containers.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
1. docker: Docker executes each user session inside a separate Docker container.
  2. kubernetes: Kubernetes executes each user session inside a separate POD in a defined cluster.
  3. local: Local executes on the host itself (same host on which Bifröst is running).
  4. ssh: SSH connects to another SSH server and forwards sessions and direct TCP channels.
  5. dummy: Dummy for demonstration purposes, it simply prints a message and exists immediately.
  6. management: Management provides authorized structured administrative commands via SSH and HTTP without a shell.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Using local environment: 
    type: local
name: "{{.authorization.user.name}}"
  2. Using simple kubernetes environment: 
    type: kubernetes
  3. Using simple docker environment: 
    type: docker
  4. Using kubernetes environment with Ubuntu image, custom kubeconfig file and additional settings: 
    type: kubernetes
config: "/etc/kube/my-kube-config"
context: "my-kube-context"
image: ubuntu
## Using /bin/bash instead of /bin/sh,
## because it does exist in the image
shellCommand: [/bin/bash]
execCommand: [/bin/bash, -c]

## Only allow login if the OIDC's groups has "my-great-group-uuid"
## ...and the tid (tenant ID) is "my-great-tenant-uuid"
loginAllowed: |
    {{ and
      (.authorization.idToken.groups | has "my-great-group-uuid")
      (.authorization.idToken.tid    | eq  "my-great-tenant-uuid")
    }}
  5. Using docker environment with Ubuntu image and additional settings: 
    type: docker
image: ubuntu
## Using /bin/bash instead of /bin/sh,
## because it does exist in the image
shellCommand: [/bin/bash]
execCommand: [/bin/bash, -c]
  6. Using an SSH environment: 
    type: ssh
address: target.example.org
user: service-user
knownHostsFile: /etc/engity/bifroest/known_hosts
identityFiles:
  - /etc/engity/bifroest/id_target
  7. Using dummy environment with a simple message: 
    type: dummy
banner: "Hello, {{.authorization.idToken.name}}!\n"

docs.title: Docker environment
docs.text:
When using Docker environments, each user session runs in a separate Docker container. This is in contrast to the local environment, where each user session runs on the same host as Bifröst.

This is useful if you explicitly do not want to give users access to the host itself, but to environments where they can work with defined toolsets. This is especially true, if you want to create demo or training environments.

In another use case you can set up a Bastion/Jump host, what allows the user to jump from one server to another network. Using different networks can be beneficial, too.

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Environment Type = "docker"

Has to be set to docker to enable the docker environment.

docs.title: variables
docs.text:
Environment Variables Authorization

Defines environment variables for commands and shells in the container. They override image values and values received from the SSH client, authorized_keys and authorization. Bifröst-generated runtime variables take precedence.

docs.title: loginAllowed
docs.text:
bool Authorization = true

Has to be true (after being evaluated) that the user is allowed to use this environment.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Require that the existing local user has the group ssh: 
    loginAllowed: |
   {{ or
       (.authorization.user.group.name | eq "ssh" )
       (.authorization.user.groups     | firstMatching `{{.name | eq "ssh"}}`)
   }}

docs.title: host
docs.text:
string Authorization = "{{ env `DOCKER_HOST` }}"

URL how to connect to the API endpoint of the docker compatible daemon.

Accepted protocols are:

  1. http
  2. https
  3. tcp
  4. unix (only supported on unix based systems)
  5. npipe (only supported on Windows)

If this variable is empty (which can be also the case if {{ env `DOCKER_HOST` }} evaluates to empty, because the environment variable is not set), the system specific connection will be chosen:

  • Unix (such as Linux): unix:///var/run/docker.sock
  • Windows: npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine

docs.title: apiVersion
docs.text:
string Authorization = 

"{{ env \`DOCKER_API_VERSION\` }}"

Defines which version of Docker API should be chosen for communication. In doubt leave this blank.

docs.title: certPath
docs.text:
File path Authorization = 

"{{ env \`DOCKER_CERT_PATH\` }}"

Is a directory which should contain the following files:

  • key.pem: Private key Bifröst should connect to the Docker API with.
  • cert.pem Certificate Bifröst should present when connect to the Docker API.
  • ca.pem: Certificate authorities to check the certificate of the Docker API Host against.

If this variable is empty (which can be also the case if {{ env `DOCKER_CERT_PATH` }} evaluates to empty) and tlsVerify is set to false, all Docker API Hosts are accepted.

docs.title: tlsVerify
docs.text:
bool Authorization = 

"{{ env \`DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY\` | ne \`\` }}"

If this variable is false (which can be also the case if {{ env `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY` }} evaluates to empty), all Docker API Hosts are accepted.

Danger

Setting this to false is only recommend, if connecting to the local socket connection (on the same machine - see host's default behavior).

docs.title: image
docs.text:
string Authorization = "alpine"

Which OCI/Docker image should be used for this environment.

Everything available within this image will be also available to the user who is connecting to the container using this image. Therefore, you should consider to creating your custom images if you need additional features like kubectl, skopeo, ... and use this one here.

This image needs to contain a valid shell executable.

ENTRYPOINT and CMD settings of the image will be ignored.

On Linux, image ENV values are not inherited by SSH commands. Bifröst deliberately clears them before starting its privileged IMP and exec wrapper, then supplies only the environment assembled for the individual authorization and SSH execution. This prevents image-controlled loader variables such as LD_PRELOAD from affecting the privileged wrapper. Windows containers retain their image environment for IMP and wrapper startup; the SSH target command still receives only its explicitly assembled execution environment.

docs.title: imagePullPolicy
docs.text:
Pull Policy Authorization = "ifAbsent"

Defines what should happen if the container starts with the required image of the container.

If the image needs to be pulled, it will trigger the image-pull preparation process.

docs.title: imagePullCredentials
docs.text:
Docker Pull Credentials Authorization

Defines credentials which should be used to pull the defined image.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
1. Using direct json: 
    imagePullCredentials: |
 {"username":"foo","password":"bar"}
  2. Using base64 URL encoded json: 
    imagePullCredentials: |
 eyJ1c2VybmFtZSI6ImZvbyIsInBhc3N3b3JkIjoiYmFyIn0
  3. Using content from file: 
    imagePullCredentials: "{{ file `/etc/engity/bifroest/secrets/my-great-secret` }}"
  4. Using content from environment variable: 
    imagePullCredentials: "{{ env `MY_GREAT_SECRET` }}"

docs.title: networks
docs.text:
[]string Authorization = ["default"]

Defines the container networks this container should be connected to.

Empty always defaults to ["default"].

Note
